scope: Official player-class archetype index exposed by AoN, including alternate, unchained and occult classes.

archetypes.name: Aerochemist
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen, Swift Poisoning; Persistent Mutagen; Poison Use; Swift Alchemy; Poison Resistance
archetypes.aonSummary: Aerochemists use scraps of Shory’s magic in their concoctions to gain personal powers of flight.

archetypes.name: Alchemical Sapper
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bomb; Mutagen; Poison Resistance; Swift Alchemy; 6th-level Discovery; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Alchemical sappers are trained to create explosives.

archetypes.name: Alchemical Trapper
archetypes.replaces: 2nd and 4th-level Discoveries
archetypes.aonSummary: (Kobold Only) Because kobolds rely on traps to soften up enemies, kobold alchemists learn to turn bombs into traps.

archetypes.name: Aquachymist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bombs; 2nd-level Discovery
archetypes.aonSummary: Aquachymists are those rare few alchemists of land-dwelling and aquatic races alike who strive to unlock new and fantastic secrets of alchemy that can be discovered only in the water’s depths.

archetypes.name: Beastmorph
archetypes.replaces: Swift Alchemy; Swift Poisoning; Poison Immunity; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: Beastmorphs study the anatomy of monsters, learning how they achieve their strange powers.

archetypes.name: Blazing Torchbearer
archetypes.replaces: Brew Potion; Poison Use; 4th-level Discovery
archetypes.aonSummary: The blazing torchbearer is especially adept at manipulating flames of all kinds.

archetypes.name: Blightseeker
archetypes.replaces: Bombs; 6th, 12th, 18th-level Discovery; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: Blightseekers are alchemists devoted to the study of fungi native to the Darklands.

archetypes.name: Blood Alchemist
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Mutagen; Bombs
archetypes.aonSummary: Most alchemists can transform matter and energy into other forms, but some wicked specialists realize that life itself is an energy that can greatly fuel their alchemy.

archetypes.name: Bogborn Alchemist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Throw Anything
archetypes.aonSummary: (Grippli Only) Some grippli alchemists are particularly attuned to the swamps and the dangerous creatures that inhabit them; these serve as their laboratories and research subjects, respectively.

archetypes.name: Bramble Brewer
archetypes.replaces: 2nd-level Discovery; Mutagen; Greater Mutagen; Grand Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: (Half-Elf Only) Some half-elven alchemists merge human curiosity with their elven link to nature.

archetypes.name: Chirurgeon
archetypes.replaces: Poison Use; Poison Resistance +4; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: An alchemist who studies anatomy and uses this knowledge to heal is a chirurgeon.

archetypes.name: Clone Master
archetypes.replaces: Bomb; Poison Resistance +6; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Clone masters practice duplicating existing creatures in order to better understand how to create new life.

archetypes.name: Concocter
archetypes.replaces: 2nd, 4th, 6th-level Discovery; Swift Poisoning
archetypes.aonSummary: Concocters are experts at combining sets of chemicals to create unique effects.

archetypes.name: Construct Rider
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Brew Potion; Mutagen; 4th-level Discovery; Extracts
archetypes.aonSummary: A construct rider creates arcane devices to emulate and surpass weak flesh.

archetypes.name: Crimson Chymist
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: Crimson chymists turn to the alchemical arts, infusing their bodies with the mutagenic essence of the Mantis God.

archetypes.name: Cruorchymist
archetypes.replaces: Poison Use; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity; Swift Poisoning; Mutagen; Brew Potion
archetypes.aonSummary: Cruorchymists see their blood as just another tool for their experiments

archetypes.name: Crypt Breaker
archetypes.replaces: Alchemist Bomb, Mutagen, Brew Potion, Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: Crypt breakers use their powers of perception and alchemical adaptation to safely investigate the mysteries of the past.

archetypes.name: Deep Bomber
archetypes.replaces: Poison Use; Swift Alchemy; Instant Alchemy; Swift Poisoning
archetypes.aonSummary: (Svirfneblin Only) Consumed with keeping hidden from the horrors below the surface, svirfneblin use their racial proclivity for alchemy and their inherent talent for obfuscation to strike their enemies from the darkness and retreat unseen.

archetypes.name: Dimensional Excavator
archetypes.replaces: 4th-level Discovery
archetypes.aonSummary: Dimensional excavators have discovered and recorded ways to cause their bombs to create minor tears in the fabric of reality, forming extradimensional pits to vex their foes.

archetypes.name: Dragonblood Chymist
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen; 2nd, 12th, 16th-level discovery; Throw Anything; Poison Resistance; Poison Use; Swift Poisoning
archetypes.aonSummary:
The dragonblood chymist specializes in the reckless distillation of extracts and elixirs that allow them to experience the might of a dragon, however dangerous it might be
.

archetypes.name: Ectochymist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bombs; Poison Resistance; Poison Use; Swift Poisoning; 8th-level Alchemist Discovery; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Ectochymists study the effects of alchemy on soul and spirit, focusing on fighting ghosts and other incorporeal creatures.

archetypes.name: Ectoplasm Master
archetypes.replaces: Brew Potion
archetypes.aonSummary: Alchemists capable of distilling spectral horrors into alchemical reagents.

archetypes.name: Eldritch Poisoner
archetypes.replaces: Bomb; Throw Anything; Mutagen; Persistent Mutagen; 4th-level Discovery
archetypes.aonSummary: Eldritch poisoners are masters of the toxic arts, synthesizing lethal and incapacitating poisons with uncanny speed and expertise.

archetypes.name: Energist
archetypes.replaces: Extracts; Bombs; Poison Immunity; Throw Anything; 2nd-level Discovery; Swift Poisoning; Poison Resistance
archetypes.aonSummary: While most alchemists experiment mainly with chemicals and physical materials to create disparate effects, energists tap into the energy of life or death: positive energy or negative energy.

archetypes.name: Energy Scientist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Alchemy; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity; Poison Use; Swift Poisoning
archetypes.aonSummary: Energy scientists fervently prepare themselves to overcome exposure to specific elemental hazards so that they can traverse the Elemental Planes in search of novel discoveries and reagents.

archetypes.name: Fermenter
archetypes.replaces: Poison Resistance; 10th-level Discovery; Poison Use; Swift Poisoning
archetypes.aonSummary: Little more than moonshiners to some, fermenters focus their efforts on imbibing substances, learning from the resulting effects on their bodies, and infusing this knowledge into their skill sets.

archetypes.name: Fire Bomber
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Bomb; Throw Anything; 4th-level Discovery; Poison Resistance +6; Poison Immunity; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: (Goblin Only) Fire bombers are exceptionally good at using bombs to burn creatures and blow things up, but are not quite as good at creating other types of bombs or extracts.

archetypes.name: First World Innovator
archetypes.replaces: Brew Potion; Poison Use; Swift Poisoning; Poison Immunity; Bombs; Poison Resistance
archetypes.aonSummary: Those who can harness primal reagents—mundane reagents infused with the power of the First World—walk a fine line between genius and catastrophe.

archetypes.name: Gloom Chymist
archetypes.replaces: Bomb; Poison Resistance; Poison Use; Swift Poisoning
archetypes.aonSummary: A breakthrough in Nidalese alchemy led to the creation of glooms, magical fields of darkness from the Shadow Plane that can be momentarily animated with the use of strange compounds.

archetypes.name: Grenadier
archetypes.replaces: Brew Potion, Poison Resistance, Poison Use, Swift Poisoning, Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Grenadiers sacrifice their skill with poisons in order to become more adept at using alchemical bombs.

archetypes.name: Grenadier [MC]
archetypes.replaces: Brew Potion; Poison Resistance; Poison Use; Swift Poisoning; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Grenadiers train to exercise their talents in the thick of battle, even when not under the influence of their mutagens. They learn methods of combining weapon attacks with their alchemical magic, and sacrifice skill with poisons in order to become more adept at using alchemical bombs or using alchemical items in conjunction with their martial skills.

archetypes.name: Gun Chemist
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Bombs; Brew Potion; Throw Anything; Poison Resistance; Swift Poisoning
archetypes.aonSummary: Simple alchemists may dabble in explosives, but for the rare gun chemist, a firearm’s barrel is his crucible

archetypes.name: Herbalist
archetypes.replaces: Alchemy; Key Ability Score; Throw Anything; Bombs; Poison Use; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: (Vine Leshy only) Vine leshys who study the physical and spiritual composition of their own bodies have discovered a strange herbal alchemy all their own.

archetypes.name: Homunculist
archetypes.replaces: Poison Use; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity; Swift Poisoning; Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: One of the grand goals of alchemy is the ability to create new life. A homunculist has made this dream a reality, growing and modifying a familiar in his own laboratory.

archetypes.name: Horticulturist
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen; 2nd and 4th-level Discoveries; Bomb; Poison Resistance; Poison Use; Poison Immunity; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: A horticulturist spends his time cultivating plants and plant creatures, allowing him to experiment with strange and wondrous herbal concoctions.

archetypes.name: Ice Chemist
archetypes.replaces: Bomb; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity; 2nd-level Discovery
archetypes.aonSummary: Reclusive alchemists who dwell in the highest mountains or on the frozen tundra devote their skills to mastering the cold.

archetypes.name: Inspired Chemist
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: Akin to a mindchemistUM, inspired chemists use a type of cognatogen that instead of increasing their mental ability scores grants them inspiration like an investigator.

archetypes.name: Internal Alchemist
archetypes.replaces: Throw Anything; Swift Alchemy; Swift Poisoning
archetypes.aonSummary: An internal alchemist studies medicine, diet, and the living body to purify the self in the hope of gaining immortality.

archetypes.name: Interrogator
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bomb; Mutagen; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: An interrogator extracts vital information from reluctant individuals using alchemical and traditional methods.

archetypes.name: Mad Scientist
archetypes.replaces: Alchemy, 2nd, 4th-level Discovery; Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: The mad scientist’s colleagues laughed at her insights, mocked her theories, and hounded her from the halls of academia, simply because they were too weak and frightened to understand her work.

archetypes.name: Metamorph
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bomb; Extracts; Throw Anything; Swift Alchemy; Swift Poisoning; Instant Alchemy
archetypes.aonSummary: Metamorphs eschew traditional alchemy, focusing on internal chemistry and the transfiguration of living forms.

archetypes.name: Mindchemist
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen; Poison Use
archetypes.aonSummary: A mindchemist can reach incredible levels of mental acuity, but suffers lingering debilitating effects to his physique.

archetypes.name: Mixologist
archetypes.replaces: Alchemy; Brew Potion; Mutagen; 2nd-level Discovery; POison Resistance; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: Mixologists focus on mastering the chemical reactions between alcohol and the physical body.

archetypes.name: Mnemostiller
archetypes.replaces: Key Ability Score; Alchemy; Throw Anything; Mutagen; Bombs; Poison Resistance; Poison Use
archetypes.aonSummary: Mnemostillers extract memories; hey can return memories as easily as administering a potion, and experienced mnemostillers create a variety of effects through the careful administration of past traumas or victories

archetypes.name: Oenopion Researcher
archetypes.replaces: Poison Use, Swift Alchemy
archetypes.aonSummary: The alchemist of Oenopion is incredibly skilled at making potions, elixirs, and other materials crucial to the country's economy and its monster-creating fleshforges.

archetypes.name: Oozemaster
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bomb; Brew Potion; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: The oozemaster is a specialized alchemist who fights and ensnares oozes.

archetypes.name: Perfumer
archetypes.replaces: Extracts; Brew Potion; Bomb; Mutagen; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: A perfumer alchemist refines extracts to their most pure and rarefied forms to spread on the wind

archetypes.name: Plague Bringer
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: (Ratfolk Only) The plague bringer sees disease as the ultimate weapon, and has worked tirelessly to master new diseases and disease-delivery systems.

archetypes.name: Preservationist
archetypes.replaces: Poison Use; Poison Resistance +4; Poison Resistance +6; Poison Immunity; Persistant Mutagen; 18th-level Discovery
archetypes.aonSummary: Some alchemists are obsessed with collecting and preserving exotic creatures.

archetypes.name: Promethean Alchemist
archetypes.replaces: Brew Potion; Throw Anything; Bombs; Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: Obsessed with discovering the origins of life, promethean alchemists build constructs they gradually endow with life.

archetypes.name: Psychonaut
archetypes.replaces: Bomb; Poison Resistance +4; Poison Resistance +6; Poison Immunity; 15th-level Bomb Damage Increase; 17th-level Bomb Damage Increase
archetypes.aonSummary: A psychonaut uses his knowledge to explore altered states of consciousness and even other planes of existence.

archetypes.name: Ragechemist
archetypes.replaces: Poison Use; Swift Poisoning; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Some alchemists create mutagens that tap into a primal anger that fuels their physical transformation.

archetypes.name: Reanimator
archetypes.replaces: Bomb; 7th-level Bomb Damage Increase; 13th-level Bomb Damage Increase; 15th-level Bomb Damage Increase
archetypes.aonSummary: A reanimator is an alchemist who has discovered how to infuse a corpse with a semblance of life.

archetypes.name: Royal Alchemist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Poison Use; Swift Poisoning
archetypes.aonSummary: Many rulers often hire specialized alchemists capable of concocting protections from both poisons and diseases for the nobles and their guests.

archetypes.name: Saboteur
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: (Gnome Only) The saboteur is an alchemist who specializes in destroying the plans, materials, and allies of his enemies.

archetypes.name: Sacrament Alchemist
archetypes.replaces: Deity; Mutagen; Swift Alchemy
archetypes.aonSummary: Sacrament alchemists serve in a great variety of priestly roles for their deities.

archetypes.name: Tinkerer
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen; Poison Resistance; Poison Use; Swift Poisoning; Poison Immunity; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: Tinkerers constantly dabble in clockworking, creating special familiars that they regularly upgrade and with which they form bizarre bonds.

archetypes.name: Toxicant
archetypes.replaces: Mutagen; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: In lands such as Daggermark and Katapesh where poisons are legal and may be openly studied and sold, some alchemists obsess over the myriad ways that poisons and venoms can be applied and delivered.

archetypes.name: Trap Breaker
archetypes.replaces: Poison Use; Poison Resistance +2, +4, +6; Swift Poisoning; Poison Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Trap breakers forgo the study of poison to instead master the construction and deployment of traps, using their nimble fingers to disable dangerous devices and their alchemical knowledge to create devastating land mines.

archetypes.name: Vaultbreaker
archetypes.replaces: Brew Potion; Bombs; Throw Anything; Poison Use
archetypes.aonSummary: The vaultbreaker combines stealth with his bomb-making talents to construct special focused charges that can disable or destroy hinges, locks, and similar mechanisms.

archetypes.name: Vivisectionist
archetypes.replaces: Bomb
archetypes.aonSummary: A vivisectionist studies bodies to better understand their function.

archetypes.name: Wasteland Blightbreaker
archetypes.replaces: Poison Resistance +2, +6; Swift Poisoning; 8th-level Discovery
archetypes.aonSummary: The deleterious effects of the weird hazards of the Mana Wastes require special skill to remedy.

archetypes.name: Winged Marauder
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Mutagen; Persistent Mutagen
archetypes.aonSummary: (Goblin Only) Goblin alchemists have created a mixture of pheromones that they use to manipulate and entice giant vultures or dire bats to do their bidding.

archetypes.name: Blighted Myrmidon
archetypes.replaces: Smite Good; Fiendish Boon; 10th-level use of Smite Good; Aura of Vengeance; 15th-level Cruelty; Unholy Champion
archetypes.aonSummary: Blighted myrmidons carry the seed of rot in their black hearts and sap life from the natural world.

archetypes.name: Dread Vanguard
archetypes.replaces: Spells; Aura of Sin
archetypes.aonSummary: Some antipaladins serve or ally themselves with villains who are bent on earthly conquest.

archetypes.name: Fearmonger
archetypes.replaces: Touch of Corruption; Cruelty
archetypes.aonSummary: The fearmonger wants to do more than cause pain, misery, and confusion. He wishes to spread fear among his foes and infect entire populations with it.

archetypes.name: Insinuator
archetypes.replaces: Code of Conduct; Aura of Evil; Detect Good; Smite Good; Touch of Corruption; Aura of Cowardice; Plague Bringer; Cruelty; Channel Negative Energy; Spells; Fiendish Boon; Aura of Despair; Aura of Vengeance; Aura of Sin; Aura of Depravity; Unholy Champion
archetypes.aonSummary: Between the selfless nobility of paladins and the chaotic menace of antipaladins, there exists a path of dedicated self-interest.

archetypes.name: Iron Tyrant
archetypes.replaces: Touch of Corruption; Cruelty; Channel Negative Energy; Fiendish Boon
archetypes.aonSummary: Iron tyrants seek the strength to rule over domains as unfettered despots, and depend on their armor as protection against those they have not yet cowed.

archetypes.name: Knight of the Sepulcher
archetypes.replaces: Fiendish Boon; Aura of Despair; 10th-level Smite Good use; Aura of Vengeance; Aura of Sin; Cruetly; Aura of Depravity; Unholy Champion
archetypes.aonSummary: Not content with the antipaladin’s mere corruption of the soul, the knight of the sepulcher sacrifices mortality along with morality.

archetypes.name: Rough Rampager
archetypes.replaces: Aura of Cowardice; Aura of Despair; Aura of Sin
archetypes.aonSummary: Rough rampagers venerate Rovagug, reveling in the destruction the dark god represents.

archetypes.name: Seal-Breaker
archetypes.replaces: Aura of Cowardice; Fiendish Boon; Aura of Despair; Aura of Vengeance
archetypes.aonSummary: Seal-breakers are dedicated to the Whispering Tyrant and have tasked themselves with finding and destroying the seals that bind him within Gallowspire.

archetypes.name: Tyrant
archetypes.replaces: Code of Conduct; Class Skills; Fiendish Boon
archetypes.aonSummary: Tyrants are manipulative and lawful antipaladins, chess masters who arrange things behind the scenes to ensure that whatever happens, evil always wins, and the tyrant along with it.

archetypes.name: Aeromancer
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 5th, 11th-level Arcane Exploit
archetypes.aonSummary: While the practice of aeromancy is rare, some arcanists today are able to rival the aerial mastery of the ancient Shory aeromancers.

archetypes.name: Arcane Tinkerer
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 5th, 11th-level Arcanist Exploit
archetypes.aonSummary: Arcane tinkerers use their knowledge and understanding of magic to disrupt or even destroy constructs

archetypes.name: Blade Adept
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 3rd, and 9th-level Arcanist Exploits
archetypes.aonSummary: A small number of arcanists learn to use blades as part of their spellcasting and in combat.

archetypes.name: Blood Arcanist
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 3rd, 9th, and 15th-level Arcanist Exploits; Magical Supremacy
archetypes.aonSummary: Though most arcanists possess only a rudimentary innate arcane gift, the blood arcanist has the full power of a bloodline to draw upon.

archetypes.name: Brown-Fur Transmuter
archetypes.replaces: 3rd and 9th-level Arcanist Exploits; Magical Supremacy
archetypes.aonSummary: Frequently called “brown-furs,” these transmutation-focused arcanists are known for transforming themselves into animals.

archetypes.name: Eldritch Font
archetypes.replaces: 3rd, 7th, and 13th-level Arcanist Exploits; Magical Supremacy
archetypes.aonSummary: For some arcanists, the power bubbling up from within is nearly too much to contain.

archetypes.name: Elemental Master
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 3rd, 9th, 11th, and 15th-level Arcanist Exploits
archetypes.aonSummary: Arcanists with an affinity for elemental forces sometimes focus on one and display its power in everything they do.

archetypes.name: Harrowed Society Student
archetypes.replaces: 1st and 9th-level Arcanist Exploits; Consume Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: Based out of Varisia’s Twilight Academy, the secretive Harrowed Society focuses its efforts on the intellectual study of the region’s supernatural quirks and hidden history, and embraces the use of the harrow deck to examine the world’s occult mysteries.

archetypes.name: Magaambyan Initiate
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; 1st, 5th, 9th, 17th-level Arcanist Exploit
archetypes.aonSummary: Aspiring students of the Magaambya often spend decades researching arcane magic while learning to follow in the footsteps of the academy’s founder, Old-Mage Jatembe.

archetypes.name: Occultist
archetypes.replaces: 1st and 7th-level Arcanist Exploits; Magical Supremacy
archetypes.aonSummary: Not all arcanists peer inward to discern the deepest secrets of magic. Some look outward, connecting with extraplanar creatures and bartering for secrets, power, and favor.

archetypes.name: School Savant
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 3rd, and 7th-level Arcanist Exploits
archetypes.aonSummary: Some arcanists specialize in a school of magic and trade flexibility for focus.

archetypes.name: Spell Specialist
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 7th, 13th, and 19th-level Arcanist Exploits
archetypes.aonSummary: Where most arcanists are broad in their study of magic, a spell specialist has her power focused in a few spells.

archetypes.name: Twilight Sage
archetypes.replaces: Consume Spells; Spells; 1st and 11th-level Arcanist Exploits; Magical Supremacy
archetypes.aonSummary: The twilight sages of Geb carry out experiments to solve the ultimate puzzle and unlock the secrets of life and death. While the twilight sages generally aren’t actively malicious, most are willing to perform human experimentation in pursuit of knowledge with little regard for the casualties.

archetypes.name: Unlettered Arcanist
archetypes.replaces: Spellbooks; Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: Some arcanists store their spells as whispered secrets within familiars instead of on paper.

archetypes.name: White Mage
archetypes.replaces: 1st and 9th-level Arcanist Exploits
archetypes.aonSummary: A white mage is an arcanist touched by a divine power and gifted with the ability to heal others.

archetypes.name: Armored Hulk
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Some barbarians disdain the hides and leather used as armor by most of their kin. Instead they master the heaviest of armors, even those created by more civilized people, to gain greater protection and stability in battle.

archetypes.name: Beastkin Berserker
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; 4th, 8th, 12th-level Rage Power
archetypes.aonSummary: While some barbarians take on bestial aspects in their rages, the beastkin berserker descends so deeply into primal fury that she actually transforms into an animal.

archetypes.name: Breaker
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Breakers find the need to destroy their surroundings.

archetypes.name: Brutal Pugilist
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Some barbarians focus on using their bare hands to tear their opponents limb from limb.

archetypes.name: Brutish Swamper
archetypes.replaces: Skills; Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; 6th-level Rage Power
archetypes.aonSummary: The hardy and insular denizens of the swamp produce warriors of narrow focus and great strength.

archetypes.name: Cave Dweller
archetypes.replaces: Skills; Fast Movement; Trap Sense; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: Unused to the light of the sun, cave dwellers use their subterranean expertise to protect their clans from the manifold dangers of deep caverns and tunnels.

archetypes.name: Deepwater Rager
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Indomitable Will; Tireless Rage
archetypes.aonSummary: Deepwater ragers bellow ferociously as they charge their enemies, tackling them into the raging seas.

archetypes.name: Dreadnought
archetypes.replaces: Rage; Fast Movement; Indomitable Will; Tireless Rage
archetypes.aonSummary: Unstoppable and fearless, the dreadnought turns the terror of her enemies into violent physical power.

archetypes.name: Drunken Brute
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement
archetypes.aonSummary: Drunken brutes use potent liquor to fuel their rage and grant them additional powers.

archetypes.name: Drunken Rager
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge; 12th-level Rage Power
archetypes.aonSummary: These hotheaded, hard-drinking ruffians and brawlers are as dangerous in the midst of combat as they are in a tavern, and they wouldn’t be caught dead without a libation for either occasion.

archetypes.name: Elemental Kin
archetypes.replaces: Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Some barbarian tribes have strong ties to the elemental forces of nature.

archetypes.name: Fearsome Defender
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Trapsense; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: These savage slaves feel little pain and exist only to rain terror down on the enemies of their pitiless masters.

archetypes.name: Feral Gnasher
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Fast Movement; 2nd-level Rage Power; Trap Sense 1-5; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: (Goblin Only) Feral gnashers grow up in the wild, either raised by animals or scraping by on their own, and soon learn to fend for themselves.

archetypes.name: Flesheater
archetypes.replaces: Rage; 2nd, 8th, and 14th-level Rage Powers; Greater Rage; Mighty Rage
archetypes.aonSummary: A flesheater eats flesh to create a spiritual bond between herself and the consumed creature, allowing her to take on aspects of the creature that served as the meal.

archetypes.name: Geminate Invoker
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Class Skills; Rage; Trap Sense; 4th, 8th, 12th-level Rage Powers
archetypes.aonSummary: Geminate invokers are barbarians who use Rivethun traditions to invite spirits into their bodies.

archetypes.name: Giant Stalker
archetypes.replaces: Rage; Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Giant stalkers are followers of the Mammoth Lords who have trained since childhood to spot and track giants.

archetypes.name: Hateful Rager
archetypes.replaces: Rage; 2nd, 8th, 14th, 20th-level Rage Powers; Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense +3
archetypes.aonSummary: (Half-Orc Only) From a young age, many half-orcs are treated cruelly, bullied, ridiculed, and made outcasts. While some hide their shame, others foster a deep, burning hatred that they channel into a raw fury and unleash against their enemies.

archetypes.name: Hurler
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement
archetypes.aonSummary: The hurler becomes skilled at throwing objects at their foes before closing in for the kill.

archetypes.name: Invulnerable Rager
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Damage Reduction; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Some barbarians learn to take whatever comes their way, shrugging off mortal wounds with ease.

archetypes.name: Jungle Rager
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: A jungle rager can disappear from sight, strike from hiding, and use the environment to shield herself from harm.

archetypes.name: Mad Dog
archetypes.replaces: 2nd, 6th, 10th, 14th, 18th-level Rage Powers; Rage; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Damage Reduction; Indomitable Will
archetypes.aonSummary: Though named for the wild savages who fight alongside rabid dogs, mad dogs employ all manner of beasts as their battle brethren.

archetypes.name: Mooncursed
archetypes.replaces: Race; Rage; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Greater Rage; Mighty Rage
archetypes.aonSummary: Some barbarians exhibit an unusual form of lycanthropy powered by their fury. Such a character transforms willfully but can maintain her animal or hybrid forms only while raging.

archetypes.name: Mounted Fury
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Many barbarian tribes are masters of the horse, teaching their members how to ride from a young age.

archetypes.name: Numerian Liberator
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Indomitable Will
archetypes.aonSummary: While many native Kellids oppose the Technic League and its espousal of foul alien artifacts, the most stalwart and staunchly dedicated of these technophobic traditionalists refer to themselves as Numerian liberators.

archetypes.name: Pack Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Rage Powers; Trap Sense; 6th-level Rage Power
archetypes.aonSummary: Pack hunter barbarians team up to hunt dangerous prey to feed, to protect their camps, and as a rite of passage.

archetypes.name: Pack Rager
archetypes.replaces: 2nd, 6th, 10th, 14th, and 18th-level Rage Powers; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: Barbarian rages can be a thing of savage beauty, exhibiting a lethal grace. While such uncontrolled displays of carnage often disregard group tactics, there are those barbarians whose rages inspire and spur on their allies during the ferocious dance of death.

archetypes.name: Primal Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Rage
archetypes.aonSummary: Rather than exploding with anger, primal hunters focus their rage to strike distant targets.

archetypes.name: Raging Cannibal
archetypes.replaces: 2nd-level Rage Power; Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: While savagery is not inherently evil, some barbaric cultures thrive on depravity and welcome the act of feeding on their own kind.

archetypes.name: Savage Barbarian
archetypes.replaces: Trap Sense; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: The savage barbarian learns to avoid blows and toughen up their skin.

archetypes.name: Savage Technologist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Rage; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Savage technologists exhort Kellids to rise up against the depredations of the Technic League. But rather than rejecting technology, they wield the League’s own weapons against it.

archetypes.name: Scarred Rager
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: The scarred rager believes each wound tells the tales of her prowess and bravery.

archetypes.name: Sea Reaver
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Some sea reavers are no more than hunters of the open sea, while others are raiders striking fear into coastal settlements within reach of the sea reavers’ longships.

archetypes.name: Sharptooth
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; 6th and 12th-level Rage Powers
archetypes.aonSummary: Coastal hunters and agents of the ocean’s rage, sharptooth barbarians emulate the greatest predators of the sea.

archetypes.name: Shoanti Burn Rider
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th-level Rage Powers; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: The Shoanti tribes who live in the Cinderlands have turned the deadly emberstorms that plague the region into a rite of passage. A few who survive the experience begin to embrace the adrenaline and surge of joy that comes from dancing along the edge of a whirling firestorm. These thrill-seekers are known as burn riders, and their exploits are celebrated by all Shoanti.

archetypes.name: Superstitious
archetypes.replaces: Trap Sense; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: The superstitious barbarian is naturally distrusting, developing keen senses to protect themselves from harm.

archetypes.name: Titan Mauler
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Indomitable Will
archetypes.aonSummary: In lands overrun by giants, dragons, and other hulking beasts, entire fellowships of barbarians hone tactics and traditions with one purpose—to bring low these massive foes.

archetypes.name: Totem Warrior
archetypes.replaces: None
archetypes.aonSummary: The totem warrior has a special totem that is the patron of her tribe.

archetypes.name: True Primitive
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Isolated and xenophobic tribes that dwell in areas untouched by civilization often see anything from cities and organized settlements as strange, dangerous, and decadent.

archetypes.name: Untamed Rager
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: There are no rules in the wild. Some barbarians enter combat with only victory in mind and do anything in their power to achieve it.

archetypes.name: Urban Barbarian
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Rage
archetypes.aonSummary: Every barbarian knows that city life can soften the spirit and the body, but some barbarians take on the trappings and ways of their adoptive homes and bend their savage powers to its challenges.

archetypes.name: Wild Rager
archetypes.replaces: Rage; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Rages are barely controlled, but there are those who wholly give in to their more savage side, letting their rages take them to a confusing and uncontrolled place of terrible savagery.

archetypes.name: Wildborn
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Trap Sense; Rage Powers; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: Some barbarians are born or bred outside the reach of civilization. These wildborn fight and survive without ever seeing a forge or worked stone, and only dare a trip into the city when no other option is available.

archetypes.name: Animal Speaker
archetypes.replaces: Fascinate; Well-Versed; Inspire Competence; Suggestion; Mass Suggestion
archetypes.aonSummary: An animal speaker focuses not on the ears and minds of humans, but on the creatures of the wild and those in the underbellies of cities.

archetypes.name: Arcane Duelist
archetypes.replaces: Countersong; Suggestion; Mass Suggestion; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed; Lore Master; Jack of all Trades
archetypes.aonSummary: A master of the martial applications of steel and spell, the arcane duelist blends both into a lethal combination.

archetypes.name: Arcane Healer
archetypes.replaces: Versatile Performance; Loremaster
archetypes.aonSummary: Though bards may have different reasons for wanting to heal the sick and injured, both out of pure altruism and in order to keep adventuring companions safe, the ability to heal also makes it much easier for a bard to pose as a cleric or other divine healer, opening the door for a wide array of swindles and scams.

archetypes.name: Archaeologist
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Performance; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed
archetypes.aonSummary: No stodgy researcher, this archaeologist meets his research head-on in the field.

archetypes.name: Archivist
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage; Suggestion; Mass Suggestion; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed; Lore Master; Jack of all Trades
archetypes.aonSummary: Some bards greatly prefer academic pursuits to the drama (and sometimes melodrama) of their artistic brethren.

archetypes.name: Argent Voice
archetypes.replaces: Fascinate; Dirge of Doom; Frightening Tune; Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: Argent voices are agents of the Silver Ravens that dedicate themselves to the study of the magical performance are known as the "Song of Silver".

archetypes.name: Arrowsong Minstrel
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiency; Spellcasting; Bardic Knowledge; Dirge of Doom; Distraction; Fascinate; Inspire Competence; Lore Master; Soothing Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: Arrowsong minstrels combine the elven traditions of archery, song, and spellcasting into a seamless harmony of dazzling magical effects.

archetypes.name: Averaka Arbiter
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Competence; Dirge of Doom; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed
archetypes.aonSummary: Some Averakan bards make it their mission to unify their fellow half-orcs, and are equally skilled at helping allies defeat common enemies and at building a new civilization that reflects their unique identity.

archetypes.name: Brazen Deceiver
archetypes.replaces: Countersong; Distraction; Bardic Knowledge; Well-Versed; Versatile Performance; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: Where other thieves use stealth or intimidation to achieve their goals, the brazen deceiver depends on lies backed by powerful shadow magic.

archetypes.name: Buccaneer
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Suggestion; Lore Master; Mass Suggestion
archetypes.aonSummary: A buccaneer is a pirate who specializes in raiding ships and port towns, but who leaves his victims alive whenever possible.

archetypes.name: Busker
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: A busker uses his dazzling physical stunts to get by on his own in the city streets.

archetypes.name: Celebrity
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage; Lore Master; Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: Known for being known, a celebrity bard is a master of performance who captures the imagination and attention of his audience.

archetypes.name: Chelish Diva
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge, Well-Versed, Lore Master, Inspire Competence, Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: In their pursuit of glory, a Chelish diva seeks to prove themselves better than any upstart actor, dancer, or chorus member through magic and discipline.

archetypes.name: Chronicler of Worlds
archetypes.replaces: Key Ability Score; Alignment; Bardic Knowledge; Inspire Greatness; Inspire Heroics; Well-Versed; Versatile Performance;
archetypes.aonSummary: A chronicler of worlds forsakes morality in service of understanding; she is both warrior and mystic, scholar and soldier.

archetypes.name: Court Bard
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage; Inspire Competence; Dirge of Doom; Frightening Tune; Bardic Knowledge; Lore Master; Jack of all Trades
archetypes.aonSummary: The court bard takes up the role of resplendent proclaimer and artist-in-residence at the hand of nobility, royalty, and the well-moneyed elite who aspire to join their ranks.

archetypes.name: Court Fool
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Countersong; Inspire Competence; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: The court fool holds up an unflattering mirror to those in charge or speaks truths, however veiled, that no one else can safely utter.

archetypes.name: Cultivator
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Spells; Bardic Knowledge; Countersong; Well-Versed; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: Cultivators use music to promote plant growth and influence the behavior of plants both naturally and supernaturally.

archetypes.name: Daredevil
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Inspire Courage; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: As quick at wordplay as at swordplay, daredevils are dashing heroes, inspiring their allies to match their clever repartee and acrobatic feats.

archetypes.name: Dawnflower Dervish
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Performance, Bardic Knowledge, Lore Master, Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: Many bards of Sarenrae's faith hone their skills with dance and scimitar to become dervish dancers.

archetypes.name: Demagogue
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage +1; Lore Master; Suggestion; Mass Suggestion
archetypes.aonSummary: Not content with providing amusing and occasionally instructive performances, the demagogue seeks to inflame and ignite his audience.

archetypes.name: Dervish Dancer
archetypes.replaces: Suggestion; Mass Suggestion; Dirge of Doom; Frightening Performance; Bardic Knowledge; Lore Master; Versatile Performance; Soothing Performance; Deadly Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: Not all bards inspire others with their performances. Dervish dancers enter a near-mystical trance that allows them to push their bodies beyond normal limits.

archetypes.name: Detective
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage; Inspire Greatness; Inspire Heroics; Bardic Knowledge; Well-Versed; Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: Piecing together clues and catching the guilty with sheer cleverness, the detective is skilled at divining the truth.

archetypes.name: Dirge Bard
archetypes.replaces: Jack of all Trades; Well-Versed; Versatile Performance; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: A composer of sonorous laments for the dead and elaborate requiems for those lost yet long remembered, dirge bards master musical tools and tropes that must appeal to the ears and hearts of both the living and the dead.

archetypes.name: Disciple of the Forked Tongue
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage; Inspire Greatness; Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: (Vishkanya) Studied in venomous words as well as venomous blood, a disciple of the forked tongue knows just the right phrase to slowly poison the soul.

archetypes.name: Dragon Herald
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Bardic Knowledge; Countersong; Fascinate; Inspire Competence; Soothing Performance; Inspire Heroics; Lore Master; Jack-of-all-Trades
archetypes.aonSummary: (Kobold Only) Dragon heralds are messengers and evangelists of true dragonkind. They carry the word of their dragon patrons far and wide, whether that’s a message of peace or a declaration of war.

archetypes.name: Dragon Yapper
archetypes.replaces: Fascinate; Dirge of Doom; Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: (Kobold Only) Kobolds’ yammering songs distract opponents in combat, hindering their ability to attack.

archetypes.name: Duettist
archetypes.replaces: Well-Versed; Jack-of-all-Trades; Bardic Knowledge; Versatile Performance; Lore Master; Dirge of Doom; Frightening Tune
archetypes.aonSummary: Whether singing a delicate duo with a nightingale or slipping coins from purses while a trained monkey distracts the crowd, the duettist blends his bond to his familiar with his natural talent for performance to create amazing effects.

archetypes.name: Dwarven Scholar
archetypes.replaces: Key Ability Score; Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Versatile Performance; Inspire Courage; Suggestion
archetypes.aonSummary: A dwarven scholar researches the lineage of the kings of the old dwarven empires and learns their ancient tactics.

archetypes.name: Faith Singer
archetypes.replaces: Deity; Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: Faith singers show their faith in their deity with songs or other appropriate performances.

archetypes.name: Fey Courtier
archetypes.replaces: Dirge of Doom; Frightening Tune; Inspire Heroics; Versatile Performance: Inspire Competence
archetypes.aonSummary: (Gathlain) Fey who associate with courts often become bards skilled at navigating the inhuman societies of the trackless wilds.

archetypes.name: Fey Prankster
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Countersong; Inspire Courage; Dirge of Doom; Well-Versed; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: Sly and mischievous like the Lantern King himself, fey pranksters learn supernatural tricks that can cause their victims to suffer mishaps and accidents.

archetypes.name: Filidh
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Spellcasting; Inspire Courage; Suggestion; Dirge of Doom; Inspire Heroics; Deadly Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: By tapping into the world’s natural music, specialized bards known as filidhs are able to see not only the tapestry of life but divine portents of the future from the rhythm of all life’s song.

archetypes.name: First World Minstrel
archetypes.replaces: Spell List; Bardic Knowledge; Inspire Courage; Dirge of Doom; Well-Versed
archetypes.aonSummary: The First World minstrel's performances channel the mysterious powers of the First World.

archetypes.name: Flame Dancer
archetypes.replaces: Countersong; Inspire Competence; Suggestion; Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: A flame dancer studies the movements of fire, adding its grace to his repertoire.

archetypes.name: Flamesinger
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Lore Master; Inspire Courage; Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: The flamesinger finds inspiration in the mesmerizing beauty of fire.

archetypes.name: Fortune-Teller
archetypes.replaces: Spell List; Bardic Performance; Countersong; Distraction; Well-Versed; Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: Instead of using song and dance, a fortune-teller influences people by divining their fate.

archetypes.name: Geisha
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Bardic Knowledge
archetypes.aonSummary: Specially trained entertainers called geisha are praised for their appearance and skill at conversation, music, dancing, singing, poetry, and calligraphy.

archetypes.name: Hatharat Agent
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Well-Versed; Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: Although the Hatharat employs all manner of specialists, bards who take up the role of agent are among its most infamous and widespread.

archetypes.name: Hoaxer
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Inspire Courage; Inspire Competence; Inspire Greatness; Countersong; Distraction; Inspire Greatness; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: Hoaxers specialize in creating valuable-looking counterfeits and infusing these false treasures with dangerous magic to make their marks more vulnerable to future swindles.

archetypes.name: Impervious Messenger
archetypes.replaces: Fascinate; Suggestion; Mass Suggestion; Dirge of Doom; Frightening Tune; Bardic Knowledge; Well-Versed
archetypes.aonSummary: The impervious messenger is capable of harnessing the unique qualities of bardic magic to keep, transport, and communicate the most precious of secrets and messages.

archetypes.name: Juggler
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Bardic Knowledge; Lore Master; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed; Soothing Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: Jugglers are masters of manipulating objects, most famously by keeping multiple objects in the air simultaneously.

archetypes.name: Lotus Geisha
archetypes.replaces: Different Weapon Proficiencies; Well-Versed; Bardic Knowledge; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: The lotus geisha of Minkai are renowned for their powers of seduction.

archetypes.name: Luring Piper
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bardic Knowledge; Dirge of Doom; Soothing Performance; Well-Versed
archetypes.aonSummary: Some bards have an exceptional ability to use their musical performances to entrance the world’s wilder creatures.

archetypes.name: Magician
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage; Dirge of Doom; Frightening Tune; Bardic Knowledge; Countersong; Well-Versed; Versatile Performance; Lore Master; Jack of all Trades
archetypes.aonSummary: A magician dabbles in performance, but sees it as a means to tap into universal energies and channel them.

archetypes.name: Masked Performer
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Countersong; Inspire Competence; Surggestion; Mass Suggestion; Versatile Performance; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: The masked performer takes on the persona represented by the likeness she wears.

archetypes.name: Mute Musician
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Inspire Competence; Frightening Tune; Inspire Heroics; Mass Suggestion; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed; Jack-of-All-Trades
archetypes.aonSummary: A mute musician forswears speech for the unnatural songs and thunderous silences of the depths of space.

archetypes.name: Negotiator
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Bardic Performance; Versatile Performance; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: Negotiators are those bards who take the skills of a performer and apply them to the realms of business and law.

archetypes.name: Phrenologist
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Well-Versed; Jack-of-all-Trades; Inspire Courage; Inspire Competence; Fascinate
archetypes.aonSummary: The phrenologist is an expert at reading creatures’ skulls, and he learns to use this knowledge to his benefit.

archetypes.name: Pitax: Academy of Grand Arts
archetypes.replaces: Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: Those who have successfully mastered the strict curriculum of the Academy of Grand Arts.

archetypes.name: Plant Speaker
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Greatness; Bardic Knowledge; Well-Versed; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: (Vine Leshy only) Plant speakers build upon their racial plantspeech ability and their storytelling tendencies to create an art form full of deep metaphors and allegory rather than specific details and facts.

archetypes.name: Prankster
archetypes.replaces: Fascinate; Suggestion; Mass Suggestion; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: (Gnome Only) The prankster sees humor as the highest form or art, and pranks as the highest form of humor.

archetypes.name: Provocateur
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; 2nd-level Versatile Performance; Suggestion, Mass Suggestion
archetypes.aonSummary: Provocateurs are bards who use their art to make controversial political statements, undermine enemies’ reputations, and upset the status quo on a large scale.

archetypes.name: Ringleader (AG)
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Performance; Well-Versed; Versatile Performance; Suggestion; Mass Suggestion; Soothing Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: Ringleaders are specialists who oversee large operations in which trouble could strike at any moment and any place.

archetypes.name: Ringleader (UI)
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Competence; Dirge of Doom; Frightening Tune; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: Ringleaders are adept in getting the most out of their allies, and they excel at planning for unexpected complications in advance.

archetypes.name: Sandman
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage; Suggestion; Inspire Greatness; Inspire Heroics; Mass Suggestion; Deadly Performance; Bardic Knowledge; Versatile Performance; Inspire Competence; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: Combining performance with stealth, trickery, and guile, the sandman uses cleverness to keep others off-balance.

archetypes.name: Savage Skald
archetypes.replaces: Fascinate; Suggestion; Jack of all Trades; Soothing Performance; Mass Suggestion
archetypes.aonSummary: Far from civilization, furious tribes have their own war-singers, work-chanters, and lore-keepers, savaging enemies with song and sword alike.

archetypes.name: Sea Singer
archetypes.replaces: Countersong; Inspire Competence; Suggestion; Mass Suggestion; Bardic Knowledge; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed
archetypes.aonSummary: The sea singer calls the blue waters his home, and is much in demand among sea captains wishing good fortune for their crew and hull as they ply the tradewinds far and wide.

archetypes.name: Shadow Puppeteer
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage; Inspire Competence
archetypes.aonSummary: (Wayang Only) A shadow puppeteer invokes amazing and terrifying shadow puppet shows, producing supernatural effects by creating and manipulating shadow.

archetypes.name: Silver Balladeer
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Suggestion; Inspire Greatness; Mass Suggestion; Well-Versed; 2nd-level Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: The bright purity of silver makes beautiful music, and its vibrations are also anathema to unnatural creatures. Some bards use a mixture of silver-stringed instruments and esoteric knowledge to battle the dark forces of the world.

archetypes.name: Solacer
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bardic Knowledge; Lore Master; Countersong; Versatile Performance; Jack-of-All-Trades
archetypes.aonSummary: Solacers are experts in the healing arts as well as creators of performances that console the distraught, rally the stricken, raise spirits, and vanquish sorrow.

archetypes.name: Songhealer
archetypes.replaces: Versatile Performance; Frightening Tune; Deadly Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: The songhealer brings peace and surcease of pain, calming wild emotions and providing a balm for the wounded body.

archetypes.name: Sorrowsoul
archetypes.replaces: Soothing Perfrmance; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: While most bards, on occasion, sing mournful tunes or craft elegies that depict the deepest sadness or the most profound suffering, the sorrowsoul has known tragedy and loss on a level so intimate, he has bound it to his soul.

archetypes.name: Sound Striker
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Competence; Suggestion
archetypes.aonSummary: They say that words can cut deeper than any blade, and the sound striker proves this true.

archetypes.name: Speaker of the Palatine Eye
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Spells; Countersong; Jack-of-all-Trades
archetypes.aonSummary: speaker of the Palatine Eye influences others using his occult knowledge rather than the boisterous enthusiasm of most bards.

archetypes.name: Stonesinger
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Bardic Performance; Countersong; Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: Stonesingers are rare bards capable of vocalizing their bardic performances through subsonic harmonies, allowing their performances to carry as subtle vibrations through stone, rather than through the air.

archetypes.name: Street Performer
archetypes.replaces: Inspire Courage; Inspire Competence; Inspire Greatness; Inspire Heroics; Countersong; Bardic Knowledge; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: Whether acrobat, troubadour, or thespian, the street performer mixes with the masses, singing for his supper.

archetypes.name: Studious Librarian
archetypes.replaces: Distraction; Suggestion; Jack-of-All-Trades; Dirge of Doom; Mass Suggestion; Deadly Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: Studious librarians are bards that have studied long in great libraries of the Inner Sea region.

archetypes.name: Thundercaller
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Inspire Competence; Suggestion; Mass Suggestion; Dirge of Doom; Frightening Tune
archetypes.aonSummary: Thundercallers bear the knowledge of the ancients, wielding it like a weapon to protect the land for which they care so deeply.

archetypes.name: Voice of Brigh
archetypes.replaces: Fascinate; Dirge of Doom; Soothing Performance; Frightening Tune
archetypes.aonSummary: The Whisper in Bronze sometimes sends inspiration to her favorite followers in the form of music

archetypes.name: Voice of the Wild
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Countersong; Versatile Performance; Jack-of-all-Trades; Inspire Competence; Dirge of Doom; Inspire Heroics
archetypes.aonSummary: Most bards are inspired by the art of civilization, yet the voice of the wild’s muse is the grandeur and beauty of nature.

archetypes.name: Wasteland Chronicler
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Inspire Competence
archetypes.aonSummary: Wasteland chroniclers explore the farthest reaches of desolate wastelands, seeking to unlock the mysteries found there and meet the inhabitants of such regions

archetypes.name: Watersinger
archetypes.replaces: Fascinate, Suggestion, Mass Suggestion, Inspire Competence, 5th-level Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: (Undine Only) The watersinger’s song reaches from the depths of his soul into the elemental waters from which life first sprang.

archetypes.name: Wit
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Inspire Competence; Dirge of Doom; Frightening Tune; Versatile Performance; Lore Master; Jack-of-All-Trades
archetypes.aonSummary: The wit is a master of clever repartee and verbal dueling, moving through noble courts like a fish through water.

archetypes.name: Ancestral Harbinger
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; 6th, 12th, and 18th-level Bloodline Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: While all bloodragers tap into their bloodlines to fuel the arcane energies they use in battle, some have the ability to call directly to the spirits of their ancestors to aid them, summoning spirits to fight for them or inspire their allies.

archetypes.name: Blood Conduit
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Bloodline Feats; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Indomitable Will
archetypes.aonSummary: Blood conduits learn to channel their arcane might directly through their flesh, without the need for mystical words or gestures.

archetypes.name: Bloodrider
archetypes.replaces: Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; 9th-level Bloodline Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: In the world’s wild lands, a mount is an advantage in both everyday life and the dealing of death

archetypes.name: Bloody-Knuckled Rowdy
archetypes.replaces: Damage Reduction; Spellcasting; Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: The bloody-knuckled rowdy focuses on tricks and maneuvers that are quick and effective, duplicating combat styles from professional brawlers, street thugs, and even trapped animals.

archetypes.name: Crossblooded Rager
archetypes.replaces: Bonus Feats; Bonus Spells; Bloodline Powers; Saving Throws
archetypes.aonSummary: While most bloodragers manifest only one bloodline, there are some that, through some quirk of heredity or the conjunction of other powers, manifest two.

archetypes.name: Enlightened Bloodrager
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; 1st, 4th-level Bloodline Power; Bloodrage; Bonus Spells; 7th, 13th, 19th-level Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: Troubled by overwhelming rage and mystic forces beyond their comprehension, bloodragers have been traveling to the Magaambya for generations, seeking the peace and enlightenment promised by students of Old-Mage Jatembe.

archetypes.name: Greenrager
archetypes.replaces: Blood Sanctuary; 6th and 9th-level Bloodline Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Typically, nature finds its greatest harmony with divine magic, but sometimes a connection with the natural world manifest itself through the arcane current in the veins of the bloodragers called greenragers.

archetypes.name: Hag-Riven
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: All changelings have the potential to transform into hags, but the process is a slow one, requiring several nights to complete. When left incomplete—by virtue of a wily changeling’s escape or her mother’s death—the creature is scarred and saturated in arcane power.

archetypes.name: Id Rager
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline; Bloodline Spells; Bloodline Powers; Spellcasting; Eschew Materials; Bloodline Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: An id rager lacks a supernatural taint to his blood, instead drawing power from pure emotion.

archetypes.name: Metamagic Rager
archetypes.replaces: Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: While metamagic is difficult for many bloodragers to utilize, a talented few are able to channel their bloodrage in ways that push their spells to impressive ends.

archetypes.name: Primalist
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline
archetypes.aonSummary: While bloodrage powers come from the very essence of a bloodrager’s being and are often strict and immutable, some bloodragers tap into ancient traditions and primitive wisdom to enhance their rages with something more primal.

archetypes.name: Prowler at World's End
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline Powers; 9th, 12th, 15th-level Bloodline Feats; Greater Bloodrage; Mighty Bloodrage
archetypes.aonSummary: Many catfolk bloodragers capable of communing with the ancient spirits of creation take on the burden of protecting the world from the sinister forces that exist at the world’s fringes.

archetypes.name: Rageshaper
archetypes.replaces: Blood Sanctuary; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: All bloodragers blend the unpredictable surge of arcane power with the savage fury of battle lust. For most, their rage is a conduit for the eldritch power locked in their heritage, but for a rageshaper, the latent magical energies in his blood bring about physical transformations and facilitate the blending of arcana and aggression into a deadly synthesis that few other barbarians (or even other bloodragers) can match.

archetypes.name: Spelleater
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: Where other bloodragers learn to avoid or shrug off minor damage of all sorts, spelleaters tap into the power of their bloodline in order to heal damage as it comes, and can even cannibalize their own magical energy to heal more damage and continue taking the fight to the enemy.

archetypes.name: Steelblood
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Fast Movement; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: Most bloodragers prefer light armor, but some learn the secret of using heavy armors.

archetypes.name: Symbol Striker
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Fast Movement; 6th, 9th, 12th, 18th-level Bloodline Feats;
archetypes.aonSummary: Symbol strikers are unique form of rune-wielding berserker spellcasters whose tradition originates from Dongun Hold, a Sky Citadel in Alkenstar

archetypes.name: Untouchable Rager
archetypes.replaces: Spells; Blood Casting; Eschew Materials; Bloodline Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: While most bloodragers are known for their inexplicable ability to focus their bloodline into a horrifying mix of martial terror and spellcasting fury, from time to time a bloodrager’s bloodline acts differently.

archetypes.name: Urban Bloodrager
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Bloodrage; Blood Sanctuary; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: Like the urban barbarian, the urban bloodrager has learned to control her rage in so-called polite society.

archetypes.name: Battle Dancer
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Armor Proficiencies; Brawler's Cunning; Brawler's Flurry; AC Bonus; Knockout
archetypes.aonSummary: Battle dancers practice a martial art that emphasizes constant motion

archetypes.name: Bouncer
archetypes.replaces: Martial Flexibility; 2nd-level Bonus Feat; Close Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Some taverns employ bouncers to keep out undesirables or for when their customers get too rowdy.

archetypes.name: Constructed Pugilist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Martial Flexibility; Bonus Combat Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Brawlers that develop combat skills that use their prostheses so they always have a weapon at hand

archetypes.name: Exemplar
archetypes.replaces: Unarmed Strike; Close Weapon Mastery; Maneuver Training; AC Bonus; Brawler’s Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: A versatile soldier who inspires her companions with her fighting prowess, an exemplar is at home on the front lines of battles anywhere.

archetypes.name: Feral Striker
archetypes.replaces: Martial Flexibility
archetypes.aonSummary: A feral striker taps into a reservoir of druidic power hidden inside herself, allowing her to take animalistic characteristics.

archetypes.name: Hinyasi
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiencies; 2nd-level Bonus Feat; Knockout; Close Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The hinyasi's martial traditions are centered on the use of farming tools and on other improvised weapons.

archetypes.name: Living Avalanche
archetypes.replaces: 2nd and 5th-level Bonus Feats; Maneuver Training; AC Bonus; Awesome Blow; Improved Awesome Blow
archetypes.aonSummary: When a living avalanche is on the move, no one can stand in her way.

archetypes.name: Mutagenic Mauler
archetypes.replaces: Martial Flexibility; AC Bonus
archetypes.aonSummary: Not content with perfecting her body with natural methods, a mutagenic mauler resorts to alchemy to unlock the primal beast within.

archetypes.name: Shield Champion
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, and 19th-level Maneuver Training; Brawler’s Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: Stalwart in battle, a shield champion has perfected an entire martial discipline relying on only her hand-to-hand fighting skills and her ever-present shield.

archetypes.name: Snakebite Striker
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Martial Flexibility; 3rd, 7th, 11th, and 19th-level Maneuver Training
archetypes.aonSummary: With her lightning quickness and guile, a snakebite striker keeps her foes’ attention focused on her, because any one of her feints might be an actual attack.

archetypes.name: Steel-Breaker
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Brawler’s Strike; Maneuver Training
archetypes.aonSummary: The steel-breaker studies destruction and practices it as an art form.

archetypes.name: Strangler
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Brawler’s Flurry; AC Bonus; Knockout; Awesome Blow; Improved Awesome Blow
archetypes.aonSummary: A strangler is trained to choke the life out of her victims with her vise-like grip.

archetypes.name: Strong-Side Boxer
archetypes.replaces: AC Bonus; Maneuver Training; Close Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: A strong-side boxer employs a unique fighting style that incorporates a rope or cord wound around her hand.

archetypes.name: Turfer
archetypes.replaces: Maneuver Training; Knockout
archetypes.aonSummary: A turfer has a mastery over particular types of terrain.

archetypes.name: Ulfen Beast-Wrestler
archetypes.replaces: Maneuver Training; AC Bonus
archetypes.aonSummary: For these mighty grapplers, wrestling normal opponents has lost its challenge—they seek greater targets for glory.

archetypes.name: Venomfist
archetypes.replaces: Unarmed Strike; Knockout; Close Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Thanks to alchemical experiments and rigorous study of venomous creatures, a venomfist has toxic unarmed strikes.

archetypes.name: Verdant Grappler
archetypes.replaces: 2nd and 11th-level Bonus Feats; Maneuver Training; Close Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: By accepting spirits of nature into her soul, a verdant grappler can entangle her foes with tangled undergrowth.

archetypes.name: Wild Child
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th, 14th, 17th, and 20th-level Bonus Combat Feats; Close Weapon Mastery; Maneuver Training
archetypes.aonSummary: The wild child works with his sworn animal friend to conquer the challenges that lay before them.

archetypes.name: Winding Path Renegade
archetypes.replaces: 2nd, 8th, 14th-level Bonus Feat; AC Bonus
archetypes.aonSummary: Winding path renegades studied at the Houses of Perfection in Jalmeray, but while they grasped the mechanical aspects of the forms, they lacked the mental discipline required by the masters of the school.

archetypes.name: Beast Rider
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Expert Trainer
archetypes.aonSummary: Where some cavaliers are simply skilled with horses or well-trained knights, the beast rider spends his life in constant pursuit of the most perfect mount, forming bonds with greater, more powerful, and more exotic creatures.

archetypes.name: Castellan
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Cavalier’s Charge; Expert Trainer; Mighty Charge; Demanding Challenge; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: A castellan is a cavalier who dedicates himself to the defense of a castle or walled city.

archetypes.name: Charger
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Mount; Cavalier’s Charge; Expert Trainer; Mighty Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: (Centaur Only) No warrior better epitomizes the centaur’s devastating martial power than the charger.

archetypes.name: Circuit Judge
archetypes.replaces: Tactician; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician; Challenge; Demanding Challenge
archetypes.aonSummary: A circuit judge claims a specific region, becoming an expert in the local laws and, perhaps, becoming a fearsome executioner.

archetypes.name: Constable
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Mount; Cavalier’s Charge; Expert Trainer; Banner; Mighty Charge; Supreme Charge; Greater Banner
archetypes.aonSummary: Constables keep order in the narrow streets and dark alleys of settlements.

archetypes.name: Courtly Knight
archetypes.replaces: Tactician; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician
archetypes.aonSummary: These courtly knights are equally at home in a duel with words or swords.

archetypes.name: Daring Champion
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Mount; Cavalier’s Charge; Expert Trainer; Mighty Charge; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: While many cavaliers are the champions of old fighting forms, some younger, more daring cavaliers mix a martial style influenced by the lighter armored and more flamboyant swashbuckler forms with the dedication of cavalier orders.

archetypes.name: Daring General
archetypes.replaces: 6th, 12th, 18th-level Bonus Feats; Demanding Challenge; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: Those cavaliers most gifted at command often become daring generals.

archetypes.name: Disciple of the Pike
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Cavalier's Charge; Expert Trainer; Banner; Greater Banner; Mighty Charge; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: The Hellknight Order of the Pike are renowned monster hunters, taking on large game using ancient weapon arts combined with modern equipment.

archetypes.name: Drakerider
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Tactcian; Expert Trainer; Banner; Greater Tactician; Greater Banner; Master Tactician;
archetypes.aonSummary: While many cavaliers dream of riding a dragon into battle, drakeriders come to learn that the reality involves far more effort than they had expected.

archetypes.name: Emissary
archetypes.replaces: Tactician; Banner; Greater Tactician; Greater Banner; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: Some cavaliers focus more on speed and mobility than they do on the raw power of the mounted charge.

archetypes.name: Esquire
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Cavalier’s Charge; Expert Trainer; Banner; Mighty Charge; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: The esquire is a roving knight who acquires the services of a faithful follower—an aide-de-camp—who serves as the esquire’s assistant, spear carrier, and guard.

archetypes.name: Fell Rider
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Cavalier’s Charge; Expert Trainer; Banner; Mighty Charge; Greater Banner; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: (Hobgoblin Only) The fell rider rides a bestial steed, a mount mastered by him alone. He tramples his enemies down, leaving twisted bodies in his wake, and fear rides with him.

archetypes.name: First Mother's Fang
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon Proficiencies; Mount; Order
archetypes.aonSummary: A first mother’s fang acts as a servant of his nation, a skilled general and tactician in times of war and a noble governor during times of peace.

archetypes.name: Gallant
archetypes.replaces: Order; Banner; Greater Banner
archetypes.aonSummary: Gallants embody the virtues of honor, generosity, and civility. Their personal symbol serves as an inspiration to others in a courtly setting as much as on a battlefield.

archetypes.name: Gendarme
archetypes.replaces: Tactician; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: The gendarme cares less for the finer points of tactical precision than he does for the exhilaration of the charge: the rush of wind through the visor of his helmet, the feel of his couched lance, the satisfying shriek of armor giving way before his weapon’s force as the point drives past metal into his foes.

archetypes.name: Ghost Rider
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Tactician; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician; Cavalier’s Charge; Expert Trainer; Banner; Mighty Charge; Greater Banner
archetypes.aonSummary: Ghost riders are conflicted warriors who use the powers of the phantasmal dead even while seeking out and banishing the corruption of undeath from plagued communities.

archetypes.name: Green Knight
archetypes.replaces: Tactician; Mount; Order; Cavalier’s Charge; Expert Trainer; Banner; Greater Tactician; Mighty Charge; Greater Banner; Master Tactician; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: Some knights serve nature itself and can be found protecting unspoiled natural places or serving fey beings.

archetypes.name: Herald Squire
archetypes.replaces: Tactician; 2nd-level Order Ability; Cavalier's Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: The herald squire is the eyes and ears of a traveling knight.

archetypes.name: Honor Guard
archetypes.replaces: Challenge; Cavalier’s Charge; Mighty Charge; Demanding Challenge
archetypes.aonSummary: Certain cavaliers are trained not as advance combatants, but as loyal guards, standing as firm defenders in the face of threats to their chosen charge.

archetypes.name: Hooded Knight
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Mount; Tactician; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician
archetypes.aonSummary: Some cavaliers wander the lonely roads of the world—any world, including the First World—protecting travelers and acting as their honor guard.

archetypes.name: Huntmaster
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Challenge; Mount; Tactician; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician; Cavalier’s Charge; Expert Trainer; Banner; Bonus Feats; Mighty Charge; Greater Banner; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: Huntmasters train the beasts favored by lordly castes into swift and deadly trackers.

archetypes.name: Hussar
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiencies; Class Skills; Tactician; Banner; Greater Banner; 6th, 12th, 18th-level Bonus Feats; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician
archetypes.aonSummary: Agile and maneuverable cavalry, hussars make up for their relatively light armor with their speed and cunning.

archetypes.name: Knight of Arnisant
archetypes.replaces: Tactician; Expert Trainer; Banner; Greater Tactician; Demanding Challenge; Greater Tactician
archetypes.aonSummary: The cavaliers known as knights of Arnisant revere the famous general who was crucial in the defeat of the Whispering Tyrant, the powerful wizard-king. Knights of Arnisant call upon Arnisant to grant them protection from evil magic, just as the Shield of Aroden protected him.

archetypes.name: Luring Cavalier
archetypes.replaces: Challenge; Cavalier’s Charge; Mighty Charge; Demanding Challenge; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: Those who study the perfection of strategy and tactics know that picking the battlefield can grant advantages that only overwhelming numbers of allies can eclipse.

archetypes.name: Musketeer
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Expert Trainer
archetypes.aonSummary: Some cavaliers are entrusted by their masters with the care and use of expensive and powerful oddities—firearms.

archetypes.name: Oceanrider
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Mount; Expert Trainer
archetypes.aonSummary: Oceanriders are underwater cavaliers who ride dolphins, orcas, or seahorses.

archetypes.name: Qabarat Outrider
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Tactician; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician; Banner; Greater Banner
archetypes.aonSummary: (Lashunta Only) The war colleges of the Castrovelian city-state of Qabarat produce a distinctive breed of cavalier known as the Qabarat outrider. In defense of the lashunta city-states, outriders lead small units of regular troops, the members of which can link minds with one another to form bonds in battle few can match.

archetypes.name: Qadiran Horselord
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Mount; Tactician; Cavalier's Charge; 6th-level Bonus Feat; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician
archetypes.aonSummary: Much like the breed of horses they ride, Qadiran horselords pride themselves on their mobility and endurance.

archetypes.name: Saurian Champion
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Challenge; Order; Cavalier’s Mount; Tactician; Greater Tactician; Master Tactician; Banner; Greater Banner
archetypes.aonSummary: These primeval cavaliers idolize dinosaurs as apex predators and value them as powerful, oversized mounts.

archetypes.name: Sister-in-Arms
archetypes.replaces: Challenge; Order; Mount; Cavalier's Charge; Expert Trainer; Mighty Charge; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: Some of the most charismatic Gray Maidens combine their devotion to their sisters with the intense tactical training they received, learning to perfectly direct their companions and inspiring them to survive and emerge victorious.

archetypes.name: Spellscar Drifter
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Tactician; Cavalier’s Charge; Banner Cavalier; Bonus Feats; Greater Tactician; Mighty Charge; Demanding Challenge; Master Tactician; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: Spellscar drifters are self-reliant and always keep their firearms loaded—in the Spellscar Desert, a rider with a slow draw doesn’t live long.

archetypes.name: Standard Bearer
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Banner; Mighty Charge; Supreme Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: Some cavaliers prefer to stand away from the fray, their banners a beacon shining brightly over the battlefield, rallying their troops to victory.

archetypes.name: Strategist
archetypes.replaces: Expert Trainer; Greater Banner; 18th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Some cavaliers make a lifelong mission out of their exceptional ability to direct troops on the battlefield, combining tactical insight with a preternatural skill at improving the teamwork of their allies in order to win the day.

archetypes.name: Verdivant
archetypes.replaces: Expert Trainer; Tactician; Banner; Greater Tactician; Greater Banner; Master Tactician; Bonus Feats; Cavalier's Charge
archetypes.aonSummary: Some vine leshys’ spirits are vibrant enough to project this animus beyond their own bodies

archetypes.name: Vermin Tamer
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Expert Trainer; Demanding Challenge
archetypes.aonSummary: Due to the strange terrain, the lack of sunlight, and numerous other hazards, keeping a traditional mount in the Darklands can prove difficult. Cavaliers native to or traveling the region may choose to tame local creatures instead.

archetypes.name: Wave Rider
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Mount
archetypes.aonSummary: Throughout the Inner Sea region, wave riders patrol harbors, keeping them safe from dangerous sea creatures and watching for smugglers. The most famous of these is the hippocampus-riding Sea Cavalry of Absalom.

archetypes.name: Angelfire Apostle
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Spellcasting; Alignment; Channel Energy
