archetypes.aonSummary: Angelfire apostles use the powers of good to avoid violence when possible and cleanse both maladies and evil creatures with blinding flames.

archetypes.name: Appeaser
archetypes.replaces: Aura; Channel Energy; Alignment; Spells; Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: A rare few seek the power of dark forces for brighter ends by focusing on the utilitarian aspects of a god’s portfolio, appeasing their deities through high praise and glorifying their chosen gods’ unaligned aspects.

archetypes.name: Asmodean Advocate
archetypes.replaces: Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: For the faithful of Asmodeus, the words used in a negotiation or contract matter more than their intent.

archetypes.name: Blossoming Light
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Alignment; Channel Energy; Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: Blossoming lights are clerics who take their pursuit of purity and light to extremes.

archetypes.name: Cardinal
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficieny; Spontaneous Casting; Domain; Class Skills; Skill Ranks; Base Attack Bonus
archetypes.aonSummary: Cardinals wield significant political power, engaging in the game of intrigue on behalf of their churches

archetypes.name: Channeler of the Unknown
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Spells; Aura; Channel Energy; Domains; Spontaneous Casting
archetypes.aonSummary: (Ex-cleric archetype) Channelers of the unknown are those faithless clerics who channel the power of an unknown entity or force of the universe

archetypes.name: Cloistered Cleric
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Domains; Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: Cloistered clerics typically live in a temple and rarely interact with the outside world. They are bookish and well learned in the lore of the faith, paying less attention to its magical and martial aspects.

archetypes.name: Crashing Wave
archetypes.replaces: Deity; Bonus Languages; Channel Energy; Spontaneous Casting
archetypes.aonSummary: Clerics who live in or near the sea sometimes embrace the watery aspect of Gozreh over the deity’s other dimensions and take the title of crashing wave; such clerics understand the tempestuousness and cruelty of the sea, but also its generosity and bounty

archetypes.name: Crusader
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: Crusaders serve the militant arm of a church, ready to stand guard over the religion’s holy places and to be its swift, avenging arm against those who resist its truth.

archetypes.name: Demonic Apostle
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: (Drow Only) Demon worship is common among the drow, and so are ranks of demonic apostles, who gain magical insight from their dark lords and crush their chaotic masters’ enemies by channeling demonic energy.

archetypes.name: Divine Paragon
archetypes.replaces: Domain; Aura
archetypes.aonSummary: Divine paragons strive to emulate their god’s ideals as closely as possible.

archetypes.name: Divine Scourge
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Divine scourges take on the role of dealing out unique punishments on behalf of their deities, taking pleasure in carrying out their sacrosanct duties.

archetypes.name: Divine Strategist
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: The divine strategist leads the armies of the faithful, not from the front lines but through her clever strategy and tactical acumen.

archetypes.name: Ecclesitheurge
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Domain; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Eschewing physical armor for protection via the strength of his faith, an ecclesitheurge focuses on the miracles his deity bestows and the breadth of that deity’s dominion.

archetypes.name: Elder Mythos Cultist
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Domains; Channel Energy; Spontaneous Casting; 5th, 11th, and 19th-level Channel Energy increase
archetypes.aonSummary: Typically grasping, secretive, and thoroughly mad, Elder Mythos cultists open their bodies and minds to horrifying realities not meant for the sane as they strive to prepare the world for the eventual return of their alien masters.

archetypes.name: Evangelist
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Channel Energy; Spontaneous Casting
archetypes.aonSummary: The evangelist is the voice of her religion in the world.

archetypes.name: Fiendish Vessel
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: (Tiefling Only) Fiendish vessels, through their fiendish heritage, share an innate connection with their patron, and that connection grants them understanding and power.

archetypes.name: Forgemaster
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: (Dwarf Only) Forgemasters are priestly dwarves who are ritual casters and expert enchanters, able to produce their rune-graven armaments with astonishing speed.

archetypes.name: Foundation of Faith
archetypes.replaces: Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Whether aiding the faithful or defending against the depredations of unbelievers, a foundation of faith is unshakable in her convictions.

archetypes.name: Herald Caller
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Domains; Armor Proficiencies;
archetypes.aonSummary: Unlike warpriests or paladins, who charge headlong into battle in the name of their patron deities, herald callers are adept at calling powerful outsiders to aid their brethren in battle.

archetypes.name: Hidden Priest
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Domain Power, 8th-level Domain Power
archetypes.aonSummary: When practicing their religion is outlawed, the hidden priest learns to hide their true nature and practice magic in secret.

archetypes.name: Idealist
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Idealist clerics are personifications of belief, each embracing the purest ideal of his deity’s realm.

archetypes.name: Iron Priest
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Channel Energy; Spellcasting
archetypes.aonSummary: Iron priests preach of the messengers from beyond the stars, envoys of the divine brought to Golarion in a falling star.

archetypes.name: Lawspeaker
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: Lawspeakers spread their philosophy of certain and unwavering justice throughout the Inner Sea region.

archetypes.name: Mendevian Priest
archetypes.replaces: Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: Crusade-minded clerics of Iomedae, Gorum, and other churches come to Mendev to learn battlefield tactics and the weaknesses of demons.

archetypes.name: Merciful Healer
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: The merciful healer is a master of battlefield revivification, sustaining and restoring allies to keep them in the fight.

archetypes.name: Roaming Exorcist
archetypes.replaces: Skill Ranks; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Domains; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: The roaming exorcist travels far and wide to root out possessions, hauntings, and hidden evils. The roaming exorcist extracts unruly spirits from not only victims of possession, but also haunted sites and accursed items.

archetypes.name: Sacred Attendant
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Channel Energy; Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: Sacred attendants bring out the varied beauty in everyone they help, and they typically worship deities of beauty, love, and sex.

archetypes.name: Scroll Scholar
archetypes.replaces: 1st Level Domain Power, Channel Energy 5th level increase, 4th-level spell slot
archetypes.aonSummary: Those who trade some of their potential to better understand ancient texts and scrolls can become learned scroll scholars.

archetypes.name: Separatist
archetypes.replaces: Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: A radical cleric, unsatisfied with the orthodoxy of her deity’s teachings, forges her own path of defiant divine expression.

archetypes.name: Stoic Caregiver
archetypes.replaces: Channel Energy; Domains;
archetypes.aonSummary: Stoic caregivers are champions of life in defiance of untimely death as well as undeath.

archetypes.name: Theologian
archetypes.replaces: Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: A theologian is an expert on one particular area of her religion

archetypes.name: Triadic Priest
archetypes.replaces: Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: Power comes not just from communion with one’s deity, but also from the formation of divine triumvirates. At the head of these groups are triadic priests.

archetypes.name: Undead Lord
archetypes.replaces: Domains
archetypes.aonSummary: An undead lord is a cleric focused on using necromancy to control undead.

archetypes.name: Varisian Pilgrim
archetypes.replaces: Altered Domain Abilities; Medium Armor/Shield Proficiency; 8th-level Domain Power
archetypes.aonSummary: While most clerics are associated with a particular temple, adventuring clerics spend much of their time away from their favored place of worship, and there are those who worship primarily on the road and during the journey.

archetypes.name: Aerie Protector
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Nature Bond; Wild Empathy; Woodland Stride; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: The aerie protector guards nature’s nests and lairs in the highest mountains, and she is only ever truly at ease when under vast expanses of open sky.

archetypes.name: Ancient Guardian
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiencies; Nature Bond; Wild Empathy; Trackless Step; Woodland Stride; Spontaneous Casting; Resist Nature’s Lure; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Ancient guardians revere nature and draw power from its divine energies, but also protect the customs, histories, and lore of their tribe and race.

archetypes.name: Ape Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: A shaman with this totem calls upon the mighty ape, a peaceful but powerful simian whose strength is beyond compare.

archetypes.name: Aquatic Druid
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Shepherds of the lakes and seas, aquatic druids guard ecosystems ranging from shallows streams to deep ocean trenches, ministering to their residents and communing with the tides.

archetypes.name: Arctic Druid
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: An arctic druid watches over the stark landscape of the far frozen reaches of the world.

archetypes.name: Ashvawg Tamer
archetypes.replaces: Resist Nature's Lure, one less Wild Shape/day, Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Ashvawg Tamers are druids who have chosen to bond with a strange and monstrous creature.

archetypes.name: Bat Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: The bat shaman’s totem is the agile bat, flitting and turning with incredible speed through even the most convoluted mazes.

archetypes.name: Bear Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: A shaman with this focus calls upon the mighty bear, titan of the woodlands and mountains, a paragon of strength and ferocity, and yet also a quiet protector rich in wisdom.

archetypes.name: Blight Druid
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: The devoted servants of nature corrupted, ruined, and destroyed, blight druids are the caretakers of lands ravaged by natural disaster.

archetypes.name: Boar Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: A boar shaman chooses the stolid and ferocious boar as her totem.

archetypes.name: Cave Druid
archetypes.replaces: Nature Sense; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure
archetypes.aonSummary: A few druids seek to preserve the hidden underdark and purge it of the fell horrors that creep up from below.

archetypes.name: Death Druid
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Wild Shape; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids believe that birth and death are the most important parts of the natural cycle.

archetypes.name: Defender of the True World
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Wild Empathy; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids specialize in protecting Golarion from the threat of First World inhabitants.

archetypes.name: Desert Druid
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Desert druids come to the desert to pay homage, protect and maintain the few habitable locales, and witness nature's majesty in all its burning, merciless glory.

archetypes.name: Devolutionist
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Devolutionists believe that the world would be better off without any sentient life at all.

archetypes.name: Dinosaur Druid
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Nature’s Bond; Wild Shape; Resist Nature’s Lure
archetypes.aonSummary: A dinosaur druid speaks for the spirit of prehistoric nature, even taking the form of great beasts of legend.

archetypes.name: Draconic Druid
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Wild Empathy; Woodland Stride; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces; Timeless Body; Nature Sense; Resist Nature's Lure
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids believe that dragons are the ultimate expression of nature and eventually transform into draconic forms.

archetypes.name: Dragon Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; 8th-level Wild Shape; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Your totem is the legendary dragon, fearsome and deadly yet cunning and wise, a creature born of pure magic and raw elemental fury, bound within a shell of fangs, claws, and scales that few dare to challenge.

archetypes.name: Drovier
archetypes.replaces: Nature's Bond; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Droviers view their allies and adventuring companions as a herd or pack to be protected and directed.

archetypes.name: Eagle Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: A shaman with this totem calls upon the noble eagle, stern and proud, soaring high above the world with keen and pitiless eyes that miss nothing.

archetypes.name: Elemental Ally
archetypes.replaces: Nature’s Bond; Wild Shape; Wild Empathy; Resist Nature’s Lure
archetypes.aonSummary: An elemental ally is a druid who has crafted powerful bonds of trust and friendship with one ally from each of the four primary elemental planes.

archetypes.name: Feral Child
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Class Skills; Nature Bond; Trackless Step; A Thousand Faces; Wild Shape; Resist Nature’s Lure; Venom Immunity; Timeless Body
archetypes.aonSummary: (Human Only) Some youths, abandoned in the wilderness and then raised by animals, are so connected with their adoptive home and family that they become feral.

archetypes.name: Feral Shifter
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces; Timeless Body
archetypes.aonSummary: A feral shifter internalizes her communion with and mastery over animals. Instead of forming a bond with an animal companion or an aspect of nature, she alters her own essence or being as homage to the noble creatures of the wild.

archetypes.name: Feyspeaker
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Wild Shape; Nature Sense; Base Attack Bonus; Class Skills; Skill Ranks; Armor Proficiency
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids hear the whispers of the natural world like fey creatures do, and learn to mimic those tantalizing murmurs in order to influence the minds of both wild beasts and civilized people.

archetypes.name: Fungal Pilgrim
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Wild Shape; Timeless Body
archetypes.aonSummary: Fungal pilgrims are druids seeking transformation into a more plantlike existence.

archetypes.name: Goliath Druid
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Nature Sense; Nature Bond; Wild Empathy; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Goliath druids hone their spiritual and magical connections to nature’s largest creatures, especially dinosaurs, giants, and megafauna, revering these massive creatures as living relics of a primeval time when all creatures were more in harmony with nature.

archetypes.name: Green Faith Initiate
archetypes.replaces: Trackless Step; 6th, 10th-level use of Wild Shape; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Druids who are initiated into the magic of nature as strict students of the Green Faith’s traditions sometimes demonstrate abilities unique to their organization.

archetypes.name: Green Scourge
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Nature Sense; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure
archetypes.aonSummary: Green scourges are militant druids sworn to restore natural order.

archetypes.name: Halcyon Druid
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Nature Sense; Class Skills; Wild Empathy; Spontaneous Casting; Wild Shape; Resist Nature's Lure; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Though they revere the natural world, halcyon druids are less focused on emulating its inhabitants. Instead, like Old-Mage Jatembe, they treat with beings from the Outer Sphere.

archetypes.name: Jungle Druid
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: The jungle druid waches over the fecund jungles of the equatorial regions, rich in life and ancient tradition.

archetypes.name: Kraken Caller
archetypes.replaces: Bonus Language; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids draw upon power irreverently stolen from one of the most dangerous creatures of the depths: the kraken.

archetypes.name: Leshy Warden
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Wild Empathy; Spontaneous Casting; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: The natural world is full of bodiless nature spirits connected to the forces of glades, springs, and individual plants. Some druids hear their call keenly and are able to effortlessly incarnate them as the miniature creatures known as leshys.

archetypes.name: Life Channeler
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Nature Bond; Wild Shape; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: By sacrificing the life of a sentient creature, life channelers can generate energy that guarantees fertility and prosperity for lower creatures like plants and animals.

archetypes.name: Lion Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: A shaman with this totem calls upon the proud lion, imposing and majestic, the mighty leader of deadly hunters.

archetypes.name: Mantella
archetypes.replaces: Wild Shape; Venom Immunity; Spontaneous Casting
archetypes.aonSummary: (Grippli) A mantella focuses on exploring her poisonous heritage, whether or not it has manifested in her own personal biology.

archetypes.name: Menhir Savant
archetypes.replaces: Nature Sense; Wild Empathy; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids study the paths of nature’s power through the nodes and ley lines that connect standing stones and megalithic circles, learning to tap into their energies.

archetypes.name: Mooncaller
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: A mooncaller is bound to the subtle influences of the ever-changing moon and its endless cycles from light to dark and back again.

archetypes.name: Mountain Druid
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: As more and more of the soft, easy lands become cultivated and civilized, many druids look for refuge and solitude among the eternal peaks of the highest mountains.

archetypes.name: Naga Aspirant
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces; Timeless Body
archetypes.aonSummary: (Nagaji Only) The naga aspirant follows the ancient beliefs and engages in the rituals of a druidic sect dedicated to the transcendence of her nagaji form through absolute devotion to nagas and naga gods.

archetypes.name: Nature Fang
archetypes.replaces: Nature Sense; Wild Empathy; Woodland Stride; Wild Shape; Resist Nature’s Lure; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: A nature fang is a druid who stalks and slays those who despoil nature, kill scarce animals, or introduce diseases to unprotected habitats.

archetypes.name: Nature Priest
archetypes.replaces: Deity; Class Skills; Weapon Proficiencies; Nature Sense; Nature Bond; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Nature priests serve two masters: their deities and nature itself, and can call upon the power of both to fuel their divine abilities.

archetypes.name: Nithveil Adept
archetypes.replaces: Nature Sense; Nature Bond; Spontaneous Casting; Resist Nature's Lure
archetypes.aonSummary: Nithveil adepts learn the secret magic of the First World fey in the moving, reality-phasing city of Nithveil

archetypes.name: Pack Lord
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; 6th-level Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids bond with many animal companions rather than just one, achieving a level of communion rare even in druidic circles and leading their pack brothers and pack sisters with total authority.

archetypes.name: Plains Druid
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Out upon the wide and rolling prairies and savannahs, plains druids stand guard over the grasslands.

archetypes.name: Planar Extremist
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Spells; Nature's Bond; Spontaneous Casting; Resist Nature's Lure; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: (Ex-druid archetype) Planar extremists are those druids that have lost their neutral stance and find themselves gravitating toward one of the four most extreme alignments

archetypes.name: Progenitor
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Nature Bond; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Progenitors are druids who tap into the vibrant power of the First World to propagate natural and supernatural wonders.

archetypes.name: Reincarnated Druid
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; Timeless Body
archetypes.aonSummary: Spun off into the endless circle of life, an incarnate druid is an embodiment of nature’s eternal renewal.

archetypes.name: Restorer
archetypes.replaces: Nature Sense; Spontanteous Casting; Resist Nature's Lore; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Restorers carefully tend to the health of both the environment and creatures in it.

archetypes.name: River Druid
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Nature Sense; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape; Timeless Body
archetypes.aonSummary: These druids are the guardians of rivers and the creatures that depend on them.

archetypes.name: Road Keeper
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Nature Bond; Wild Empathy; Woodland Stride; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Guardians of the lonely paths between cities, road keepers protect the wild from travelers, and travelers from the wild.

archetypes.name: Rot Warden
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Nature Bond; Wild Empathy; Trackless Step; Venom Immunity; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Harbingers of decay, rot wardens live in damp lands where insects and rot break down the dead to feed the living.

archetypes.name: Saurian Shaman
archetypes.replaces: Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: A shaman with this focus calls upon the primeval dinosaur, the archaic terror that lingers as a hungering, atavistic stranger at the fringes of the ecosystem, a destroyer and despoiler whose coming other animals dread.

archetypes.name: Season Keeper
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Trackless Step; Venom Immunity; Timeless Body; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: (Triaxian Only) Imbued with the primeval potency of their planet’s seasons, those druids known as season keepers guide Triaxian communities through the stark transition from summer to winter (and vice versa).

archetypes.name: Season Sage
archetypes.replaces: Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: (Gathlain) Season sages wander as the seasons change, turning the leaves and transforming nature as they pass and taking pleasure in the transition between seasons.

archetypes.name: Serpent Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: A shaman with this totem calls upon the cunning serpent, the stealthy deceiver who draws the weak minded in and strikes while they are unaware.

archetypes.name: Shark Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids emulate the deadly shark, a remorseless hunter that marine dwellers dread.

archetypes.name: Skinshaper
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Wild Shape; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Using the same primal energy with which other druids assume animal forms, skinshapers can imitate some of the most dangerous beasts of all: humans and other humanoids.

archetypes.name: Sky Druid
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Nature Bond; Woodland Stride; Resist Nature’s Lure; Trackless Step; Wild Shape; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: (Sylph Only) Some druids develop ties not to a particular landscape, but instead to the endless blue expanse of the skies.

archetypes.name: Storm Druid
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: While most druids focus their attention upon the rich earth and the bounty of nature that springs forth from it, the storm druid’s eyes have ever been cast to the skies and the endless expanse of blue, channeling the most raw and untamed aspects of nature.

archetypes.name: Sunrider
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Nature Bond; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Sunriders help their allies, be they fellow tribe members or fellow adventurers, to survive in harsh desert terrain, while simultaneously making it even harsher for their foes.

archetypes.name: Supernaturalist
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Nature Bond; Wild Empathy; Nature Sense; Trackless Step; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Supernaturalists wholly embrace paranormal phenomena as extensions of nature.

archetypes.name: Survivor
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Spellcasting; Nature Bond; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: The survivor embodies the neutral aspect of the natural world and eschews druidic magic in favor of more pragmatic and worldly survival methods.

archetypes.name: Swamp Druid
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; A Thousand Faces
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids eschew pleasant glades and groves and instead seek out dank marshes, misty bogs and heaths, and trackless swamps as the place they call home and watch over with care, finding beauty and life in abundance in places few others would willingly enter.

archetypes.name: Swarm Monger
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Woodland Stride; Nature Sense; Resist Nature's Lure; 12th-level Wild Shape options
archetypes.aonSummary: Whereas other druids commune with nature or even the spirit of a city, swarm mongers find beauty and strength in decay, and they draw their power from fungus, disease, and their own singular will to survive.

archetypes.name: Tempest Druid
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Nature Bond; Nature Sense; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: Some druids have come to worship the Eye of Abendego as an aspect of pure elemental fury, channeling its mysteries into their own magic

archetypes.name: Tempest Tamer
archetypes.replaces: Bonus Languages; Resist Nature's Lure; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary:
Tempest Tamer
Source Blood of the Sea pg. 25
Druids draw upon the fiercest powers of nature, and tsunamis, typhoons, and whirlpools are among the most powerful forces in the ocean.

archetypes.name: Toxicologist
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Wild Empathy; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Toxicologists specialize in the stealthy application of insidious poisons to their targets, believing word of their foes’ horrifying deaths will deter others from attempting similar desecrations of the natural world.

archetypes.name: Treesinger
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Wild Empathy; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: (Elf and Vine Leshy Only) Some elves turn to the timeless growth of nature for solace, finding allies among the great trees themselves, and even leading the forest’s plants into combat.

archetypes.name: Troll Fury
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Resist Nature’s Lure; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: (Troll Only) Troll furies combine a druid’s love of natural balance with a single-minded devotion to the welfare of the troll tribe.

archetypes.name: Undine Adept
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: (Undine Only) An undine adept dedicates herself to preserving the knowledge of the first undines and ensuring her people’s ancient connections to the natural world remain undisturbed.

archetypes.name: Urban Druid
archetypes.replaces: Spontaneous Casting; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature's Lure; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: While many druids keep to the wilderness, some make their way within settlements, communing with the animals and vermin who live there and speaking for the nature that runs rampant in civilization's very cradle.

archetypes.name: Urushiol
archetypes.replaces: Nature Bond; Resist Nature's Lure
archetypes.aonSummary: When an urushiol druid forms a bond with nature, it takes a vastly different form than for most druids. His body becomes increasingly toxic, allowing him to secrete a deadly poison through his pores.

archetypes.name: Wild Whisperer
archetypes.replaces: Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Resist Nature’s Lure; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: A wild whisperer is an expert at studying, predicting, and explaining animal behavior.

archetypes.name: Wolf Shaman
archetypes.replaces: A Thousand Faces; Venom Immunity
archetypes.aonSummary: A shaman with this totem calls upon the clever wolf, capable of roaming alone yet wise enough to run with a pack when facing dangers too great for one alone.

archetypes.name: World Walker
archetypes.replaces: Trackless Step; Resist Nature’s Lure; Venom Immunity; Timeless Body
archetypes.aonSummary: While all druids traverse the wilderness with ease, the world walkers take it upon themselves to travel the entire world.

archetypes.name: Aerial Assaulter
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bravery; 2nd, 12th-level Bonus Feat, Armor Mastery, Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Aerial assaulters leap to great heights and create higher ground where there is none.

archetypes.name: Airborne Ambusher
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Class Skills; Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: (Strix Only) Driven by suspicion and hatred, strix doggedly guard their territories, making deadly use of their flight.

archetypes.name: Aldori Defender
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training; 6th, 8th, 10th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Trained warrior in the art of the Aldori dueling sword.

archetypes.name: Aquanaut
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Armor Mastery; Weapon Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: Aquanaut fighters master the movement of water, using its flow to their advantage in combat.

archetypes.name: Archer
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The archer is dedicated to the careful mastery of the bow, perfecting his skills with years of practice.

archetypes.name: Armiger
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Skill Points; 1st, 10th-level Bonus Feats; Bravery
archetypes.aonSummary: Fighters who focus their training to become Hellknights.

archetypes.name: Armor Master
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: While many fighters hone their weapon skills to a point of inescapable grace and lethality, there are those who live under the maxim that a good offense can be accomplished though an impenetrable defense.

archetypes.name: Brawler
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery, Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: All melee is up close and personal, but some warriors bring it as close as they can get.

archetypes.name: Cad
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: In combat, most fighters have some sort of code of honor. Some believe that one should not kick enemies when they are down, or should limit use of other such dirty tricks to the most dire of circumstances. The cad places no such limitations on himself.

archetypes.name: Calistrian Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Class Skills; Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Like a bounty hunter following his own rules, a Calistrian hunter tracks down elusive prey using his wits and delivers long-overdue retribution while easily ignoring his own injuries thanks to the joy he receives from a job well done.

archetypes.name: Cavern Sniper
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 1st, 4th-level Fighter Bonus Feats; Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: (Drow Only) Perfectly at home in the darkness, the cavern sniper capitalizes on stealth and ranged attacks imbued with his spell-like abilities to harass his opponents.

archetypes.name: Child of Acavna and Amaznen
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Skills; 1st, 2nd, 8th, 12th, 16th, and 20th-level Combat Feats; Armor Training; Weapon Training
archetypes.aonSummary: The child of Acavna and Amaznen has trained in the nearly forgotten arts of Azlant passed down by Aroden, which combine martial prowess with elementary wizardry. Inspired by the deities Aroden once worshiped long ago, children of Acavna and Amaznen strive to understand the dangers of the world and overcome them with knowledge and strength of arms.

archetypes.name: Corsair
archetypes.replaces: 2nd-level Bonus Feat; Armor Training; 6th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: A corsair is a pirate who focuses on shipboard combat, relying on his strength of arms over his agility.

archetypes.name: Crossbowman
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The crossbowman has perfected the deadly use of the crossbow, a simple but cruelly efficient weapon, as a craftsman mastering a lethal tool.

archetypes.name: Cyber-Soldier
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Training 1; Armor Training 2 and 4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Cyber-soldiers replace fallible flesh with precisioncrafted machinery.

archetypes.name: Dirty Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: (Orc Only) The dirty fighter laughs at concepts like honor and fair play. He cares only for victory, no matter how he achieves it, and spends as much time mastering sneaky combat maneuvers as he does drilling with weapons or learning how to wear armor.

archetypes.name: Dragonheir Scion
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 1st, 3rd, 5th-level Bonus Feats; Bravery; Armor Training; Armor Mastery; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Dragonheir scions are the martially inclined humanoid descendants of those influenced by draconic power.

archetypes.name: Dragoon
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; 1st-level Bonus Feat; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Training 2-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: These gallant lancers serve in the vanguard of many armies or as knights-errant.

archetypes.name: Drill Sergeant
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: Drill sergeants excel at training other combatants in fighting techniques.

archetypes.name: Druman Blackjacket
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th-level Bonus Feats;
archetypes.aonSummary: Known as the Blackjackets, the elite soldiers of Druma are and always have been mercenaries rather than a standing army.

archetypes.name: Eldritch Guardian
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 1st and 2nd-level Bonus Feats; Bravery
archetypes.aonSummary: Eldritch guardians are trained to detect and give warning about magic threats to the people and places they protect.

archetypes.name: Foehammer
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 2-4; Armor Mastery; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: (Dwarf Only) While the axe is the most famous dwarven weapon, the hammer is at the heart of dwarves’ heritage as forgemasters and warriors alike.

archetypes.name: Free Hand Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The free hand fighter specializes in the delicate art of handling a single weapon in one hand while using his free hand to balance, block, tip, and distract his opponents.

archetypes.name: Gladiator
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Bravery
archetypes.aonSummary: The gladiator is both a cunning warrior and a consummate performer, knowing life and death are balanced not only on a sword’s edge, but also on the cheers or jeers of the crowd.

archetypes.name: Gloomblade
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Armor Proficiencies; Armor Training; Weapon Training
archetypes.aonSummary: The Shadow Plane’s substance is legendary for its versatility. In shadow-shrouded lands, secretive martial practitioners long ago learned to shape supernatural weapons from ribbons of pure darkness.

archetypes.name: High Guardian
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 1st, 2nd, 4th-level Bonus Feats; Bravery
archetypes.aonSummary: High guardians epitomize personal devotion, serving as the shield that protects his lord from the myriad dangers around every corner.

archetypes.name: Lore Warden
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiencies; Bravery; 2nd-level Bonus Feat; Armor Training; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Lore wardens are fighters who benefit from learning to outsmart and outmaneuver their foes rather than just overpower them.

archetypes.name: Lore Warden (PFS Field Guide)
archetypes.replaces: Medium Armor, Heavy Armor, and Shield Proficiency; Bravery 1; Armor Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Lore wardens are fighters who benefit from learning to outsmart and outmaneuver their foes rather than just overpower them.

archetypes.name: Martial Master
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Training; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: There are those who learn the fighting arts though countless hours of repetition and training, while others seem to pick up new stances and forms as if they were born to them.

archetypes.name: Mobile Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Training 3-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Where some fighters focus on strength and raw power, the mobile fighter relies on swiftness and mobility, gliding across the battlefield like a steel whirlwind and leaving destruction in his wake.

archetypes.name: Molthuni Defender
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training
archetypes.aonSummary: Taking advantage of their weighty armor, Molthuni defenders can hold back an onslaught of enemies intent on breaking through their line.

archetypes.name: Mutation Warrior
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: While most fighters rely on physical fitness and rigorous training to achieve martial superiority, a few prefer to create and imbibe dangerous concoctions that mutate them into fearsome creatures.

archetypes.name: Opportunist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skils; Bravery; 1st, 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, 20th-level Bonus Feat; Weapon Training 1
archetypes.aonSummary: Opportunists believe every battle is one of wits rather than arms.

archetypes.name: Pack Mule
archetypes.replaces: Skill Ranks; 1st-level Bonus Feat; Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Pack mules carry heavy loads with ease and small packages with discretion.

archetypes.name: Phalanx Soldier
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The phalanx soldier specializes in defensive tactics, using his shield to guard himself and his allies and forming a shield wall like an unbreakable anvil against which his enemies break.

archetypes.name: Polearm Master
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The polearm master is schooled in the ancient wisdom that enemies are best faced at the end of long striking pole.

archetypes.name: Qadira: Dawnflower Dervish
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: Spinning warrior dervish of Sarenrae, wielding a scimitar with devastating consequences.

archetypes.name: Relic Master
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Armor Training; Weapon Training; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Commonly trained in the well-funded temples of Osirion or Qadira, the relic master is skilled in magic item mastery.

archetypes.name: Roughrider
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Roughriders study and practice the fine points of mounted combat, drilling endlessly with warbeasts—from noble thoroughbreds to trained monsters—to form a perfect synergy between rider and steed.

archetypes.name: Savage Warrior
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Warriors' might is not measured only by their skill with steel, but also by their ability to inflict death with fang and claw, horn and hoof, and every exotic appendage the natural and unnatural world has to offer.

archetypes.name: Scrapper
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training; Weapon Training 1
archetypes.aonSummary: Scrappers are adept at collecting the leftovers from their enemy’s armor and using these scraps to improve their own armor.

archetypes.name: Seasoned Commander
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiencies; Skill Ranks per Level; Class Skills; 1st-level Bonus Feat; Armor Training 1, 3, 4; Weapon Training
archetypes.aonSummary: The seasoned commander excels at leading troops through inspiration and the use of unit tactics.

archetypes.name: Sensate
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 2-4; Armor Mastery; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: A sensate perceives battle through senses beyond mortal ken, anticipating his opponents’ movements before they even begin to act.

archetypes.name: Shielded Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: A shielded fighter focuses on both offense and defense, blending weapon and shield in perfect balance to impede his enemies while delivering deadly blows, and even turning the shield itself into a formidable weapon.

archetypes.name: Siegebreaker
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 2nd, 4th, and 8th-level Bonus Feats; Bravery; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The siegebreaker is trained to break through lines of enemy soldiers.

archetypes.name: Skirmisher
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiencies; Class Skills; Skill Ranks; 2nd-level Bonus Feat; Bravery; Armor Training; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Not all battles are fought between armies; sometimes, a settlement or nation faces a threat too dire to fight in the open. In order to repel a much larger enemy force, some soldiers must abandon equipment and tactics designed for open-field warfare and instead rely on ambushes, hit-andrun tactics, and sabotage to whittle down their enemies’ strength and morale.

archetypes.name: Spear Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Armor Proficiencies; Bravery; Armor Training; Armor Mastery; Weapon Training; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: One of the oldest spear-fighting styles originates in Vudra, where many martial arts traditions consider the spear to be the ultimate weapon.

archetypes.name: Steelbound Fighter
archetypes.replaces: 1st level Bonus Feat; Weapon Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: A fighter who has impressive martial resolve and technique with a specific weapon as the result of a powerful relationship a similar weapon had with one of his ancestors.

archetypes.name: Swarm Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; 1st, 2nd, 6th, 10th, 14th, 18th-level Bonus Feats; Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: (Kobold Only) Scuttling between the legs of friend and foe alike, the swarm fighter is an unshakable combatant.

archetypes.name: Tactician
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; 1st-level Bonus Feat; Bravery; Weapon Training 1; Armor Training 3, 4
archetypes.aonSummary: While many fighters focus on the fundamentals of melee and ranged combat, there are those who are trained to view the bigger picture on the battlefield.

archetypes.name: Taldor: Rondelero Duelist
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-3, Bravery, Weapon Training 1
archetypes.aonSummary: One who has perfected the art of rondelero, fighting with falcata and buckler.

archetypes.name: Thunderstriker
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 3-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The thunderstriker adopts an unusual fighting style, gripping a heavy weapon with both hands and switching to a defensive posture with weapon and buckler, lashing out with the shield with surprising speed and power.

archetypes.name: Titan Fighter
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Bonus Feat; Armor Training; Weapon Training
archetypes.aonSummary: Titan fighters make use of enormous weapons others can barely lift.

archetypes.name: Tower Shield Specialist
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Many fighters believe the tower shield is a tool suitable only for troops on the battlefield, claiming it is too large and bulky to use in skirmishes or within dungeon corridors.

archetypes.name: Trench Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: Advances in technology have made archaic armors obsolete by the twentieth century, and modern soldiers concentrate training on firearms and swift feet.

archetypes.name: Tribal Fighter
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Bonus Feat; Weapon Training
archetypes.aonSummary: A tribal fighter knows that it is not the weapon that matters but the hand that wields it. Instead of encasing himself in metal armor like the soldiers fighting and dying for the socalled civilized lands do, he prefers to wear something he or his ancestors have killed.

archetypes.name: Two-Handed Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Some fighters focus their efforts on finding the biggest, heaviest, most imposing weapon they can find and training to manage and harness the weight of their massive weapons for maximum impact.

archetypes.name: Two-Weapon Warrior
archetypes.replaces: Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Trained under great masters who preached the simple truth that two are better than one when it comes to weapons, the two-weapon warrior is a terror when his hands are full.

archetypes.name: Unarmed Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; 1st-level Bonus Feat; Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; 8th, 12th-level Bonus Feat; Armor Mastery; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The unarmed fighter picks up a weapon only rarely, and when he does, he prefers the weapons of the monk.

archetypes.name: Unbreakable
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; 1st-level Bonus Feat; Bravery; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Training 3-4; Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: The unbreakable is a warrior of indomitable will, unstoppable and implacable once he has set his mind upon a course of action.

archetypes.name: Ustalavic Duelist
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; 1st-level Bonus Feat; Weapon Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: The University of Lepidstadt has developed a reputation for churning out fearsome duelists. At the end of each academic year, the students all gather together and duel one another with light blades. Each student duels one opponent after another until he is marked on the cheek by an adversary’s blade. These “Lepidstadt scars” are recognized throughout the Inner Sea region and beyond as marks of their prowess. The Lepidstadt Style is one of fluid motion and precise thrusts.

archetypes.name: Varisian Free-Style Fighter
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 1st, 6th, 10th, and 12th-level Bonus Feats; Weapon Training; Weapon Mastery; Armor Training
archetypes.aonSummary: Free-style fighters are most common in Varisia, where their training—students’ traveling study with multiple teachers, or perhaps instruction in the anything-goes mentality of the Price of Freedom school in Kaer Maga—allows them to blend fighting styles into a greater whole.

archetypes.name: Venomblade
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 6th, 12th-level Bonus Feat; Bravery
archetypes.aonSummary: (Nagaji) The venomblade has learned to take full advantage of his toxic spittle, blinding his targets and then rushing in to cut them down where they stand.

archetypes.name: Viking
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Bravery; Armor Training; Weapon Training; Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Vikings seek to raid “softer societies” and return with their longships filled with plunder. A viking strikes fear into the heart of her foes, and in battle she can fly into a terrible rage.

archetypes.name: Warlord
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Armor Training; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Honorable, fearless experts in gun and blade, warlords eschew armor as impractical to their harsh and often desert-like environment

archetypes.name: Weapon Bearer Squire
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Bonus Feat; 2nd-level Bonus Feat; Armor Training 1
archetypes.aonSummary: The weapon bearer squire ensures her knight is equipped for any task.

archetypes.name: Weapon Master
archetypes.replaces: Bravery; Armor Training 1-4; Weapon Training 1-4; Armor Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Devoted to the perfection of a single weapon, the weapon master's meditations upon his favored weapon border on the obsessive, but none can deny his consummate skill.

archetypes.name: Black Powder Vaulter
archetypes.replaces: Deadeye; Gunslinger's Dodge; Gunslinger Initiative; Startling Shot; Expert Loading
archetypes.aonSummary: Black powder vaulters like to get into the thick of the battle, maneuvering among the fray to find the most advantageous positions from which to kill their enemies.

archetypes.name: Blatherskite
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Gunslinger's Dodge; Gunslinger Initiative; Pistol-Whip; Startling Shot
archetypes.aonSummary: The blatherskate has an extraordinary talent for retreating from harm’s way and fooling his enemies into thinking he is weaker than he is.

archetypes.name: Bolt Ace
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiencies; Gunsmith; Grit; Deadeye; Quick Clear; Utility Shot; Startling Shot; Expert Loading; Lightning Reload; Menacing Shot; Gun Training
archetypes.aonSummary: While gunslingers are full of sound and fury, there is a class of gunslingers that never soil their hands with powder or feel the sting of gun smoke.

archetypes.name: Buccaneer
archetypes.replaces: Quick Clear Deed; Pistol Whip Deed; Dead Shot Deed; Lightning Reload Deed; Grit; Nimble; Gun Training 1,2, and 4
archetypes.aonSummary: (Human Only) Freebooters who cling to the convoluted codes that rule independent ships, the buccaneer is a gunslinger of the high seas.

archetypes.name: Bushwhacker
archetypes.replaces: Grit; Utility Shot Deed; Targeting Deed; 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th, 20th-level Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: (Kobold Only) The bushwhacker specializes in the art of the ambush. For her, gunplay works best when it comes from a concealed position and is directed against a target that falls with the very first volley and is dead before the smoke clears.

archetypes.name: Commando
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Utility Shot; Expert Loading; Lightning Reload; Slinger's Luck; 4th-level Bonus Feat; Gun Training
archetypes.aonSummary: Commandos are those rough and ready gunslingers who excel at hit-and-run tactics and leveraging their expertise in the wild against their enemies.

archetypes.name: Experimental Gunsmith
archetypes.replaces: Gunsmith; Gunsmithing; Gun Training
archetypes.aonSummary: (Gnome Only) The experimental gunsmith is obsessed with creating the ultimate firearm, and is willing to take risks to work the kinks out of her design.

archetypes.name: Firebrand
archetypes.replaces: Gunsmith; Grit; Deadeye; Dead Shot; Bonus Feats; Gun Training
archetypes.aonSummary: Where other gunslingers rely on precision shooting, the firebrand instead masters explosive ordnance.

archetypes.name: Graveslinger
archetypes.replaces: Deadeye; Startling Shot; Bleeding Wound; Menacing Shot; 4th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Graveslingers craft signature bullets to hunt down wandering undead. With this infused ammunition, they can take on the most resilient spectral foes with ease.

archetypes.name: Gulch Gunner
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Grit; Deadeye Deed; Pistol Whip Deed; Menacing Shot Deed; 9th, 13th, 17th-level Gun Training
archetypes.aonSummary: (Ratfolk Only) These gulch gunners often specialize in proficiency with a single pistol (easily handled in tight spaces) and wander from warren to warren selling their tunnel-shooting skills to the highest bidder.

archetypes.name: Gun Scavenger
archetypes.replaces: Gunsmith; Quick Clear Deed; Targeting Deed; Nimble
archetypes.aonSummary: A gun scavenger collects scraps, spare parts, and other components that might—if modified properly—give her firearm an extra edge.

archetypes.name: Gun Tank
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Gunslinger’s Dodge Deed; Evasive Deed; Nimble; Bonus Feats (4th level and every 4 levels after)
archetypes.aonSummary: Gunslingers usually don’t use heavy armor, but there are a few who use and modify their armor to protect themselves from both traditional weapons and gunfire.

archetypes.name: Gunner Squire
archetypes.replaces: Gunslinger's Dodge; Gunslinger Initiative; Nimble +1
archetypes.aonSummary: The gunner squire is prepared to reload or repair her lord's firearms at a moment's notice.

archetypes.name: Maverick
archetypes.replaces: Dodge; Pistol Whip; Gunslinger Initiative
archetypes.aonSummary: Quick with her gun and no stranger to barroom brawls, a maverick can hold her own when bullets and punches start flying.

archetypes.name: Musket Master
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiency; Gunsmith; Gunslinger’s Dodge Deed; Utility Shot Deed; Gun Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: Some gunslingers want a little more firepower and range. These are the musket masters; the best of these gunslingers can reload a musket with dazzling speed, potentially putting even their pistol-wielding brethren to shame.

archetypes.name: Mysterious Stranger
archetypes.replaces: Grit; Quick Clear Deed; Nimble; Gun Training 1
archetypes.aonSummary: A few rare gunslingers seem to accomplish their chosen tasks purely through willpower and an unwillingness to ever give up.

archetypes.name: Pistolero
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiency; Gunsmith; Deadeye Deed; Startling Shot Deed; Menacing Shot Deed; Gun Training 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: While most gunslingers have favorite firearms, there are those rare ones who choose to specialize in one-handed firearms exclusively.

archetypes.name: Planar Rifter
archetypes.replaces: Grit; Deadeye; Dead Shot; Menacing Shot; Death's Shot; Nimble; Gun Training
archetypes.aonSummary: Planar rifters harvest pieces of the Outer Planes, absorbing some of the energy into themselves and condensing other portions of it into bullets they can fire from their guns

archetypes.name: Scatter Gunner
archetypes.replaces: Gunsmith; Deadeye; Utility Shot; Dead Shot; Targeting
archetypes.aonSummary: Punishing firearms such as the blunderbuss and dragon pistol can lay waste to invaders in tight corridors, and the dwarves of Dongun Hold have pioneered masterful methods for making the most of these indiscriminate weapons

archetypes.name: Siege Gunner
archetypes.replaces: Grit; Nimble; Deadeye; Gunslinger Initiative; Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: The Grand Duchy of Alkenstar has spawned all manner of firearm specialists, wielding small and large firearms alike. Siege gunners specialize in the very largest— cannons, bombards, and firedrakes.

archetypes.name: Techslinger
archetypes.replaces: Deadeye; Quick Clear; Expert Loading; Gun Training
archetypes.aonSummary: Techslingers spurn unreliable gunpowder weapons in favor of high-tech armaments.

archetypes.name: Thronewarden
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Nimble; 4th-level Bonus Feat; Startling Shot; Bleeding Wound
archetypes.aonSummary: As vigilant sentinels, thronewardens identify and head off trouble.

archetypes.name: Wyrm Sniper
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Starling Shot Deed; Lightning Reload Deed; Menacing Shot Deed
archetypes.aonSummary: These long-shot artists are masters at taking down dragons with sharp shooting and light siege weaponry.

archetypes.name: Aquatic Beastmaster
archetypes.replaces: Animal Focus; Wild Empathy; Improved Empathic Link
archetypes.aonSummary: Hunters beneath the sea are just as committed as their surface-dwelling counterparts to working alongside their animal companions to eradicate threats.

archetypes.name: Chameleon Adept
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Teamwork Feats; Hunter’s Tactics; Wild Empathy; Precise Companion; Woodland Stride; Raise Animal Companion; One with the Wild
archetypes.aonSummary: Some hunters are masters of blending into every situation, even making their companions appear humanoid for brief periods of time.

archetypes.name: Colluding Scoundrel
archetypes.replaces: Animal Focus; Second Animal Focus; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: The colluding scoundrel is a canny and conniving skirmisher, manipulating her enemies and leveraging her allies for her own benefit.

archetypes.name: Courtly Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Animal Companion; Animal Focus; Precise Companion; Hunter Tactics; Teamwork Feats; Bonus Tricks
archetypes.aonSummary: While most hunters find themselves at ease in the wildest parts of the world, courtly hunters instead make their homes in cultured urban environments.

archetypes.name: Divine Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Class Skills; Teamwork Feats; Hunter Tactics
archetypes.aonSummary: While most hunters heed the call of nature and fight to protect its bounty, some are inspired to serve a higher power.

archetypes.name: Feral Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Animal Companion; Animal Focus; Hunter Tactics; Speak with Master; Precise Companion; Bonus Tricks; Improved Empathic Link; Greater Empathic Link; Master of the Wild; Raise Animal Companion; 6th, 9th, 12th, 15th, and 18th-level Teamwork Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: A feral hunter has forged a bond with nature that’s so strong that she doesn’t merely channel the aspects of animals— she actually becomes an animal herself.

archetypes.name: Feykiller
archetypes.replaces: Animal Focus; Wild Empathy; Speak with Master; Improed Empathic Link; One with the Wild
archetypes.aonSummary: Some hunters in fey-plagued regions are dedicated to tracking down and eradicating these threats.

archetypes.name: Flood Flourisher
archetypes.replaces: Hunter Tactics; Woodland Stride; Teamwork Feats; Swift Tracker
archetypes.aonSummary: Well adapted to their drenched surroundings, flood flourishers coordinate deadly ambushes with their loyal animal companions by capitalizing on their mastery of the soggy terrain.

archetypes.name: Forester
archetypes.replaces: Animal Focus; Animal Companion; Precise Companion; Hunter Tactics; Improved Empathic Link; Bonus Tricks; Raise Animal Companion; Speak with Master; Greater Empathic Link
archetypes.aonSummary: While all hunters have a bond with the natural world, a forester has a stronger tie to her environment than to the animals within it.

archetypes.name: Packmaster
archetypes.replaces: Animal Companion; Animal Focus; Teamwork Feats; Second Animal Focus; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Some hunters form bonds with packs of well-trained creatures. Whether such a hunter is a northern berserker running with a pack of timber wolves or a savage warrior dashing through the jungle alongside her herd of dimetrodons, the packmaster revels in the thrill of the hunt and the glory of the kill.

archetypes.name: Patient Ambusher
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Nature Training; Wild Empathy; Hunter Tactics; Teamwork Feats; Raise Animal Companion
archetypes.aonSummary: Wandering the wilds, some hunters eschew the bond of innate teamwork with their animal companions. Instead, these hunters master the creation and deployment of intricate ranger traps, often using themselves or their animal companions to lure foes into their snares.

archetypes.name: Pelagic Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Animal Companion; Animal Focus; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: Pelagic hunters form strong bonds that extend deep beneath the sea.

archetypes.name: Plant Master
archetypes.replaces: Animal Companion; Animal Focus; Wild Empathy; One with the Wild; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Some hunters form a bond with plant life instead of an animal and take on those aspects instead.

archetypes.name: Primal Companion Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Animal Focus; Second Animal Focus; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Most hunters are skilled at awakening the primal beasts inside themselves. However, some can instead activate the primal essence within their animal companion.

archetypes.name: Roof Runner
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Armor Proficieny; Track; Woodland Stride; Swift Tracker; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Roof runners are skilled ambushers, skirmishers, and spies who eschew heavier types of armor in order to remain light on their feet.

archetypes.name: Scarab Stalker
archetypes.replaces: Animal Focus; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: The forgotten ruins in the desert sands have given rise to a breed of hunters who call upon the powers of the pyramids to protect and explore the ancient sites of their people.

archetypes.name: Totem-Bonded
archetypes.replaces: Animal Companion; Animal Focus
archetypes.aonSummary: Totem-bonded are hunters who are able to form a true spiritual bond with the powerful fauna that dominate the wildlands.

archetypes.name: Treestrider
archetypes.replaces: Animal Companion; Animal Focus; Second Animal Focus; Precise Companion; Raise Animal Companion
archetypes.aonSummary: Some hunters are masters of the wild. Whether raised by apes or having some other link with simian creatures, these hunters glide through the wilderness with ease.

archetypes.name: Uprooter Scout
archetypes.replaces: Improved Empathic Link; Speak with Master; Greater Empathic Link; Raise Animal Companion; One with the Wild
archetypes.aonSummary: The Uprooters are an elite band of Kyonin elves skilled and brave enough to foray into the Tanglebriar and take the offensive in the fight against Treerazer.

archetypes.name: Urban Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Animal Companion; Hunter Tactics; Teamwork Feat; Woodland Stride; One with the Wild
archetypes.aonSummary: Urban hunters help guards track down and apprehend criminals or spies, find lost children and disaster victims, and protect animals from abuse in the city.

archetypes.name: Verminous Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Animal Companion; Wild Empathy; Animal Focus; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: A verminous hunter calls on the ceaseless, single-minded dedication of vermin to hunt and overwhelm her prey.

archetypes.name: Abolisher
archetypes.replaces: Domains; Stern Gaze; Detect Alignment; Discern Lies
archetypes.aonSummary: Abolishers are incorruptible inquisitors who weed out creatures of alien, unnatural origins, finding and exposing aberrations for what they are.

archetypes.name: Cloaked Wolf
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Stern Gaze; Cunning Initiative; Monster Lore; Solo Tactics; Teamwork Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Some inquisitors are adept at appearing harmless until they throw off their unassuming facades and take their enemies by surprise.

archetypes.name: Cold Iron Warden
archetypes.replaces: 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th, 15th, 18th-level Teamwork Feats; Bane; Discern Lies
archetypes.aonSummary: The natural enemies of demoniacs and other cultists of fiendish forces, cold iron wardens are inquisitors who dedicate their lives to eradicating the taint of demonkind from Golarion.

archetypes.name: Exarch
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore; Detect Alignment; Bane; Second Judgment; Greater Bane; Third Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: (Dwarf Only) The gruff traditionalism of most dwarves finds its apex in those who adhere to a strict orthodoxy rooted in ancient principles and practices and who are not amenable whatsoever to change or innovation.

archetypes.name: Exorcist
archetypes.replaces: Second Judgment; Third Judgment; Slayer; True Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: Some inquisitors, as they learn more about the threat of possession and the machinations of the planes, task themselves to expel possessing spirits and conniving outsiders from the world whenever possible.

archetypes.name: Expulsionist
archetypes.replaces: Domain; Monster Lore; Discern Lies
archetypes.aonSummary: Expulsionists are inquisitors who seek to rid the material world of the corrupting influences of wicked spirits that twist mortals to their own ends.

archetypes.name: Faith Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Domain; Justice, Destruction Judgement; Detect Alignment
archetypes.aonSummary: Certain relentless inquisitors burn with special hatred for an enemy of specific convictions, and they stop at nothing when obsessively hunting these foes down.

archetypes.name: Green Faith Marshal
archetypes.replaces: Domain; Stern Gaze; Monster Lore; Discern Lies; Stalwart
archetypes.aonSummary: The Green Faith marshal serves as a literal force of nature, hunting down and punishing those who have committed sins against nature through enslavement and mistreatment of animals or destruction of wild places.

archetypes.name: Heretic
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore
archetypes.aonSummary: While all inquisitors hunt the enemies of the faith, sometimes, either through political maneuvering by her enemies or an unyielding tenacity that breaks her faith’s basic tenets, an inquisitor can find herself a heretic.

archetypes.name: Hexenhammer
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore; Stern Gaze; Domain; Cunning Initiative; Teamwork Feats; Solo Tactics; Spellcasting
archetypes.aonSummary: Hexenhammers learn to use the hexes and some spells of witches, but must pay the price for dealing with supernatural powers, as they slip ever closer to the evil they seek to destroy.

archetypes.name: Iconoclast
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore; Detect Alignment; Discern Lies; Exploit Weakness; True Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: Some magic items are heretical by nature, enabling the unfaithful to spread wickedness. Iconoclasts seek out and remove such crutches, cleansing the taint these items exude.

archetypes.name: Immolator
archetypes.replaces: Smiting Judgment; Bane; Greater Bane; True Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: (Ifrit Only) The immolator puts her pyromaniacal urges to work in the service of a deity. She brings burning retribution down upon the enemies of her faith, consigning their souls to the sacrificial flames.

archetypes.name: Infiltrator
archetypes.replaces: Stern Gaze; Monster Lore; Track; Discern Lies
archetypes.aonSummary: This inquisitor uses guile and deception to blend in among the enemies of the faith rather than confronting them head-on.

archetypes.name: Keeper of Construct
archetypes.replaces: Domain; Stern Gaze; Monster Lore; Exploid Weakness
archetypes.aonSummary: Some of Brigh’s inquisitors, and occasionally those who follow Torag, track down malicious construct crafters and fight renegade constructs with unrivaled expertise.

archetypes.name: Keeper of the Current
archetypes.replaces: Track; Spellcasting; Discern Lies
archetypes.aonSummary: Water-related deities all have organized churches beneath the waves that engage zealous followers to hunt down apostates and enemies. Regardless of their faith, these undersea zealots are known as keepers of the current.

archetypes.name: Kinslayer
archetypes.replaces: Destruction Judgment; Teamwork Feats; Detect Alignment
archetypes.aonSummary: (Dhampir Only) Appalled and guilt-ridden by the horrific circumstances of her birth, a kinslayer dedicates herself to eradicating the very creatures whose blood flows within her veins.

archetypes.name: Living Grimoire
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore; Spellcasting; Cunning Initiative; Orisons; Judgement; Bane; Greater Bane; Second Judgement; Third Judgement; True Judgement
archetypes.aonSummary: The living grimoire literally wields the sacred word of his deity, using his holy tome to smite the foes of his god with divine might.

archetypes.name: Monster Tactician
archetypes.replaces: Judgment; Discern Lies; Second Judgment; Third Judgment; Slayer; True Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: While most inquisitors have learned to take advantage of the movements of their opponents and allies in combat, some instead summon creatures as a means of claiming strategic advantage, exploiting the mystic connection between themselves and their summoned creatures to impart a bit of their own tactical knowledge.

archetypes.name: Oathkeeper
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Class Skills; Monster Lore; Track
archetypes.aonSummary: Oathkeepers formally oversee the creation of bargains and personally hunt down those who dare to violate them.

archetypes.name: Preacher
archetypes.replaces: Solo Tactics
archetypes.aonSummary: Some inquisitors wander the land to spread the true word of their faith.

archetypes.name: Ravener Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Domain; Spells; 3rd-level Teamwork Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: For generations, the catfolk of Murraseth have viewed the cults of Angazhan with loathing and hatred, and they believe it is their sacred duty to hunt down the followers of the Ravener King and expel them from the Material Plane

archetypes.name: Reaper of Secrets
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore; Stern Gaze; Solo Tactics
archetypes.aonSummary: Masters of mind tricks and deception, these divine assassins track down and kill anyone who has forbidden knowledge about their faiths.

archetypes.name: Relic Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Judgment; Domain; Bane; Greater Bane; Second Judgment; Third Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: Some inquisitors specialize in the use and recovery of long-lost relics of their faiths, drawing forth divine might from the recovered items in order to restore their sanctity and wield these artifacts against the enemies of their gods.

archetypes.name: Royal Accuser
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Stern Gaze; Detect Alignment; Solo Tactics; Teamwork Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Royal accusers serve the prince of Ustalav, cutting through the nation’s baroque politics and quietly facing its many threats.

archetypes.name: Sacred Huntsmaster
archetypes.replaces: Judgment; Solo Tactics; Second Judgment; Third Judgment; Slayer; True Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: Some inquisitors create a strong bond with an animal companion, and they hunt and punish threats to the faith as an awe-inspiring duo.

archetypes.name: Sanctified Slayer
archetypes.replaces: Judgment; Second Judgment; Third Judgment; Slayer; True Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: While all inquisitors root out enemies of the faith, in many orders and churches there’s a select group of these religious hunters devoted to one goal, and one goal alone—to terminate the enemies of the faith wherever they can be found.

archetypes.name: Secret Seeker
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore; Bane; Greater Bane; Exploit Weakness
archetypes.aonSummary: Recognizing that torture is a poor method of securing truthful intelligence, secret seekers instead prefer magical means of inquiry.

archetypes.name: Sin Eater
archetypes.replaces: Domain; 6th-level Teamwork Feat; Exploit Weakness
archetypes.aonSummary: There is a sect of inquisitors in some religions that believes it is not enough to hunt the enemies of the church—one must also devour those enemies’ sins.

archetypes.name: Spellbreaker
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore; Bonus Teamwork Feats; Solo Tactics; Final Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: The world is full of dangerous magic, and many recoil in the face of such power. The spellbreaker, by contrast, learns to recognize and resist certain types of magic, wading through waves of magic to reach her foes.

archetypes.name: Suit Seeker
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Domain; Judgment; Second Judgment; Third Judgment; Detect Alignment; True Judgment
archetypes.aonSummary: Though surrounded by meaning and tradition revered by most harrowers, the harrow is a tool that could be abused. Those inquisitors known as suit seekers take grave offense at the misuse of this ancient power, and dedicate their considerable skills to hunting and eliminating any who would abuse the harrow’s magic and the heritage it represents.

archetypes.name: Sworn of the Eldest
archetypes.replaces: Deity; Domain; Monster Lore; Stern Gaze; Solo Tactics; Teamwork Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Although the Eldest rarely have adherents as other deities do, they still occasionally require mortal agents to advance their aims.

archetypes.name: Tactical Leader
archetypes.replaces: Stern Gaze; Solo Tactics; Teamwork Feats; Exploit Weakness
archetypes.aonSummary: Rather than pursuing their holy missions alone, some inquisitors see the inherent value of working with like-minded allies to accomplish mutual goals.

archetypes.name: Traceless Operative
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore; Stern Gaze; Track; Bane; Greater Bane
archetypes.aonSummary: Traceless operatives practice subterfuge and careful preparation in order to accomplish their divine mandates.

archetypes.name: Umbral Stalker
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Domain; Justice Judgement
archetypes.aonSummary: As a consummate lurker in the shadows, an umbral stalker observes the enemies of her faith and strikes before the unfortunate victims even know she is skulking nearby.

archetypes.name: Urban Infiltrator
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Monster Lore; Stalwart
archetypes.aonSummary: Masters of secretly gathering information to further their faith’s ends, urban infiltrators excel at operating within an unfriendly society or infiltrating an enemy cult.

archetypes.name: Vampire Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Altered Judgments (Purity, Smiting); Detect Alignment; Altered Bane
archetypes.aonSummary: The vampire hunter believes that the worst of undead are the ones with unnatural appetities for flesh and blood.

archetypes.name: Vigilant Defender
archetypes.replaces: Judgement; Stern Gaze; Exploit Weakness; True Judgement
archetypes.aonSummary: Some inquisitors focus more on protecting those who share their faiths and their ideals than on actively hunting their enemies.

archetypes.name: Witch Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Monster Lore; Detect Alignment; Discern Lies; True Judgment; Track; Exploit Weakness
archetypes.aonSummary: When pursuing justice for their faith, inquisitors sometimes hunt sorcerers, witches, wizards, and other practitioners of arcane magic—but especially witches, since their devotion to a patron is often seen as suspect by many religions.

archetypes.name: Antiquarian
archetypes.replaces: Alchemy; Poison Lore; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity; Swift Alchemy
archetypes.aonSummary: Antiquarians are collectors, explorers, and scholars who delve into ruined places in search of lost lore and artifacts.

archetypes.name: Bonded Investigator
archetypes.replaces: Poison Lore; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity; 4th-level Studied Strike, 7th-level Investigator Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Bonded investigators use intelligent familiars to assist them in their investigations.

archetypes.name: Cartographer
archetypes.replaces: Poison Lore; Poison Resistance; Keen Recollection; Swift Alchemy
archetypes.aonSummary: Cartographers are eager trailblazers who explore uncharted terrain, study landmarks, and find new paths through the wilderness.

archetypes.name: Cipher
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Inspiration; Trapfinding; Poison Lore; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity; Trap SenseSwift Alchemy; 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, 11th-level Investigator Talent; Studied Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: A cipher trains himself to remain undetected and ignored in order to conduct his investigations without opposition or bothersome questions

archetypes.name: Conspirator
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Inspiration; Trap Sense; 7th-level Investigator Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: A conspirator uses his knowledge of investigations to make sure he avoids any investigations that his rivals perform.

archetypes.name: Cryptid Scholar
archetypes.replaces: Poison Lore; Poison Resistance; Studied Combat; Studied Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: Cryptid scholars research monsters that lurk secretly at the edge of civilization, developing a deep expertise regarding their anatomy, habits, and ecology.

archetypes.name: Cult Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity; Poison Lore; Trap Sense; Swift Alchemy; Studied Combat Studied Strike; 7th, 13th-level Investigator Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Cult hunters seek out heretical secret societies, purging their ideological taint and banishing summoned servants.

archetypes.name: Dread Investigator
archetypes.replaces: Inspiration; Studied Combat; Studied Strike; Poison Lore; Poison Resistance; Poison Immunity; 7th, 13th, and 19th-level Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: The dread investigator observes human behavior after the fact, honing their intuition by delving into the mysteries of death.

archetypes.name: Empiricist
archetypes.replaces: Poison Lore; Poison Resistance; Swift Alchemy; True Inspiration
archetypes.aonSummary: Champions of deductive reasoning and logical insight, empiricists put their faith in facts, data, confirmed observations, and consistently repeatable experiments—these things are their currency of truth.

archetypes.name: Engineer
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Poison Lore; Poison Resistance; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: A number of investigators use their vast knowledge to build machines that replicate the intricacies of the world
