archetypes.aonSummary: Invigorators devote themselves to keeping their allies bodily whole by bolstering their health and spirits.

archetypes.name: Iomedaen Enforcer
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Detect Evil; Smite Evil; Aura of Faith; Aura of Righteousness; Holy Champion
archetypes.aonSummary: Iomedaean enforcers have altered abilities that allow them to stand against the forces of chaos.

archetypes.name: Iroran Paladin
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Aura of Good; Detect Evil; Smite Evil; Aura of Courage; Channel Positive Energy; Divine Bond; Aura of Justice
archetypes.aonSummary: Iroran paladins meditate on self-perfection and train relentlessly, knowing that their example can inspire others to excel.

archetypes.name: Knight of Coins
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Skill Ranks; Detect Evil; 3rd, 9th, 15th-level Mercy
archetypes.aonSummary: Knights of coins promote fair trade and stable commerce between cities and between nations.

archetypes.name: Kraken Slayer
archetypes.replaces: Smite Evil; Divine Health; Divine Bond; Aura of Faith
archetypes.aonSummary: Triton kraken slayers oppose all underwater threats, but they especially target the tentacled monstrosities called krakens.

archetypes.name: Legate
archetypes.replaces: Mercy
archetypes.aonSummary: Though they hold to the same strict paladin code, legates present themselves not as armed crusaders, but as peaceful envoys and advisors, bringing wisdom garnered from the long, stable history of their nation.

archetypes.name: Martyr
archetypes.replaces: Smite Evil; Divine Grace; Aura of Courage; Aura of Resolve; Aura of Righteousness; Divine Health; Lay on Hands; Mercy
archetypes.aonSummary: Martyrs shoulder the blackest suffering of the world onto themselves in order to help others and inspiring their allies to achieve heights of valor rather than seeking the glory for themselves.

archetypes.name: Mind Sword
archetypes.replaces: Lay on Hands; Mercy; Channel Positive Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Veterans of mystical battles against demons of the Worldwound, mind swords merge psychic and divine power, probing and cleansing minds while their telekinetic blades cleave demonic flesh.

archetypes.name: Pearl Seeker
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Class Skills; Detect Evil; Aura of Courage; Aura of Resolve; Spells; Divine Bond; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Some paladins are called to their faith by strange empathic visions and dreams that beckon them to the oceans and beyond.

archetypes.name: Redeemer
archetypes.replaces: Smite Evil; Detect Evil; Aura of Resolve; Aura of Justice
archetypes.aonSummary: (Half-Orc Only) As most half-orcs are outcasts, a half-orc paladin recognizes that often those who are monstrous are not necessarily evil and that sometimes even those who are evil became that way because of circumstances and misfortune.

archetypes.name: Sacred Servant
archetypes.replaces: Smite Evil; Divine Bond; Aura of Resolve
archetypes.aonSummary: Paladins as a general rule, venerate the gods of good and purity, but some take this a step further, dedicating themselves to a specific deity and furthering the cause of the faith.

archetypes.name: Sacred Shield
archetypes.replaces: Smite Evil; Channel Positive Energy; Divine Bond; Aura of Justice; Holy Champion
archetypes.aonSummary: When faced by evil, the sacred shield reaches first not for a weapon, but for her trusty shield. With her faith, she can ward others from harm.

archetypes.name: Scion of Talmandor
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Divine Grace; Divine Bond; Aura of Resolve; Aura of Justice
archetypes.aonSummary: A scion of Talmandor serve by offering assistance to the oppressed and facilitating the peaceful transfer of power from the few to the many.

archetypes.name: Shining Knight
archetypes.replaces: Divine Health; Aura of Justice
archetypes.aonSummary: While paladins often are seen mounted atop a loyal steed, the shining knight is the true symbol of mounted bravery.

archetypes.name: Silver Champion
archetypes.replaces: Divine Bond; Channel Energy; Aura of Justice; Aura of Righteousness; Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: Drake-riding paladins who serve as priests of Apsu.

archetypes.name: Soul Sentinel
archetypes.replaces: 6th, 12th-level Mercy; Aura of Justice
archetypes.aonSummary: Soul sentinels use the strength of their resolve to stem the tide of corruption and insanity, as they believe that the greatest tragedy is a soul lost to evil when it was within their power to save it.

archetypes.name: Stonelord
archetypes.replaces: Smite Evil; Divine Grace; 3rd, 9th, 12th, 15th, 18th-level Mercies; Spells; Channel Positive Energy; Divine Bond; Aura of Justice; Holy Champion
archetypes.aonSummary: (Dwarf Only) A stonelord is a devoted sentinel of dwarven enclaves, drawing the power of the earth and ancient stone to protect her people.

archetypes.name: Sword of Valor
archetypes.replaces: Divine Grace; 6th-level Mercy; Aura of Justice
archetypes.aonSummary: A paladin who chooses to follow in Iomedae's footsteps can become a sword of valor.

archetypes.name: Tempered Champion
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting
archetypes.aonSummary: Tempered champions are trained in the Tempering Hall in Absalom to master their deities’ favored weapons.

archetypes.name: Temple Champion
archetypes.replaces: Spells; Divine Bond; Aura of Justice
archetypes.aonSummary: A temple champion is a powerful warrior dedicated to a good or lawful deity. She thinks of herself primarily as a servant of her deity and secondarily as an agent of her deity’s church.

archetypes.name: Tortured Crusader
archetypes.replaces: Key Ability Score; Skills; Detect Evil; Divine Grace; Smite Evil; Lay on Hands; Channel Energy; Divine Bond; Aura of Courage; Aura of Resolve; Aura of Faith; Aura of Righteousness; Aura of Justice ; Lay on Hands
archetypes.aonSummary: Though tortured crusaders may be beaten and battered, body, mind, and soul, they still somehow continue through torment and hardship. Despite setbacks and impossible odds, they shine like candles even in the darkest times

archetypes.name: Tranquil Guardian
archetypes.replaces: Smite Evil; Aura of Courage; Divine Bond; Aura of Resolve; Aura of Justice; Holy Champion
archetypes.aonSummary: (Aasimar Only) A tranquil guardian is a missionary of peace and tranquility, a soothing voice of succor in a violent and dangerous world.

archetypes.name: Undead Scourge
archetypes.replaces: Aura of Resolve; Aura of Justice
archetypes.aonSummary: Undead are an abomination in the eyes of the just and righteous. It is no surprise then that there are some paladins that dedicate themselves to wiping these unholy terrors from the world.

archetypes.name: Vindictive Bastard
archetypes.replaces: Aura; Detect Evil; Smite Evil; Divine Grace; Lay on Hands; Divine Health; Mercy; Channel Energy; Divine Bond; Aura of Justice; Aura of Faith; Aura of Righteousness; Holy Champion
archetypes.aonSummary: (Ex-paladin archetype) A vindictive bastard is a paladin that strikes out for retribution and revenge, far more interested in tearing down those who have harmed her or her companions than furthering a distant deity’s cause.

archetypes.name: Virtuous Bravo
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Smite Evil; Mercy; Spellcasting
archetypes.aonSummary: Virtuous bravos rely on their wit and grace rather than might and strong armor.

archetypes.name: Warrior of the Holy Light
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Aura of Faith
archetypes.aonSummary: Some paladins use their gifts to focus on the holy light that shines within their souls.

archetypes.name: Wilderness Warden
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Divine Grace; Smite Evil; Aura of Courage; 3rd, 9th, 15th-level Mercy; Spells; Aura of Resolve; Aura of Justice
archetypes.aonSummary: Wilderness wardens are vigilant guardians of natural places of all kinds, from mountain peaks to tangled thickets.

archetypes.name: Amnesiac
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting
archetypes.aonSummary: The amnesiac once possessed great psychic power, but mental blocks—resulting from either a traumatic event or intentional implantation—have caused her to forget what she knew before

archetypes.name: Esoteric Starseeker
archetypes.replaces: Discipline Spells; 1st, 11th-level Phrenic Amplifications; Major Amplifications
archetypes.aonSummary: An esoteric starseeker is a psychic who focuses her studies on uncovering the secrets of the sky and the constellations of the Cosmic Caravan.

archetypes.name: Formless Adept
archetypes.replaces: Phrenic Pool; Psychic Discipline; Discipline Powers; 1st and 15th-level Phrenic Amplification; Discipline Spells; Remade Self
archetypes.aonSummary: Formless adepts master their psychic powers to unshackle themselves from the confines of the flesh and empower their spellcasting.

archetypes.name: Magaambyan Telepath
archetypes.replaces: Discipline Spells; 1st, 11th-level Phrenic Amplifications; Telepathic Bond; Telepathy
archetypes.aonSummary: Followers of Old-Mage Jatembe’s more esoteric wisdom instead focus on the occult connection between all living creatures and the resonance between the natural and supernatural world.

archetypes.name: Mutation Mind
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Phrenic Amplification; Phrenic Amplifications; Major Amplifications
archetypes.aonSummary: Exposure to unintended spell effects, curses, or sources of radiation cause some to manifest psychic powers. When a mutation mind uses her psychic abilities, her physical body changes under the stress, and she risks losing control if she pushes too far.

archetypes.name: Psychic Duelist
archetypes.replaces: 4th-level Discipline Spell; 7th-level Phrenic Amplification; Phrenic Amplifications; Telepathic Bond; Telepathy
archetypes.aonSummary: Psychic duelists hone their mental powers for combat, much as warriors do with their blades.

archetypes.name: Psychic Marauder
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Detect Thoughts; 3rd, 11th, 19th-level Phrenic Amplification; Telepathic Bond; Remade Self
archetypes.aonSummary: The psychic marauder’s powers come hand in hand with madness, either from exposure to alien psyches or from terrifying glimpses into the cosmos that the psychic can’t suppress.

archetypes.name: Terror Weaver
archetypes.replaces: Detect Thoughts; Telepathic Bond; 11th, 15th, 19th-level Phrenic Amplifications
archetypes.aonSummary: A number of exceptional Darklands half-orcs have developed potent psychic abilities, unlocked by generations of exposure to a specific combination of mind-altering fungi and radiation

archetypes.name: Abendego Diver
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Track; Wild Empathy; Favored Terrain; Woodland Stride; Swift Tracker; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Named for the vicious and unending storm in the southern Arcadian Ocean, Abendego divers have pushed their bodies to their limits, holding their breath to expand their lung capacity and swimming until ocean travel is second nature to them.

archetypes.name: Battle Scout
archetypes.replaces: Hunter’s Bond; 2nd, 3rd, 4th Favored Enemies; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Though regular outdoorsmen might suffice in many cases, some large forces look to battle scouts to keep the body of their troops safe and prepared for the terrain and whatever dangers that terrain hides.

archetypes.name: Beast Master
archetypes.replaces: Hunter's Bond; 6th-level Combat Style Feat; Camouflage
archetypes.aonSummary: Some rangers, particularly those in primitive lands or who were raised by animals, have unusually strong bonds with animals.

archetypes.name: Blightwarden
archetypes.replaces: Favored Enemy; Wild Empathy; 1st Favored Terrain; Endurance;
archetypes.aonSummary: Some rangers feel so closely connected to their homelands that they stand as guardians against pervasive corruptions that pervert those lands beyond the point of recognition.

archetypes.name: Bow Nomad
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Combat Style; Endurance; Favored Terrain; 6th-level Combat Feat; Camouflage; Hide in Plain Sight
archetypes.aonSummary: (Kasatha Only) Thanks to their four arms, kasathas can master a combat form native to their home world and rarely witnessed on Golarion—wielding two bows at once.

archetypes.name: Cinderwalker
archetypes.replaces: 1st Favored Terrain; Wild Empathy; Hunter’s Bond; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: Cinderwalkers traverse burning wastelands and restless mountains, thriving in lands most creatures avoid.

archetypes.name: Code Runner
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Wild Empathy; Hunter's Bond
archetypes.aonSummary: A code runner specializes in the subtle and speedy transfer of secret messages.

archetypes.name: Corpse Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Spells; Favored Enemies; Woodland Stride; Swift Tracker
archetypes.aonSummary: Many rangers count the undead among their favored enemies, but some make a full-time job out of hunting down and destroying these walking corpses.

archetypes.name: Dandy
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Favored Enemy; Wild Empathy; Favored Terrain; Hunter's Bond; Spellcasting; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: The antithesis of the gruff and wild woodsmen, a dandy takes effort to master the subtle etiquette of noble courts, the whispers of dark rumors, and the customs of the cultured world.

archetypes.name: Darklands Sailor
archetypes.replaces: Track; Favored Terrain; Woodland Stride; Swift Tracker; Camouflage; Hide in Plain Sight
archetypes.aonSummary: Those plying the lightless waters of the Darklands learn to use sound to augment their compromised vision, providing insight into the hazards lurking below the surface.

archetypes.name: Deep Walker
archetypes.replaces: Favored Terrain; Woodland Stride; Camouflage; Hide in Plain Sight
archetypes.aonSummary: Some rangers devote their lives to the woods, becoming hunters, protectors, and wilderness guides among its diverse terrain types.

archetypes.name: Divine Tracker
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Wild Empathy; Hunter’s Bond
archetypes.aonSummary: Blessed by his deity, a divine tracker hunts down those he deems deserving of his retribution.

archetypes.name: Dragon Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Track; 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th-level Favored Enemies
archetypes.aonSummary: The quintessential dragonslayers, dragon hunters are experts at forging through the wilds in search of great wyrms.

archetypes.name: Drake Warden
archetypes.replaces: Hunter's Bond; 2nd Favored Enemy; Swift Tracker
archetypes.aonSummary: Some rangers specialize in dealing with rambunctious younger drakes and thanks to their methods, their drakes are both fiercely loyal and extremely useful for scouting and stealth missions.

archetypes.name: Dungeon Rover
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Track; Wild Empathy; Hunter’s Bond; Woodland Stride; Swift Tracker
archetypes.aonSummary: These rangers specialize in surviving hostile subterranean environs. They are well equipped to avoid traps, spot secret passages, and deal with inimical dungeon tenants.

archetypes.name: Dusk Stalker
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Favored Terrain; Hunter’s Bond; Camouflage
archetypes.aonSummary: (Fetchling Only) Hunters and guides through the Shadow Plane, dusk stalkers are rangers that thrive in shadow.

archetypes.name: Elemental Envoy
archetypes.replaces: Combat Style; Favored Terrain
archetypes.aonSummary: An elemental envoy travels the Elemental Planes. He has learned to protect himself from their many dangers, and he models his fighting style after their teachings.

archetypes.name: Falconer
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Hunter’s Bond; 6th-level Combat Style Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Rangers have always enjoyed a special bond with a specific animal, but the falconer takes this bond to a deeper level.

archetypes.name: Flamewarden
archetypes.replaces: Hunter's Bond; Spells; Evasion; Camouflage; Improved Evasion; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Emulating the blazing phoenix, flamewardens sweep through the world like a selective forest fire, burning away corruption, evil, and those who cling to decay.

archetypes.name: Fortune-Finder
archetypes.replaces: Track; Hunter's Bond; Woodland Stride; Quarry; Improved Quarry; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Vanaras often leave home to seek fortune and sate their curiosity regarding the mysterious lands that lie beyond their native territories. The most skilled of these thrillseekers are called ba-sadhaks, or fortune-finders.

archetypes.name: Freebooter
archetypes.replaces: Favored Enemy; Hunter's Bond; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: A freebooter is a natural leader, a pirate who works well with a variety of people and in a variety of roles.

archetypes.name: Galvanic Saboteur
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Favored Enemy; Wild Empathy; Favored Terrain; Woodland Stride; Swift Tracker; Camouflage; Hide in Plain Sight
archetypes.aonSummary: Many Kellid locals blame Kevoth-Kul’s change on the influence of the Technic League and view both the League and their mechanical minions with a mix of fear and distrust. Some Kellid rangers have since developed skills to defeat the League’s robotic enforcers and devious arcanists.

archetypes.name: Groom
archetypes.replaces: Track; Endurance; 1st Favored Terrain
archetypes.aonSummary: The groom attends to the needs of the party’s mounts and beasts of burden during their adventures, and guards these animals while the party goes underground.

archetypes.name: Guide
archetypes.replaces: Favored Enemy; Hunter's Bond; Evasion; Quarry; Improved Quarry; Improved Evasion
archetypes.aonSummary: Many rangers are loners, but some choose to use their familiarity with the land to guide others safely through the wilderness.

archetypes.name: Guildbreaker
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Favored Enemy; Wild Empathy; Hunter's Bond; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: Guildbreakers stoke their enmity for their foes, and they train to track the movements of rival organizations, and even to infiltrate these groups to gather secret intelligence.

archetypes.name: Hooded Champion
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Favored Enemy; Combat Syle; Wild Empathy; Endurance; Evasion; Improved Evasion
archetypes.aonSummary: The hooded champion lives on the periphery of civilized lands, and is often at odds with the forces of law and order.

archetypes.name: Horse Lord
archetypes.replaces: Hunter's Bond; Camouflage; Hide in Plain Sight
archetypes.aonSummary: Rangers of the plains use horses or other riding beasts to hunt their lands, forging a near-mystical relationship with their mounts.

archetypes.name: Ilsurian Archer
archetypes.replaces: Track; Wild Empathy; Combat Style; Spellcasting; Swift Tracking; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: Ilsurian archers maintain the strong tradition of archery first developed by soldiers in the service of Ilsur, who raised a small army with which he intended to overthrow the monarch of Korvosa after the fall of the Chelish Empire.

archetypes.name: Infiltrator
archetypes.replaces: Favored Terrain
archetypes.aonSummary: Some rangers study their favored enemies and learn their ways, applying this knowledge to their own abilities and using their foes’ strengths against them.

archetypes.name: Jungle Lord
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Favored Enemy; Favored Terrain; Hunter's Bond; Spells; 5th, 10th, 15th, 18th-level Favored Terrain; Quarry; Improved Quarry; Camouflage; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Jungle lords are tempered by their harsh and unforgiving environments into something more than ordinary men and women.

archetypes.name: Lantern Lighter
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Endurance; Favored Terrain; Woodland Stride; Camouflage; Hide in Plain Sight
archetypes.aonSummary: Lantern lighters were originally entrusted with secretly eliminating the drow and quarantining any knowledge of their existence, but in the new Lantern Bearer era, the lantern lighters have refocused their efforts on helping to rescue those imprisoned by the drow, or even to help individual drow who seek to escape the cruelties of their society for a chance at redemption on the surface.

archetypes.name: Nirmathi Irregular
archetypes.replaces: Normal Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Favored Enemy; Favored Terrain; Altered Spell List
archetypes.aonSummary: An irregular troop from Nirmathas, this ranger chooses to focus on the magic of stealth.

archetypes.name: Planar Scout
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Wild Empathy; Favored Terrain; Hunter's Bond; Evasion; Improved Evasion
archetypes.aonSummary: Planar scouts are rangers specializing in traversing the planes—and surviving their journeys.

archetypes.name: Poison Darter
archetypes.replaces: Favored Enemy; Wild Empathy; Combat Style; Hunter's Bond; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: In dense jungles, foliage and tight spaces hinder all but the most deceptively humble weapons: blowguns and poison.

archetypes.name: Raven Master
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Wild Empathy; Hunter's Bond; Woodland Stride; Swift Tracker; Camouflage; Spellcasting
archetypes.aonSummary: Raven masters serve as messengers and spies for the Silver Ravens, eschewing a ranger’s usual connection to the natural world to form a mystic bond with their birds and to grant both animal and master a number of specialized abilities

archetypes.name: Realm Wanderer
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Track; Hunter's Bond; Swift Tracker; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: These rangers take to heart the lessons they’ve learned from their vastly contrasting experiences and know that creatively embracing this wisdom is sometimes the difference between life and death.

archetypes.name: Sable Company Marine
archetypes.replaces: Hunter’s Bond
archetypes.aonSummary: Sable Company marines receive their training at the elite Endrin Military Academy in Korvosa. A large portion of their education is the handling and riding of hippogriffs, the iconic mounts of members of the company.

archetypes.name: Sentinel
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Hunter's Bond; Woodland Stride; 6th-level Combat Style Feat; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: A sentinel specializes in heightening all of her senses to expose spies and those who work for opposing factions, rooting out all who attempt to slip past her evervigilant watch.

archetypes.name: Shapeshifter
archetypes.replaces: Favored Terrain; Camouflage; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Most rangers venture into the wilderness, but there are some who let the wilderness seep into them.

archetypes.name: Skirmisher
archetypes.replaces: Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: Many rangers rely on spells, but there are some who eschew aid from divine powers for their own reasons.

archetypes.name: Spirit Ranger
archetypes.replaces: Hunter's Bond; Camouflage
archetypes.aonSummary: Some rangers nurture a connection with the spirits that reside in all things.

archetypes.name: Stormwalker
archetypes.replaces: Combat Style; Hunter's Bond; Swift Tracker; Quarry; Improved Evasion; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: Rangers who walk in the tempest unafraid draw the power of the storm into themselves and become stormwalkers.

archetypes.name: Summit Sentinel
archetypes.replaces: Combat Style; Favored Terrain; Swift Tracker; Hide in Plain Sight
archetypes.aonSummary: Some rangers eschew the path of the swift skirmisher and embrace the implacable strength of the mountain.

archetypes.name: Sword-Devil
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Favored Enemy; Favored Terrain; Hunter's Bond; Spells; Quarry; Improved Quarry; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Agile, vengeful, and deadly, a sword-devil ﬁghts with precision and grace, channeling the difficult lessons of a star-crossed life into unparalleled battle prowess.

archetypes.name: Tanglebriar Demonslayer
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Favored Enemy; Endurance; Spells; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: Though they are sworn foes of Treerazer and his kin, Tanglebriar demonslayers are known to venture forth from Kyonin to broaden their expertise in the destruction of demons.

archetypes.name: Tidal Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; 6th-level Combat Style Feat; Track; Camouflage; Favored Terrain; Woodland Stride; Improved Evasion
archetypes.aonSummary: The tidal hunter draws strength from the fish and other wildlife of the deep.

archetypes.name: Toxic Herbalist
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Endurance; Hunter's Bond; Swift Tracker; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: Saviors and destroyers in equal measure, toxic herbalists use nature’s bounty to craft remedies and poisons.

archetypes.name: Toxophilite
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Combat Style; Endurance; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: The toxophilite emulates the sharpshooting rangers of legend, who could pin a fly to the wall with a single shot or split one arrow with another.

archetypes.name: Transporter
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Favored Terrain; Hunter's Bond; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: Transporters specialize in smuggling people as efficiently as possible through harsh and difficult environments.

archetypes.name: Trapper
archetypes.replaces: Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: A trapper is a ranger who focuses exclusively on traps, rather than learning conventional magic.

archetypes.name: Trophy Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Combat Feat Style; Hunter’s Bond
archetypes.aonSummary: Some rangers have taken up the mysteries of black powder in order to become big game hunters.

archetypes.name: Urban Ranger
archetypes.replaces: Favored Terrain; Endurance; Woodland Stride; Camouflage; Hide in Plain Sight
archetypes.aonSummary: For the urban ranger, the streets and sewers of the city are just as dangerous as the barren wastelands or the deep forests.

archetypes.name: Warden
archetypes.replaces: Favored Enemy; Combat Style Feats; Hunter’s Bond; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: All rangers have a bond with the wilderness, but the warden may have the strongest. This protector sits guard in the middle of the wilderness, keeping a lookout for any dangers that might spill from the deeper wilderness beyond, and protecting civilization from the savagery of nature—and vice versa.

archetypes.name: Wave Warden
archetypes.replaces: Track; Combat Style; Favored Terrain; Woodland Stride; Swift Tracker
archetypes.aonSummary: (Merfolk Only) The wave warden patrols beneath the sea, preserving the safety and secrets of merfolk communities.

archetypes.name: Wild Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Favored Enemy; Woodland Stride; Swift Tracker
archetypes.aonSummary: A wild hunter seeks to emulate the animals around him to keep him safe while he tracks his prey.

archetypes.name: Wild Shadow
archetypes.replaces: Track; Wild Empathy; Favored Terrain; Hunter’s Bond; Woodland Stride; Quarry; Camouflage; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: (Half-Elf Only) The isolation that some half-elves feel leads them to live a life of isolation amid the wild places of the world.

archetypes.name: Wild Soul
archetypes.replaces: Code of Conduct; Favored Enemy; Swift Tracker; Quarry; Improved Quarry; Master Hunter
archetypes.aonSummary: Wild souls hail from primitive roots in the wild and venture to more civilized lands and learn their ways.

archetypes.name: Wild Stalker
archetypes.replaces: Favored Enemy; 2nd-level Combat Style Feat; Hunter’s Bond
archetypes.aonSummary: The wild stalker forsakes the bonds of community and lives in the trackless wilds far from others of his kind, or perhaps grew up there, never knowing of civilization as anything more than his enemy.

archetypes.name: Wilderness Explorer
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Wild Empathy; Hunter's Bond; Swift Tracker; Favored Terrain; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: Wilderness explorers are adept at making peaceful contact with remote societies.

archetypes.name: Wilderness Medic
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Endurance; Evasion; Hunter's Bond; Improved Evasion
archetypes.aonSummary: Wilderness medics know a variety of ways they can supply and preserve a rebellion or similar movement without requiring any resources that might make them easier to track down.

archetypes.name: Witchguard
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Hunter’s Bond; Endurance; Spells; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: Witchguards are the sworn defenders of the White Witches of Irrisen.

archetypes.name: Yokai Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Favored Enemy; Woodland Stride; Camouflage
archetypes.aonSummary: Yokai hunters possess a supernatural tether to the spirit worlds that shroud mortal existence.

archetypes.name: Acrobat
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Whether they are daring thieves, infiltrating assassins, or intrepid spies, proper training in acrobatics is a valuable boon for rogues.

archetypes.name: Bandit
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Bandits tend to have a variety of skills; sometimes these skills are similar to a ranger’s, but a bandit’s tactics always deal with surprise followed by intimidation, with the clear threat of naked force if intimidation does not do the trick.

archetypes.name: Bekyar Kidnapper
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: A Bekyar kidnapper is not only adept at hiding herself in thick jungles and quickly subduing her prey, but also at spreading rumors of hidden ruins, buried treasure, and other such valuables that might lure an unwary foreigner into her traps.

archetypes.name: Bellflower Irrigator
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 4th-level Rogue Talent; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Rather than focusing on saving slaves, Bellflower irrigators seek to defeat slavery by aiming to eliminate the source.

archetypes.name: Burglar
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Adept at infiltration, trap removal, and lock picking, burglars prey on the homes of the wealthy and forgotten tombs alike.

archetypes.name: Carnivalist
archetypes.replaces: 2nd, 4th, 6th-level Rogue Talents; Sneak Attack; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Carnivalists train their miniature minions to perform acts of larceny and often hide their true talents behind theatrical sideshows.

archetypes.name: Cat Burglar
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: (Catfolk Only) Cat burglars are masters of breaking and entering, using their feline grace to make it seem as though no crime was ever committed in the first place.

archetypes.name: Chameleon
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: An absolute master of disguise, a chameleon effortlessly blends into any environment.

archetypes.name: Charlatan
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: A charlatan is a master of lies and deception.

archetypes.name: Consigliere
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Trapfinding; Evasion; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Trap Sense; 10th-level Rogue Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Consiglieres act as trusted mediators and administrators for crime families and various criminal organizations, and many serve as the right hand to the leaders of such groups.

archetypes.name: Construct Saboteur
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Trapfinding; 2nd-level Rogue Talent; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: The construct saboteur harnesses arcane energy to combat the golems and eldritch guardians that prowl the depths of ancient ruins and forgotten tombs.

archetypes.name: Counterfeit Mage
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 4th-level Rogue Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Charlatans and stage magicians use slight of hand to fake magic. A counterfeit mage goes a step further, parroting the motions and activation phrases used by arcane casters to activate wands or other magical accoutrements.

archetypes.name: Cutpurse
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Cutpurses are often trained by guilds to collect the guild’s tax from local businesses on a daily basis, whether through intimidation or pickpocketing. Some find themselves taking up the mantle of adventurer, and their talents are generally appreciated in this role, but the cutpurse is still the first person her companions look to when an item goes missing.

archetypes.name: Dark Lurker
archetypes.replaces: Evasion; 2nd, 8th, 14th, and 20th-level Rogue Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Dark lurkers use darkness as an ally.

archetypes.name: Deadly Courtesan
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 2nd-level Rogue Trick; Trap Sense; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: (Vishkanya Only) Skilled at manipulation and diversion, the deadly courtesan builds up those around her and periodically takes them down.

archetypes.name: Desert Raider
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Desert raider learn the secrets of the deserts and become inured to their dangers.

archetypes.name: Discretion Specialist
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense/Danger Sense; 4th, 12-th level Rogue Talents; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Discretion specialists deal with bodies, inconvenient witnesses, and other loose ends.

archetypes.name: Dreamthief
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Sneak Attack; Master Strike; Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; 12th-level Rogue Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Each dreamthief bears a focused fragment of emotion, known as a dreamshard, within her soul. This metaphysical crystal grants a dreamthief supernatural powers, which she supplements with skill and grace.

archetypes.name: Driver
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: A driver makes her living driving vehicles in the service of those who can pay for her considerable talents.

archetypes.name: Earthshadow
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Evasion; 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th-level Rogue Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: In the centuries since the Quest for the Sky, the mystic lore the dwarves call earthcraft has been passed down through the generations, and its practitioners are called earthshadows.

archetypes.name: Eldritch Raider
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Skill Ranks; 2nd-level Rogue Talent; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: (Gillman Only) An eldritch raider is a rogue who seeks to unravel the mysteries of the destruction of the gillmen’s homeland.

archetypes.name: Eldritch Scoundrel
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiency; Skills; Trap Sense; Sneak Attack; Rogue Talents; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Students of arcane magic, legerdemain, and stealth, eldritch scoundrels are a rare breed of adventurer most commonly found seeking lost and valuable arcane writings in the ruins of fallen empires, such as Thassilon or the Jistka Imperium.

archetypes.name: Escapologist
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: The escapologist excels at escaping any confinement, whether physical, magical, or mental. Few restraints can hold an escapologist for long.

archetypes.name: False Medium
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd-level Rogue Talent; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: The false medium is a master of pretending to have occult powers in order to manipulate the emotions and atmosphere of the people and places around him, often reaping a healthy reward from the bereaved, who find solace in his comforting lies.

archetypes.name: Fey Prankster
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd, 6th, 8th, and 12th-level Rogue Talents; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: (Gathlain) Fey pranksters specialize in tricking others to teach a lesson or for their own entertainment.

archetypes.name: Filcher
archetypes.replaces: Evasion; Trap Sense 1-6; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: (Halfling Only) Whether cutting purses in the midst of combat or replacing prized items with fakes under the noses of their owners, the filcher is the master of the quick and quiet steal.

archetypes.name: Galtan Agitator
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense; 4th, 8th, 12th-level Rogue Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Galtan agitators fight mightily to cast down the enemies of their ideals within the shambles of the tumultuous nation of Galt.

archetypes.name: Guerrilla
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Evasion; Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Guerrillas fight against oppressive leadership and governments including Chelish colonization in Sargava and the power structures in Cheliax proper, Nidal, and Razmiran

archetypes.name: Guild Agent
archetypes.replaces: Evasion; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Evasion; Master Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: Guild agents are members of a thieves’ guild or other shadowy organization. What they lose in independence, they more than make up for in benefits gained due to their association’s infrastructure.

archetypes.name: Gun Smuggler
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiencies; Trapfinding; Sneak Attack; Trap Finding; 6th-level Rogue Talent; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Gun smugglers are adept at procuring firearms and concealing their secret weapons

archetypes.name: Heister
archetypes.replaces: 2nd, 4th, 8th-level Rogue Talent; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Notorious for their stealth, imagination, and elaborately planned thefts and capers, heisters specialize in breaking into secure locations, stealing items of value, and escaping undetected.

archetypes.name: Investigator
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding
archetypes.aonSummary: Not all rogues work against the law. Investigators use their skills to serve the law, often in the employ of nobles or in the pursuit of noble causes.

archetypes.name: Kintargo Rebel
archetypes.replaces: Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Whenever the Chelish navy sails into the port, these rebels are quick to appear agreeably subservient in order to conceal their noncompliance and avoid retribution.

archetypes.name: Kitsune Trickster
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: (Kitsune Only) The kitsune trickster combines her sharpened wit with minor arcane powers of charm and persuasion.

archetypes.name: Knife Master
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Sneak Attack; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: The knife master is a trained killer who specializes in close-up combat and the wave and weave of knife fighting.

archetypes.name: Makeshift Scrapper
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiencies; Trapfinding; Trap Sense; 12th-level Rogue Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Some combatants specialize in the study of certain weapons, but those without formal training often learn to survive a fight by making brilliant use of whatever is lying around.

archetypes.name: Master of Disguise
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd, 10th-level Rogue Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: A master of disguise believes that never letting her adversaries know her true identity protects her from bad luck or missteps on a job.

archetypes.name: Nameless Shadow
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 14th, 18th-level Rogue Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Where bandits and tyrants prey on merchants and caravans, the nameless shadow preys on bandits and tyrants.

archetypes.name: Needler
archetypes.replaces: Evasion; Uncanny Dodge; 6th-level Rogue Talent; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Needlers use subtlety and misdirection to deliver deadly poisons to unsuspecting victims in creative and unorthodox ways.

archetypes.name: Numerian Scavenger
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: A Numerian scavenger lives for the discovery of new technological wonders scraped from the depths of the strange ruins, metal caverns, and outlandish junkyards of Numeria.

archetypes.name: Okeno Liberator
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: The sight of yellow sails on the Inner Sea signals the approach of a ship from Okeno, home port of the most ruthless and feared of all slaving operations. Most who see these sails flee in terror, but some freedom fighters actually endeavor to be captured, knowing that being taken to Stonespine Island in manacles is the easiest way to infiltrate the city, liberate other slaves, and lead them to freedom.

archetypes.name: Phantom Thief
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Sneak Attack; Trapfinding; Trap Sense; Master Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: Phantom thieves come from the ranks of the elite, having grown bored with their finery, and seek thrills from acts of daring, skill, and crime.

archetypes.name: Pirate
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd-level Rogue Talent; Trapfinding
archetypes.aonSummary: A pirate breaks from the confines of country and king to commit her crimes upon the high seas.

archetypes.name: Planar Sneak
archetypes.replaces: Trapsense; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: A planar sneak finds creative ways to defy conventional limitations when trying to overcome extraplanar obstacles.

archetypes.name: Poisoner
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: The poisoner knows poison is just a tool toward an end, and is no different than any other weapon.

archetypes.name: Rake
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: The rake is a rogue who is open about her skills and talents, often to the point of being boastful.

archetypes.name: Relic Raider
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Relic raiders are rogues who specialize in recovering treasures from ruins and tombs, some in a quest for knowledge, others out of a desire for riches.

archetypes.name: River Rat
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: River rats are skilled at hiding amid reeds and roots, striking the unwary from the shallows as others would from the shadows.

archetypes.name: Roof Runner
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: A specialized urban acrobat, the roof runner makes her home high atop the spires and gables of great cities.

archetypes.name: Rotdrinker
archetypes.replaces: Evasion; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Poisons are common tools in a rogue’s trade, and some poison-using rogues are so frequently exposed to these toxins that they have developed resistances to particular poisons.

archetypes.name: Sanctified Rogue
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: The sanctified rogue serves a higher purpose, acting as a representative of a church or cult, or following the tenets of a specific faith or deity.

archetypes.name: Sapper
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd and 4th-level Rogue Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: The sapper is a trained siege engineer and can deal with traps and other obstacles given plenty of time.

archetypes.name: Scout
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Scouts frequently roam the wilderness, often banding together as bandits, but sometimes serving as guides, as trailblazers, or as companions to a ranger or barbarian warrior.

archetypes.name: Scroll Scoundrel
archetypes.replaces: 2nd-level Rogue Talent, Trap Sense, Uncanny Dodge, Improved Uncanny Dodge, 10th-level Rogue Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Using knowledge from extensive research, the scroll scoundrel exploits overconfidence and predictability to better stay alive.

archetypes.name: Sczarni Swindler
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Evasion; Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: If life is a game, the Sczarni play to win. When skill and luck aren’t enough, cheating is often the best option.

archetypes.name: Seeker of the Lost
archetypes.replaces: 2nd-level Rogue Talent; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Aquatic elven adventurers descending into the ruins of sunken Azlant developed techniques to ease their explorations, and they now share these techniques among a loose group of acquaintances calling themselves the seekers of the lost.

archetypes.name: Shadow Scion
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd, 8th, 14th-level Rogue Talent; Master Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: Shadow scions have learned the secrets of light and dark and draw power from the shadows themselves.

archetypes.name: Shadow Walker
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd-level Rogue Talent; Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Shadow walkers are comfortable in light, darkness, and the shadows in between.

archetypes.name: Sharper
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 16th-level Rogue Talent; Trap Sense;
archetypes.aonSummary: Sharpers use trickery and deception to part an owner from his valuables.

archetypes.name: Skulking Slayer
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiency; Class Skills; Trapfinding; Rogue Talent; Advanced Rogue Talent; Trap Sense 1-4
archetypes.aonSummary: (Half-Orc Only) Pushed into a life of crime by the society around them, half-orcs gravitate toward criminal activities that suit them best.

archetypes.name: Sly Saboteur
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge;
archetypes.aonSummary: Sly saboteurs are irregular soldiers who specialize in sabotage and surprise attacks.

archetypes.name: Smuggler
archetypes.replaces: Trap Sense; Trapfinding; Evasion
archetypes.aonSummary: Smugglers specialize in moving contraband from one area to another while avoiding detection by authorities.

archetypes.name: Snare Setter
archetypes.replaces: Sneak Attack; Trapfinding; Master Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: (Kobold Only) Deep in darkness, the snare setter constructs his deadly traps and brutal mechanisms to confound and destroy any who try to invade his domain.

archetypes.name: Sniper
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Some say that the sniper is the worst kind of assassin: a killer who waits silently in the shadows and then strikes from a distance without remorse.

archetypes.name: Snoop
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Evasion; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; 8th-level Rogue Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Snoops act as information peddlers, specializing in gathering secrets through investigation, subterfuge, and coercion, and selling or trading those secrets for personal gain.

archetypes.name: Spy
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: The best spies are like chameleons, but not only can they change their appearances to fit the situation, they can also change their personalities, allegiances, and even loves if that’s what it takes to achieve their clandestine goals.

archetypes.name: Survivalist
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: The survivalist focuses her talents on surviving harsh and unforgiving conditions that would kill a lesser rogue.

archetypes.name: Swamp Poisoner
archetypes.replaces: Racial Traits; Trapfinding; 2nd-level Rogue Talent; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: (Grippli) Swamp poisoners use their own toxins to defend their homes and level the playing field

archetypes.name: Swashbuckler
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: A paragon of mobile swordplay, the swashbuckler is a rogue who focuses almost exclusively on honing her skill at arms and perfecting daring acrobatic moves and elaborate flourishes that border on performance.

archetypes.name: Swordmaster
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: (Tengu Only) A swordmaster meditates to strengthen her spiritual connection to her blade. She strives to perfect her skills by mastering six deadly trances.

archetypes.name: Sylvan Trickster
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Trapfinding; Rogue Talents; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Sylvan tricksters are rogues who model themselves after the mischievous fey of legend.

archetypes.name: Thug
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense
archetypes.aonSummary: Some criminals steal with finesse, their victims only discovering the crime when the rogue is long gone and the coin already spent. A thug, on the other hand, cares nothing for finesse.

archetypes.name: Tidal Trickster
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; 4th, 8th-level Rogue Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Tidal tricksters roam the seas, using their skillful mastery of the currents to move across aquatic battlefields and throw their enemies off-balance.

archetypes.name: Toxic Talon
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiencies; Trapfinding; Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: A toxic talon spends resources and time combining easy-to-obtain materials into dangerous toxins to aid in the defense of Andoran.

archetypes.name: Trapsmith
archetypes.replaces: Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Some rogues are not content with just disabling traps—they love to build them, finding a captivating beauty in the turning of gears and the slither of ropes over pulleys.

archetypes.name: Underground Chemist
archetypes.replaces: Evasion; 4th-level Rogue Talent; Advanced Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Underground chemists are part of the rotting, fetid underbelly of the alchemical world.

archetypes.name: Vexing Dodger
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; 2nd-level Rogue Talent; Trap Sense; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: Vexing dodgers take advantage of their smaller size to outmaneuver larger foes such as giants.

archetypes.name: Waylayer
archetypes.replaces: Trapfinding; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; 12th and 20th-level Rogue Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: A clever rogue knows the easiest battle to win is the one that’s over before your foe knows it has begun.

archetypes.name: Brawling Blademaster
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Mount; Weapon Expertise; Mounted Archer; Banner; Greater Banner
archetypes.aonSummary: Brawling blademaster samurai use weapon strikes and unarmed attacks in equal measure

archetypes.name: Ironbound Sword
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Expertise; Banner; Greater Banner
archetypes.aonSummary: The ironbound sword’s fighting style, focused on incapacitating opponents rather than killing them, can subdue a foe without causing permanent harm, leaving the soul of the samurai unstained by deaths of her enemies.

archetypes.name: Sovereign Blade
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Mount; Mounted Archer; 6th, 12th, 18th-level bonus feats
archetypes.aonSummary: In Tian Xia, many samurai are tutored in the ways of honor using lessons that originate from sovereign dragons and their dedication to safeguarding harmony.

archetypes.name: Sword Saint
archetypes.replaces: Samurai's Mount; Mounted Charge; Banner; Greater Banner
archetypes.aonSummary: Sword saints hail from lands where samurai are prevalent, and are often ronin who wander the world seeking new challenges to perfect their intricate style of swordplay called iaijutsu.

archetypes.name: Ward Speaker
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Resolve; Greater Resolve; True Resolve; Honorable Stand
archetypes.aonSummary: The ward speaker draws power from simple rituals to honor the spirits found throughout the world so that he might better protect those entrusted to his care.

archetypes.name: Warrior Poet
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Mount; Weapon Expertise; Banner; Greater Banner; Challenge; Mounted Archer; Demanding Challange; Bonus Combat Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Warrior poets often study calligraphy, flower arrangement, poetry, and other courtly arts, but when called to battle, they treat combat as its own art form, fighting with beauty and grace.

archetypes.name: Yojimbo
archetypes.replaces: Mount; Weapon Expertise; Mounted Archer
archetypes.aonSummary: Yojimbo are highly trained bodyguards favored by the nobles and warlords of distant Minkai.

archetypes.name: Animist
archetypes.replaces: Spirit Magic Spells; 2nd, 8th, 10th, 12th, and 18th-level Hexes; Manifestation
archetypes.aonSummary: Even among mystical practitioners, the animist has a strange perspective and even stranger magic. The animist perceives that all things have a spirit, including objects, constructs, illnesses, buildings, and the environment.

archetypes.name: Benefactor
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Hexes;
archetypes.aonSummary: A benefactor seeks to improve the lives of others by primarily offering powerful supportive abilities and magic to her allies and others she deems worthy.

archetypes.name: Crystal Tender
archetypes.replaces: Spirit Animal; Wandering Spirit; 8th-level Shaman Hex; Manifestation
archetypes.aonSummary: A crystal tender focuses on the spirits of metal and stone, using crystals as a means to focus the power of the spirits she venerates.

archetypes.name: Deep Shaman
archetypes.replaces: Spirit; Spirit Animal; Class Skills; Spirit Abilities
archetypes.aonSummary: Deep shamans are tied to spirits from the depths.

archetypes.name: Draconic Shaman
archetypes.replaces: Spirit; Spirit Animal; 4th, 10th-level Hexes; Spirit Magic
archetypes.aonSummary: Some shamans draw their powers from the might of dragons. These shamans each gain a powerful drake as an ally, and view caring for that drake as a sacred duty

archetypes.name: Grasping Vine
archetypes.replaces: Spirit Animal; Spirit Magic; 2nd, 8th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Grasping vine shamans are typically adherents of one of several scattered sects dedicated to the Green Mother. They revere plant life in all its forms, with a special fondness for poisonous or carnivorous plants.

archetypes.name: Name-Keeper
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Spirit Animal; Spirit Magic; Wandering Spirit; Wandering Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Name-keepers have delved into the storied histories etched into the Wall of Names and communed with the departed spirits of those whose names are memorialized on the monument.

archetypes.name: Overseer
archetypes.replaces: Spirit Magic; Deliver Touch Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: While all shamans use their connection to the spirits of the world to draw upon otherworldly magic powers, the shamans of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings have a unique tradition in which they use the power of patron spirits to directly control their enemies.

archetypes.name: Possessed Shaman
archetypes.replaces: Spirit Magic; 2nd and 6th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: For a possessed shaman, merely communing with the spirit world is insufficient. Instead, she invites the spirits to share her body, granting them the chance to experience corporeal existence.

archetypes.name: Primal Warden
archetypes.replaces: Spirit Animal; Spirit Magic; 4th, 8th, 12th-levle Hex
archetypes.aonSummary:
A
shaman who communes with spirits that linger in areas where primal magic reigns, learning to stabilize
these erratic energies and draw upon them to her benefit.

archetypes.name: Serendipity Shaman
archetypes.replaces: Spirit Magic spells
archetypes.aonSummary: The serendipitous, shamanistic rites associated with the traditional catfolk worship of the so-called “spirits of creation” focus upon attracting good fortune and banishing ill fortune in the name of these spirits.

archetypes.name: Speaker for the Past
archetypes.replaces: Spirit Familiar; Wandering Spirit; Wandering Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: A speaker for the past is a shaman who specifically serves as the voice for spirits from her people’s history.

archetypes.name: Spirit Warden
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Spirit Magic Spells; 2nd and 10th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Not all spirits deserve reverence and respect. Some are twisted and despicable. It’s a spirit warden’s duty to end these spirits’ existence.

archetypes.name: True Silvered Throne
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Spirit Animal; Wandering Spirit; Wandering Hex; 8th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Members in good standing who have risen to a prestigious rank within the Esoteric Order of the Palatine Eye, true silvered thrones have managed to discover rituals and occult secrets within the lore of their order.

archetypes.name: Unsworn Shaman
archetypes.replaces: Spirit; Hex; Spirit Animal; Wandering Spirit; Wandering Hex; Spirit Magic
archetypes.aonSummary: An unsworn shaman never binds herself to one specific spirit, always making new deals as she deems necessary for the circumstances that she finds herself in.

archetypes.name: Visionary
archetypes.replaces: Wandering Spirit; Spirit Magic Spells; Wandering Hex; Greater Wandering Spirit; True Wandering Spirit
archetypes.aonSummary: The visionary is a master at divination, drawing upon her intimate relationship with the spirit world to ferret out all manner of secrets and insights about the world around her and beyond.

archetypes.name: Witch Doctor
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; 4th, 8th, 10th, and 12th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: The witch doctor is a healer who specializes in afflictions of the soul.

archetypes.name: Adaptive Shifter
archetypes.replaces: Shifter Claws; Shifter Aspect; Chimeric Aspect; Greater Chimeric Aspect; Final Aspect; Wild Empathy; Track; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Rather than emulate other animals entirely, some shifters learn to reshape their forms on the fly in response to a range of stimuli

archetypes.name: Dragonblood Shifter
archetypes.replaces: Shifter Aspect; Wilder Shape; Chimeric Aspect; Greater Chimeric Aspect; Final Aspect
archetypes.aonSummary: Dragonblood shifters draw upon the inherent strength and majesty of the true dragons, gaining a measure of their powers from their association.

archetypes.name: Elementalist Shifter
archetypes.replaces: Languages; Shifter Aspect; Wild Empathy; Shifter Claws; Wild Shape; Chimeric Aspect; Greater Chimeric Aspect
archetypes.aonSummary: Rather than drawing power from bestial aspects, elementalist shifters channel power from the Inner Sphere and can take on powerful elemental forms at the cost of the greater diversity available to traditional shifters.

archetypes.name: Feyform Shifter
archetypes.replaces: Shifter Aspect; Wild Shape; Chimeric Aspect; Greater Chimeric Aspect; Final Aspect
archetypes.aonSummary: Feyform shifters are intimately linked to the First World, and can draw from it to gain otherworldly powers.

archetypes.name: Fiendflesh Shifter
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Shifter Claws; Wild Shape; Shifter Aspect; Defensive Instinct; Chimeric Aspect; Greater Chimeric Instinct
archetypes.aonSummary: By forging dark pacts with extraplanar forces, fiendflesh shifters invoke sinister powers to assume the strengths of daemons, demons, or devils.

archetypes.name: Holy Beast
archetypes.replaces: Deity; Shifter Claws; Wild Empathy; Track; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step
archetypes.aonSummary: Holy beast shifters pledge to hunt down their deity’s enemies to earn that deity’s blessing.

archetypes.name: Leafshifter
archetypes.replaces: Shifter Claws; Shifter Aspect
archetypes.aonSummary: (Ghoran only) Rather than assume aspects taken from the traits of natural animals, a leafshifter transforms into plant-animal hybrids that resemble living topiaries.

archetypes.name: Oozemorph
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Chimeric Form; Greater Chimeric Form; Wild Shape; Shifter Aspect; Shifter Claws; Wild Empathy; Defensive Instinct; Woodland Stride
archetypes.aonSummary: While most shifters are trained in druidic traditions that allow them to tap into animalistic powers, others look instead to the simplest forms of life for inspiration. Known as oozemorphs, these shifters focus on the ooze—a form of life as simple in construction as it is dangerous in combat.

archetypes.name: Rageshaper
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Wild Shape; Shifter Aspect; Shifter Claws; Defensive Instinct; Chimeric Aspect; Greater Chimeric Aspect; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step
archetypes.aonSummary: The rageshaper is a destructive force of nature brought to bear—a wild and uncontrollable engine of annihilation fueled by wrath.

archetypes.name: Style Shifter
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiencies; Shifter Aspect; Chimeric Aspect; Greater Chimeric Aspect; Final Aspect; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Style shifters have been able to perfect their combat techniques to the point where they can augment a combat style by partially transforming into the creature that inspired it.

archetypes.name: Swarm Shifter
archetypes.replaces: Wild Shape; Shifter Aspect; Chimeric Aspect; Greater Chimeric Aspect; Final Aspect
archetypes.aonSummary: Swarm shifters channel the essence of the basest and most overlooked animals, vermin.

archetypes.name: Verdant Shifter
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Shifter Aspect; Defensive Instinct; Wild Shape; Chimeric Form; Greater Chimeric Form
archetypes.aonSummary: Verdant shifters have an affinity for plants rather than animals and gain a plantlike form that grows in power as they do.

archetypes.name: Weretouched
archetypes.replaces: Shifter Aspect; Wild Empathy; Wild Shape
archetypes.aonSummary: Weretouched shifters are scions of lycanthropic forces, whether hereditary or supernaturally imposed. They can assume both animal and hybrid forms, as a lycanthrope does.

archetypes.name: Wild Effigy
archetypes.replaces: Wild Empathy; Track; Woodland Stride; Trackless Step; Defensive Instinct
archetypes.aonSummary: A wild effigy still takes on the shapes of natural animals, but rather than transforming her body into flesh and muscle, she transforms into constructed effigies of her chosen aspects.

archetypes.name: Augur
archetypes.replaces: Well-Versed; Versatile Performance; Spell Kenning
archetypes.aonSummary: Tales of Merivesta Olinchi are surprisingly common among the Bekyar of the Mwangi Expanse, who claim she spent some time studying their traditions and history.

archetypes.name: Bacchanal
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; Versatile Performance; Song of Marching; Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: Bacchanals are skalds who use ecstatic dancing and ribald songs to influence the primal instincts of listeners.

archetypes.name: Battle Scion
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Dirge of Doom; Song of the Fallen; Master Skald
archetypes.aonSummary: The battle scion possesses a unique mixture of courtly grace alongside martial and magical prowess.

archetypes.name: Bekyar Demon Dancer
archetypes.replaces: Skills; Versatile Performance; 3rd, 6th, and 9th-level Rage Powers
archetypes.aonSummary: While the twisted power of the demon-worshiping Bekyar’s skalds is great, it comes at a terrible price.

archetypes.name: Belkzen War Drummer
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiencies; Bardic Knowledge; Scribe Scroll; Lore Master; 7th-level Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: These fierce drummers are equally adept at tapping out a driving rhythm and rapping enemies upside the head with the same massive clubs they use to beat the crude hidecovered drums they carry into battle.

archetypes.name: Boaster
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; Uncanny Dodge; Song of Marching; Lore Master; Song of the Fallen; Rage Powers; 6th-level Rage Power
archetypes.aonSummary: Boasters use incredible tales and claims to challenge themselves and their allies to accomplish remarkable feats.

archetypes.name: Bold Schemer
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bardic Knowledge; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Damage Reduction; Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: The bold schemer combines wrath, wits, and daring to win battles and wars in unconventional ways, often through infiltration and deception.

archetypes.name: Court Poet
archetypes.replaces: Inspired Rage; Song of Strength; Well-Versed
archetypes.aonSummary: Court poets elevate the skald’s love of history and poetry to an aristocratic ideal, captivating courts with complicated poetic traditions and inspiring others with their craft.

archetypes.name: Dragon Skald
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; Bardic Knowledge; Well-Versed; Song of Marching
archetypes.aonSummary: The Ulfen prize skalds on sea raids and linnorm hunts. Dragon skald performances involve song, whistling, or blowing mighty horns, and viking sailors often talk about having a skald along to whistle up a wind or sing away the mists on the morning of a momentous raid.

archetypes.name: Elegist
archetypes.replaces: Raging Song; Rage Powers; Well-Versed; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: Some skalds internalize the saddest and must mournful of stories, so much that they are able to manifest the emotions caused by these tales in physical form.

archetypes.name: Fated Champion
archetypes.replaces: Well-Versed; Spell Kenning; Dirge of Doom; Master Skald
archetypes.aonSummary: Among cultures where skalds are the keepers of lore and wisdom, there are those who learn to read the winds of fate and take up the mantle of the fated champion, knowing and embracing their destined paths with strength borne of conviction.

archetypes.name: Herald of the Horn
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; 5th, 11th, and 17th-level Spell Kenning; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: Whether with the polished metal trumpet of a standing army or the crude curved animal horn of savage raiders, a herald of the horn sounds his raging song with thunderous blasts, which can bolster allies or shatter castle walls.

archetypes.name: Hunt Caller
archetypes.replaces: Well-Versed; Song of Strength; Song of the Fallen; 6th, 18th-leve Rage Power; Spell Kenning
archetypes.aonSummary: Hunt callers are skalds whose songs draw their allies into the animal world.

archetypes.name: Instigator
archetypes.replaces: Spell Kenning; Dirge of Doom; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: he instigator influences the will of the people, turning them toward his own purposes.

archetypes.name: Red Tongue
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; 7th, 12th, 17th-level Versatile Performance
archetypes.aonSummary: The tengu tendency toward dramatic flourishes and rhetoric creates an environment in which political clubs led by hot-blooded firebrands—referred to as red tongues in polite company—dominate the political scene by swaying emotions in the moment and wielding magic in the shadows.

archetypes.name: Serpent Herald
archetypes.replaces: 3rd-level Rage Power; Spell Kenning
archetypes.aonSummary: Warrior bands devoted to Ragadahn are often led by a serpent herald, whose deep roars shake the earth itself.

archetypes.name: Spell Warrior
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; Inspired Rage; Spell Kenning; Dirge of Doom; Master Skald
archetypes.aonSummary: The spell warrior uses his arcane knowledge rather than his rage to turn the tide of battle in favor of himself and his allies.

archetypes.name: Sunsinger
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Song of Marching; Spell Kenning;
archetypes.aonSummary: Qadiran sunsingers are particularly religious skalds of Sarenrae who call down their goddess’s glory to fill soldiers with fire.

archetypes.name: Totem Channeler
archetypes.replaces: Bardic Knowledge; Rage Powers; Spell Kenning; Damage Reduction
archetypes.aonSummary: Some Shoanti skalds discover deeper truths in their tribes’ totems. These skalds, known as totem channelers, learn how to share the totems’ gifts with their allies in the heat of battle.

archetypes.name: Totemic Skald
archetypes.replaces: 3rd-level Rage Power; Uncanny Dodge; Improved Uncanny Dodge; Spell Kenning
archetypes.aonSummary: The totemic skald forms a close connection to an animal totem. Through the power of this mystical ally, the skald can change shapes, assuming its form as his own.

archetypes.name: Twilight Speaker
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Deity; Bardic Knowledge; Inspired Rage; Song of Strength; Dirge of Doom; Versatile Performance; Well-Versed; Lore Master; Master Skald
archetypes.aonSummary: (Elf Only) Twilight speakers are elven skalds of Findeladlara who consider it a sacred duty to seek out and befriend non-elven communities

archetypes.name: Undying Word
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; Lore Master; Inspired Rage; Song of Strength; Dirge of Doom; Spell Kenning
archetypes.aonSummary: Some who have survived the Mana Wastes cannot accept defeat, and those who have learned to speak the undying word can lend others the strength to endure

archetypes.name: Urban Skald
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Inspired Rage; Song of Marching; Damage Reduction; Dirge of Doom
archetypes.aonSummary: The urban skald finds that challenging and mocking foes is sometimes more effective than inspiring uncontrolled rage in a city.

archetypes.name: War Painter
archetypes.replaces: Raging Song; Spell Kenning; Lore Master
archetypes.aonSummary: The gripplis of the Valashmai Jungle exhibit savage strength for their size—attributed in part to the frightful magical pigments applied to their skin by the tribes’ mystical lore keepers.

archetypes.name: Warlord
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; Well-Versed; Spell Kenning; Lore Master; Improved Uncanny Dodge
archetypes.aonSummary: The warlord wields his force of personality like a weapon, intimidating his allies and ensuring that his followers heed his commands.

archetypes.name: Wyrm Singer
archetypes.replaces: Inspired Rage; Song of the Fallen; 12th-level rage power
archetypes.aonSummary: Wyrm singers spin fragments of the story of the ongoing struggle between noble Apsu and wicked Dahak.

archetypes.name: Ankou's Shadow
archetypes.replaces: Studied Target; Stalker; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: Ankou’s shadow practice the deadliest skills of the First World’s most feared enforcers: terrifying, winged fey assassins dispatched by the greatest lords of the First World to eliminate their rivals

archetypes.name: Avalancher
archetypes.replaces: Studied Target; Track; Swift Tracker; Stalker; Quarry; Improved Quarry; Master Slayer
archetypes.aonSummary: Avalanchers attack from overhead cliffs and mesas like a landslide of arrows and blades.

archetypes.name: Bloody Jake
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Studied Target; 4th, 6th, 8th, 12th, 16th-level Slayer Talents; Swift Tracker; Slayer's Advance
archetypes.aonSummary: Bloody jakes are cruel backwoods folk who prey upon their country cousins while terrorizing civilized people who venture into their rural range.

archetypes.name: Bounty Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; 2nd, 6th, and 10th-level Slayer Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Whether tasked with bringing in wanted criminals or paid to drag debtors back to their loan sharks, bounty hunters are valued for their ability to capture targets alive.

archetypes.name: Butterfly Blade
archetypes.replaces: Studied Target; Track; Sneak Attack; Stalker; Swift Tracker; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: Butterfly blades work in the shadows, eliminating threats with their namesake weapons and intimidating troublesome nobles.

archetypes.name: Cleaner
archetypes.replaces: Track; 4th-level Slayer Talent; Stalker
archetypes.aonSummary: A cleaner is responsible for destroying or removing incriminating evidence from a crime scene, disposing of corpses and eliminating witnesses to make a crime look like an accident or a mere disappearance.

archetypes.name: Covenbane
archetypes.replaces: Track; 2nd-level Slayer Talent; Stalker; Swift Tracker
archetypes.aonSummary: Covenbane slayers are scarred by arcane magic at a young age, and that resonance gives them supernatural insight into the psychic bonds between others.

archetypes.name: Cutthroat
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Track; 2nd and 6th-level Slayer Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Street-smart and extremely resourceful, cutthroats stalk city streets and alleyways, preying on those unfortunate enough to catch their eye.

archetypes.name: Deliverer
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; 2nd, 6th, and 10th-level Slayer Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Also known as a divine assassin, god’s blade, or wrath-bringer, a deliverer is a weapon chosen by a god to punish those who have committed an affront to that deity.

archetypes.name: Dune Rider
archetypes.replaces: Track; Swift Tracker; Studied Target; Stalker, 4th, 8th-level Slayer Talent; Master Slayer
archetypes.aonSummary: Mounted harriers, saboteurs, and skirmishers, dune riders can disrupt even the most organized opposition.

archetypes.name: Family Hunter
archetypes.replaces: 2nd, 6th-level Slayer Talent; Sneak Attack; Studied Target
archetypes.aonSummary: Most slayers focus their efforts on single targets, but family hunters try to root out every branch of a tainted tree of life.

archetypes.name: Grave Warden
archetypes.replaces: 2nd and 10th-level Slayer Talents; Stalker;
archetypes.aonSummary: While paladins and inquisitors use their connection with the divine to fight undead hordes and other horrors of the night, a grave warden relies on knowledge, skill with weapons, and tenacity to put an end to these night-born terrors.

archetypes.name: Guerrilla
archetypes.replaces: Track; Swift Tracker; 6th-level Slayer Talent; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: Slayers characterized by cunning and patience, guerrillas specialize in ambush and harassment of enemies.

archetypes.name: Pureblade
archetypes.replaces: Track; 2nd and 8th-level Slayer Talents; Stalker; Master Slayer
archetypes.aonSummary: In Numeria, Pureblades are skilled at slaying naturally arising aberrations and any creatures that have been mutated by exposure to the bizarre alien technology that pervades the land. Pureblades from Alkenstar and Nex lead forays into the magic-starved Mana Wastes to eliminate aberrations before the creatures can threaten their lands.

archetypes.name: Sczarni Executioner
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Studied Target; 4th-level Slayer Talent; Swift Tracker; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: These professional killers are trained and used almost exclusively by the various Sczarni crime families.

archetypes.name: Sniper
archetypes.replaces: Track
archetypes.aonSummary: Whether it’s with a bullet from a sling, a quarrel from a crossbow, or even an expertly thrown dagger, the sniper ensures that a single shot disables his targets.

archetypes.name: Spawn Slayer
archetypes.replaces: Studied Target; Stalker; Master Slayer
archetypes.aonSummary: Generations of Ninshaburian warriors fought the Spawn of Rovagug, holding the line against impossible odds. Some of their ancient techniques persist to this day.

archetypes.name: Spire Diver
archetypes.replaces: Studied Target; Stalker; Track; Swift Tracker; Slayer's Advance; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: Peerless divers, assassins, and scouts, spire divers operate in and out of water using the same weapons and equipment.

archetypes.name: Spiritslayer
archetypes.replaces: 2nd level Slayer Talent; Stalker
archetypes.aonSummary: Slayers that focus in culling ghosts, shadow demons, and other incorporeal creatures.

archetypes.name: Stygian Slayer
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiencies; 4th and 10th-level Slayer Talents; Stalker
archetypes.aonSummary: A stygian slayer crawls out of the darkest shadows to strike fear into the hearts of civilized folk.

archetypes.name: Toxic Sniper
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Track; Studied Target; Slayer Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Followers of the daemonic harbinger Cixyron hide throughout the Mana Wastes, scavenging for guns. With significant firepower in hand, the Furious Thunder’s snipers bring poisonous death to the wastes.

archetypes.name: Turncoat
archetypes.replaces: Track; Stalker; Quarry; Improved Quarry
archetypes.aonSummary: The turncoat’s natural talents for deception and treachery are fitting when negotiating with the untrustworthy individuals and his ability to adapt allows him to preempt opponents’ schemes.

archetypes.name: Vanguard
archetypes.replaces: Track; 2nd and 4th-level Slayer Talents; Stalker
archetypes.aonSummary: Vanguards are battlefield commanders who focus on the brutality of combat and lead their allies to bloody victory.

archetypes.name: Velvet Blade
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Armor Proficiency; Studied Target; Track; Swift Tracker
archetypes.aonSummary: Velvet blades specialize in infiltrating the upper echelons of society, mingling with nobles and courtiers, and killing them.

archetypes.name: Witch Killer
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Studied Target; 4th, 10th-level Slayer Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Born into cultures where magic users are hated and feared, witch killers devote their lives to purge the arcane taint from the world.

archetypes.name: Woodland Sniper
archetypes.replaces: Track; Sneak Attack; Stalker; Swift Tracker; Slayer's Advance
archetypes.aonSummary: Woodland snipers are guardians of forest and grove, keeping vigil on their borders and hunting bounties and trespassers from the shelter of sturdy branches.

archetypes.name: Crossblooded
archetypes.replaces: Spells Known
archetypes.aonSummary: A crossblooded bloodline combines the powers of two distinct heritages.

archetypes.name: Dragon Drinker
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline Arcana; Claws Bloodline Power; 7th, 13th, and 19th-level Bloodline Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: (Requires Draconic Bloodline) The blood of dragons not only flows through a dragon drinker’s veins, but also empowers her spells and magical abilities when consumed.

archetypes.name: Eldritch Scrapper
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 9th, and 15th-level Bloodline Powers
archetypes.aonSummary: An eldritch scrapper is usually spoiling for a fight, looking to prove that she’s just as tough as a martial character.

archetypes.name: Mongrel Mage
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline; Bloodline Powers; Bloodline Spells; 7th, 13th, and 19th-level Bloodline Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: A mongrel mage is a sorcerer whose bloodline is so weak, or mixed with so many others, that her power isn’t clearly associated with any bloodline source.

archetypes.name: Nine-Tailed Heir
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline Spell
archetypes.aonSummary: (Kitsune only) Tian stories often tell of kitsune with multiple tails who have a magical quirk in their blood or have been blessed by their race’s deific matron, Daikitsu

archetypes.name: Razmiran Priest
archetypes.replaces: Eschew Materials; 3rd-level Bloodline Spell; 5th-level Bloodline Spell; 9th-level Bloodline Power
archetypes.aonSummary: The Razmiran priest is a magical charlatan, missionary servant of the Living God.

archetypes.name: Seeker
archetypes.replaces: Eschew Materials, 3rd-level Bloodline Power, 15th-level Bloodline Power
archetypes.aonSummary: The seeker is obsessed with learning about their heritage and history, researching ancient texts and obscure ruins for clues.

archetypes.name: Sorcerer of Sleep
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline Arcana; Eschew Materials; 1st-level Bloodline Power
archetypes.aonSummary: Some sorcerers have trouble accessing their innate gifts and must find another way to unlock them. For a sorcerer of sleep, the mind-altering drug pesh is the key.

archetypes.name: Stone Warder
archetypes.replaces: Eschew Materials; 3rd-level Bloodline Spell; 7th-level Bloodline Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Stone warders have an innate ability to create runes that allow them to ward areas with magic traps built from their spells.
