These sorcerers are most common among dwarves, but have been known to appear among other races who have strong ties to earth, rock, stone, mountains, and the Darklands.

archetypes.name: Tattooed Sorcerer
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Bloodline Power; Eschew Materials; 7th-level Bloodline Feat; 9th-level Bloodline Power
archetypes.aonSummary: The tattooed sorcerer has embraced the ancient traditions of Varisian spellcasting, and uses colorful and intricate tattoos to enhance her magical powers.

archetypes.name: Umbral Scion
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline (Shadow Only); Spellcasting; Shadowstrike Bloodline Power; 7th and 13th-level Bloodline Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Umbral scions are sorcerers who are able to expertly control their especially potent shadow heritage. The majority of umbral sorcerers hail from the Darklands.

archetypes.name: Wildblooded
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline
archetypes.aonSummary: A wildblooded sorcerer has a mutated version of a more common bloodline, with one arcana and at least one bloodline power that are different from those of an unmutated bloodline.

archetypes.name: Wishcrafter
archetypes.replaces: Bloodline Arcana; Bloodline Bonus Spells; 7th, 13th, 19th-level Bloodline Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: (Ifrit Only) Wishcrafters are born with a talent for manipulating reality inherited from their efreeti ancestors.

archetypes.name: Drowned Channeler
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Phantom; Shared Consciousness; Etheric Tether; Bonded Manifestation; Bonded Senses; Detect Undead; Calm Spirit; See Invisibility; Call Spirit
archetypes.aonSummary: When a drowned spirit doomed to a watery grave descends toward the evil of undeath and seeks refuge in a mortal shell, the result is an unusual spiritualist with powers that resonate with the drowned spirit’s demise.

archetypes.name: Ectoplasmatist
archetypes.replaces: Etheric Tether; Phantom; Shared Consciousness; Fused Consciousness; Spiritual Bond; Empowered Consciousness; Bonded Manifestation; Phantom Recall; Dual Bond; Spiritual Interference; Greater Spiritual Interference
archetypes.aonSummary: Instead of calling upon a phantom from the Ethereal Plane, an ectoplasmatist infuses herself with the mysterious substance called ectoplasm.

archetypes.name: Exciter
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Emotional Focus; Phantom Recall; Etheric Tether; Bonded Senses; Spiritual Bond; Spiritual Interference; Fused Consciousness; Spiritual Interference;
archetypes.aonSummary: The phantom that accompanies the exciter fills him with unbridled exultation, as he lets feeling and passion rule and sharpen his mind and body into a glorious fusion.

archetypes.name: Fated Guide
archetypes.replaces: Antagonistic; Bonded Manifestation; See Invisibility; Call Spirit
archetypes.aonSummary: Not all phantoms are restless dead escaping the afterlife. On rare occasions, Pharasma returns a judged soul to the Material Plane—linking the spirit to a devout believer—to complete some final task, make amends for a crime, or grant a sharply divided soul a second chance.

archetypes.name: Fractured Mind
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Detect Undead; Calm Spirit; See Invisibility; Call Spirit
archetypes.aonSummary: Most spiritualists harbor the spirits of the deceased in their psyches, but a small number of them—known as fractured minds—draw their powers instead from a fraction of their own souls that resonates with extremely powerful emotions.

archetypes.name: Geist Channeler
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Emotional Focus; Bonded Manifestation
archetypes.aonSummary: Some phantoms retain less of their personalities and memories than others. Though most phantoms maintain some semblance of their former selves, others of their kind, known as geists, came close to being lost forever before they became phantoms.

archetypes.name: Grim Apostle
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Emotional Focus; Shared Consciousness; Fused Consciousness
archetypes.aonSummary: Some devotees of the Four Horsemen can form spiritual manifestations of the daemonic demigods.

archetypes.name: Hag-Haunted
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Shared Consciousness; Fused Consciousness; Spells; Spiritual Interference; Greater Spiritual Interference
archetypes.aonSummary: A hag who dies with a curse on her breath is often anchored to the Ethereal Plane by the power of her hatred— similar to vile and angry mortal souls—and some even claw their way back to the living world through the souls of those they despised or ruined... or those unfortunate souls they birthed. Hag-haunted spiritualists are tethered to these spiteful spirits, anchoring them once again in the world of the living.

archetypes.name: Haunted
archetypes.replaces: Bonded Manifestation; Dual Bond
archetypes.aonSummary: The haunted are a dangerous breed of spellcasters bound to temperamental and unpredictable phantoms that leech power from their spiritualists.

archetypes.name: Involutionist
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Phantom; Emotional Focus; Bonded Manifestation; Detect Undead, 11th, 15th, 17th-level uses of Calm Spirit
archetypes.aonSummary: Rather than bond with an existing spirit as most Rivethun eventually do, the involutionist creates a spirit from a piece of her own soul.

archetypes.name: Necrologist
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Share Consciousness; Share Spells; 5th, 13th-level slam damage increase; Devotion; Bonded Manifestation; Spiritual Interference; Greater Spiritual Interference
archetypes.aonSummary: The vile spiritualists known as necrologists reach toward the Negative Energy Plane and for whatever evil purpose, they bring back malevolent spirits whose passions have turned to vengeance and hate for all life.

archetypes.name: Onmyoji
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Shared Consciousness; Fused Consciousness; Spiritual Interference; Greater Spiritual Interference
archetypes.aonSummary: Though most spiritualists are chosen by their phantoms, others deliberately call phantoms to them through years of careful preparation and study in obscure divine traditions.

archetypes.name: Phantom Blade
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Phantom; Phantom Recall; Spiritual Bond; Dual Bond; Etheric Tether; Shared Consciousness; Fused Consciousness; Empowered Consciousness; Bonded Senses; Bonded Manifestation; Spiritual Interference; Greater Spiritual Interference
archetypes.aonSummary: A small selection of spiritualists are connected to spirits of combat and warfare, and manifest a weapon instead of a phantom.

archetypes.name: Plague Eater
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Shared Consciousness; Spiritual Interference; Detect Undead; Calm Spirit; See Invisibility; Fused Consciousness; Greater Spiritual Interference; Call Spirit
archetypes.aonSummary: A plague eater bears the weight of many souls within her consciousness, spirits that remember the devastation of disease and seek to protect their host from infections, cleanse others of plague, and use disease itself as a weapon.

archetypes.name: Priest of the Fallen
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Shared Consciousness; Bonded Manifestation; Phantom Recall; Fused Consciouness; Dual Bond; Empowered Consciousness
archetypes.aonSummary: A priest of the fallen is a spiritualist who channels her land’s legends and provides a vessel for mighty heroes to perform heroic acts once more.

archetypes.name: Quintessentialist
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Phantom
archetypes.aonSummary: The quintessentialist learns to project her best self—her exemplar—as an independent being, but in doing so leaves only the weakest and basest aspects behind in her body.

archetypes.name: Scourge
archetypes.replaces: Spiritual Interference; Devotion; Calm Spirit; Greater Spiritual Interference
archetypes.aonSummary: Scourges are students of pain and have a rare connection to tormented and wracked spirits.

archetypes.name: Seeker of Enlightenment
archetypes.replaces: Shared Consciousness; Detect Undead; Calm Spirit; See Invisibility; Fused Consciousness; Call Spirit
archetypes.aonSummary: Sometimes a spiritualist is so haunted by a past life’s failure to reach enlightenment that the past life is reborn not as a new creature but as a phantom in a spiritualist’s consciousness.

archetypes.name: Shadow Caller
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Emotional Focus; Shared Consciousness; Etheric Tether; Phantom Recall; See Invisibility; Fused Consciousness; Empowered Consciousness
archetypes.aonSummary: While most spiritualists form a bond with the remnants of a creature’s soul, some explore ways to bind ephemeral shadows to their own souls in exchange for power.

archetypes.name: Soul Warden
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Etheric Tether; Shared Consciousness; Spiritual Interference; Fused Consciousness; Greater Spiritual Interference; Bonded Senses; Phantom Recall; Bonded Manifestation; Dual Bond; Empowered Consciousness
archetypes.aonSummary: Soul wardens have helped their phantoms pass on and have become wardens of the soulstream, serving Pharasma and working with psychopomps to protect vulnerable souls from those who seek to capture, corrupt, or devour them.

archetypes.name: Totem Spiritualist
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Shared Consiousness; See Invisibility; Dual Bond
archetypes.aonSummary: These specialized spiritualists call upon phantoms that are manifestations of animals and personifications of nature.

archetypes.name: Usher of Lost Souls
archetypes.replaces: Bonded Senses; Spiritual Interference; Greater Spiritual Interference; See Invisibility; Spiritual Bond
archetypes.aonSummary: Ushers of lost souls are spiritualists who focus on bringing the souls of the dead to their final judgments at the end of the River of Souls.

archetypes.name: Ward Spiritualist
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Spellcasting; Bonded Senses; Phantom Recall; Greater Spiritual Interference
archetypes.aonSummary: A ward spiritualist ventures into the wilderness and petitions a kami to help her in her travels, either taking an existing ward with her or becoming the kami’s new ward.

archetypes.name: Zeitgeist Binder
archetypes.replaces: Phantom; Detect Undead; Calm Spirit; See Invisibility; Call Spirit; Bonded Senses; Fused Consciousness
archetypes.aonSummary: Zeitgeist binders channel the emotional connections of a group of people into a unique phantom that personifies a community.

archetypes.name: Blood God Disciple
archetypes.replaces: Summon Monster
archetypes.aonSummary: (Half-Orc) A half-orc summoner who devotes himself to one of the bloody orc gods may believe his eidolon is an avatar of that god rather than a mere supernatural creature.

archetypes.name: Blood Summoner
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Shield Ally; Transposition; Greater Shield Ally; Merge Forms
archetypes.aonSummary: A blood summoner conjures an eidolon born from violence and blood.

archetypes.name: Broodmaster
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Life Link; Life Bond; Merge Forms
archetypes.aonSummary: Most summoners bond with one eidolon for their entire lives, but the broodmaster forges a link with multiple smaller eidolons that make up his brood.

archetypes.name: Counter-Summoner
archetypes.replaces: Summon Monster; Bond Senses; Aspect; Greater Aspect
archetypes.aonSummary: While most summoners excel at conjuring monsters, there are those who focus instead on disrupting the conjurations of opponents.

archetypes.name: Evolutionist
archetypes.replaces: Maker’s Call; Transposition; Greater Shield Ally
archetypes.aonSummary: An evolutionist possesses greater power over his eidolon’s form, and is able to evolve his eidolon and its abilities to meet any challenge or face any threat as it comes up, seemingly on a whim.

archetypes.name: First Worlder
archetypes.replaces: Summon Monster I; Eidolon
archetypes.aonSummary: A first worlder summoner has a more primal connection to nature, their power being tied to the First World.

archetypes.name: God Caller
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Life Link; Transposition; Aspect; Greater Aspect; Twin Eidolon
archetypes.aonSummary: God callers follow a fractured tradition that originated in the now-lost nation of Sarkoris. They speak to an assortment of ancient divine powers to lead their communities and sometimes stir up reformations in faiths with ideals similar to their personal convictions.

archetypes.name: Leshy Caller
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Summon Monster
archetypes.aonSummary: A leshy caller summons creatures from the First World and forges a bond with a leshy eidolon.

archetypes.name: Master Summoner
archetypes.replaces: Summon Monster I; Shield Ally; Bond Senses
archetypes.aonSummary: The master summoner sacrifices the power of his eidolon in favor of summoning a plethora of otherworldly creatures to aid him.

archetypes.name: Morphic Savant
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Summon Monster; Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: A morphic savant is an agent of change who draws power from the Abyss, Elysium, or the Maelstrom to fulfill whatever goals strike his fancy.

archetypes.name: Naturalist
archetypes.replaces: Summon Monster; Shield Ally; Greater Shield Ally; Aspect Summoner; Life Bond; Greater Aspect
archetypes.aonSummary: A naturalist is a summoner who is in tune with the natural world, using his magic like a lens to focus various animal aspects onto his eidolon.

archetypes.name: Pyroclast
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Eidolon; Maker’s Call; Transposition
archetypes.aonSummary: Pyroclasts harness the primal elemental energy of magma. Their eidolons often resemble elemental beings.

archetypes.name: Shadow Caller
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Summon Monster; Eidolon
archetypes.aonSummary: (Fetchling Only) While most summoners can call any manner of creature from across the planes to serve them in combat, supplementing the skills of their eidolon with a diverse range of creatures, others eschew this broad utility and instead concentrate upon calling forth entities from the Shadow Plane.

archetypes.name: Shaitan Binder
archetypes.replaces: Share Spells; Shield Ally; Greater Shield Ally; Aspect; Greater Aspect; Twin Eidolon
archetypes.aonSummary: (Oread Only) Shaitan binders call upon a reflection of their genie ancestors to serve as their eidolons.

archetypes.name: Spirit Summoner
archetypes.replaces: Summon Monster; Eidolon; Aspect; Maker’s Call; Merge Forms; Transposition
archetypes.aonSummary: A spirit summoner is an arcane spellcaster whose eidolon is a manifestation of a shamanic spirit.

archetypes.name: Storm Caller
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Summon Monster; Shield Ally; Greater Shield Ally; Maker's Call; Transposition
archetypes.aonSummary: Many summoners beckon monsters from the Elemental Planes, but few are as specialized as storm callers, who channel the elemental energies of the Plane of Air.

archetypes.name: Story Summoner
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Bond Senses; Transposition
archetypes.aonSummary: Story summoners rely on the harrow to weave the paths they walk, turning their tales into reality. They channel magic through their harrow decks to influence the strange extraplanar beings they summon, bringing familiar and fateful characters to life.

archetypes.name: Synthesist
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Life Link; Shield Ally; Maker’s Call; Transposition; Greater Shield Ally; Merge Forms
archetypes.aonSummary: Rather than summon an eidolon to serve by his side, the synthesist fuses his eidolon’s essence to his own.

archetypes.name: Twinned Summoner
archetypes.replaces: Shield Ally; Greater Shield Ally; Maker's Call; Transposition; Merge Forms
archetypes.aonSummary: Reflecting the connected nature of Imbrex, a twinned summoner and his eidolon appear identical save for any obvious differences, such as evolutions or equipment.

archetypes.name: Unwavering Conduit
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Summon Monster; Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: Unwavering conduits work to keep everything ordered and regimented, drawing on power from the Eternal City of Axis, Heaven, or Hell to enforce whichever laws the summoner finds paramount.

archetypes.name: Wild Caller (ARG)
archetypes.replaces: Summon Monster; Eidolon
archetypes.aonSummary: (Half-Elf Only) The wild caller calls eidolons that take more natural and savage forms and summons from nature rather than the Great Beyond.

archetypes.name: Wild Caller (HotW)
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Summon Monster; Aspect; Greater Aspect
archetypes.aonSummary: A wild caller summons creatures from the First World and forges a bond with an eidolon with a plant body.

archetypes.name: Construct Caller
archetypes.replaces: Subtype; Summon Monster
archetypes.aonSummary: Construct callers use their mechanical and planar understandings to work planar energies as a tinkerer works parts

archetypes.name: Devil Binder
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Summon Monster I; Bond Senses; Shield Ally; Maker's Call; Transposition; Greater Shield Ally; Merge Forms; Twin Eidolon; Devotion
archetypes.aonSummary: A devil binder borrows extraplanar quintessence from her eidolon, gaining strange abilities for herself and evolving her eidolon’s magical powers.

archetypes.name: Devil Impostor
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bond Senses; Eidolon; Summon Monster; Shield Ally; Greater Shield Ally; Transposition
archetypes.aonSummary: Some summoners can’t abide the cruelty of devils, or simply can’t outwit them, but must appear to do so to get by in Cheliax, the Outer Planes, or similar areas of infernal influence. Rather than risk binding true devils, they reshape their eidolons into deceptive forms.

archetypes.name: Fey Caller
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Summon Monster; Eidolon Subtype
archetypes.aonSummary: Fey callers are summoners whose voices reach out into those strange faerie realms and call forth the fey who dwell there.

archetypes.name: God Caller
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Life Link; Transposition; Aspect; Greater Aspect; Twin Eidolon
archetypes.aonSummary: God callers follow a fractured tradition that originated in the now-lost nation of Sarkoris. They speak to an assortment of ancient divine powers to lead their communities and sometimes stir up reformations in faiths with ideals similar to their personal convictions.

archetypes.name: Leshy Caller
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Summon Monster
archetypes.aonSummary: A leshy caller summons creatures from the First World and forges a bond with a leshy eidolon.

archetypes.name: Soulbound Summoner
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Life Link; Summon Monster
archetypes.aonSummary: Soulbound summoners, as a rule, never set out to bind their soul to a dangerous and enigmatic power. Rather, they have found themselves unintentional masters of eidolons through incredible circumstances.

archetypes.name: Storm Caller
archetypes.replaces: Eidolon; Summon Monster; Shield Ally; Greater Shield Ally; Maker's Call; Transposition
archetypes.aonSummary: Many summoners beckon monsters from the Elemental Planes, but few are as specialized as storm callers, who channel the elemental energies of the Plane of Air.

archetypes.name: Twinned Summoner
archetypes.replaces: Shield Ally; Greater Shield Ally; Maker's Call; Transposition; Merge Forms
archetypes.aonSummary: Reflecting the connected nature of Imbrex, a twinned summoner and his eidolon appear identical save for any obvious differences, such as evolutions or equipment.

archetypes.name: Arrow Champion
archetypes.replaces: Panache; Opportune Parry and Riposte; Precise Strike; Swashbuckler's Initiative; Swashbuckler Weapon Training; Swashbuckler Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Arrow champions combine a swashbuckler’s agile style of combat with mastery over the bow

archetypes.name: Azatariel
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Menacing Swordplay; Precise Strike; Targeted Strike; Bleeding Wound; Charmed Life; Nimble; Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Azatariels are the champions of Elysium, dedicated to spreading its unpredictable whimsy and capricious goodness across the planes.

archetypes.name: Courser
archetypes.replaces: Opportune Parry and Riposte; Nimble; Menacing Swordplay; Superior Feint; Bleeding Wound
archetypes.aonSummary: Coursers move with grace and ease, racing across rooftops, dashing up walls, and clearing vast gaps between buildings.

archetypes.name: Daring Infiltrator
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Bonus Feat; Swashbuckler Initiative; Menacing Swordplay; Bleeding Wound
archetypes.aonSummary: Not known for their flashy entrances or for standing out in a crowd, a daring infiltrator uses stealth, disguise, and ruthless guile to pursue her goals.

archetypes.name: Dashing Thief
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Derring-Do; Swashbuckler's Edge; Panache; Bonus Feats; Menacing Swordplay; Dizzying Defense
archetypes.aonSummary: The dashing thief relies on swift swordplay, dazzling charm, and spirited courage to commit audacious acts of thievery.

archetypes.name: Flying Blade
archetypes.replaces: Panache; Dodging Panache; Kip-Up; Menacing Swordplay; Targeted Strike; Bleeding Wound; Perfect Thrust; Swashbuckler Weapon Training; Swashbuckler Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: While most swashbucklers prefer their battles up close, others prefer dealing death from a distance.

archetypes.name: Guiding Blade
archetypes.replaces: Bonus Feats; 1st, 7th, 15th-level Deeds; Charmed Life; Nimble; Kip-up
archetypes.aonSummary: Instead of parrying attacks against her, a guiding blade redirects her enemies’ ire away from her allies, interfering with enemies who attack her allies, whether that attack comes by blade or by spell.

archetypes.name: Inspired Blade
archetypes.replaces: Panache; Swashbuckler Finesse; Bleeding Wound; Swashbuckler Weapon Training; Swashbuckler Weapon Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: An inspired blade is both a force of personality and a sage of swordplay dedicated to the perfection of combat with the rapier.

archetypes.name: Mouser
archetypes.replaces: Opportune Parry and Riposte; Menacing Swordplay; Targeted Strike; Bleeding Wound
archetypes.aonSummary: In the hands of a trained warrior, a well-sharpened blade is deadly regardless of size. A mouser moves in close, using her size and skill as an advantage.

archetypes.name: Musketeer
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiencies; Swashbuckler Finesse; Dodging Panache
archetypes.aonSummary: A number of organizations and kingdoms search for warriors who are brave (or foolish) enough to wield firearms on the battlefield.

archetypes.name: Mysterious Avenger
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Class Skills; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Swashbuckler Finesse; Nimble; 4th-level Bonus Feat; Swashbuckler Weapon Training
archetypes.aonSummary: While some swashbucklers fight for queen and country, and others for coin, glory, or just the enhancement of their own reputations, the mysterious avenger fights directly for a cause.

archetypes.name: Noble Fencer
archetypes.replaces: Dodging Panache; Superior Feint; Subtle Blade; Charmed Life
archetypes.aonSummary: Noble fencers use their quick wits and panache in both physical and social confrontations, and they rely on their training and discipline to emerge victorious, rather than merely trusting to luck.

archetypes.name: Okayo Corsair
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Swashbuckler Finesse; Panache; Menacing Swordplay; Superior Feint; Bleeding Wound; Dizzying Defense; Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: An Okayo corsair practices a unique acrobatic martial art that draws inspiration from both the mysticism of monastic combat traditions and the flair of a swashbuckler.

archetypes.name: Picaroon
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiencies; Panache; Opportune Parry and Riposte; Kip-Up; Superior Feint; Bleeding Wound; Swashbuckler Finesse
archetypes.aonSummary: While some swashbucklers take pride in their ability to wear down an opponent with great skill at arms and clever positioning, there are those who use firearms to get in close and hit hard.

archetypes.name: Rondelero Swashbuckler
archetypes.replaces: Derring-Do; Kip-Up; Bleeding Wound; Perfect Thrust; Charmed Life
archetypes.aonSummary: Rondelero swashbucklers are Taldan specialists in an aggressive, lightly armored fighting style that utilizes the falcata and buckler.

archetypes.name: Rostland Bravo
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Armor Proficiency; Menacing Swordplay; Superior Feint; Bleeding Wound; Swashbuckler's Edge
archetypes.aonSummary: While some duelists favor more technical approaches, others study flashier maneuvers, wielding the curved blade with artful flair. Disdainfully called “bravos” by classically trained rivals, students of this approach have claimed the label with pride.

archetypes.name: Shackles Corsair
archetypes.replaces: Nimble; Swashbuckler Initiative; Targeted Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: A Shackles corsair’s debonair charm and style make her a paradoxical celebrity even among the nations whose ships she plunders.

archetypes.name: Veiled Blade
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Opportune Parry and Riposte; Menacing Swordplay; Swashbuckler's Grace; Swashbuckler's Edge
archetypes.aonSummary: Veiled blades specialize in subtlety, not through clandestine sneaking but simply by appearing to be someone harmless and unarmed.

archetypes.name: Whirling Dervish
archetypes.replaces: Swashbuckler Finesse; Panache; Superior Feint; Targeted Strike; Bleeding Wound; Deadly Stab
archetypes.aonSummary: In Qadira and throughout the Padishah Empire, Sarenrae’s worshipers praise the Dawnflower through dance. Her more warlike followers adapted these dances into graceful martial forms, and their swashbuckling style is feared throughout the Inner Sea region and beyond for its ability to devastate foes with a scimitar through motion and agility regardless of strength of arms.

archetypes.name: Wildstrider
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Dodging Panache; Derring-Do; Swashbuckler's Edge; Kip-Up; Subtle Blade
archetypes.aonSummary: Most swashbucklers call cities their home, but some prefer deserts, marshlands, mountains, or woods, where the rough terrain grants them an advantage, and have little interest in the comforts of an urban lifestyle.

archetypes.name: Agathiel
archetypes.replaces: Dual Identity; Vigilante Specialization; 1st-level Social Talent; 6th-level Vigilante Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Agathiels surrender a portion of their immortal souls to Nirvana in exchange for a measure of animalistic might to aid them in their righteous crusades.

archetypes.name: Anaphexia Thought-Killer
archetypes.replaces: 2nd, 6th-level Social Talent; 7th, 15th-level Vigilante Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Anaphexia thought-killers cut out their own tongues to gain magical protection from exposure and hunt down secrets to steal before they can be spread

archetypes.name: Avenging Beast
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Skill Ranks; Dual Identity; 4th, 7th, 10th ,14th, 16th-level Vigilante Talents; Vigilante Specialization; Startling Appearance; Frightening Appearance; Stunning Appearance
archetypes.aonSummary: Some vigilantes turn to natural traditions and supernatural forces to transform into beasts, unleashing a primal fury on their foes before returning to an ordinary guise.

archetypes.name: Bellflower Harvester
archetypes.replaces: Dual Identity; Vigilante Specialization; 1st-level Social Talent; 2nd-level Vigilante Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Bellflower harvesters are the front-line operatives of the secretive Bellflower Network

archetypes.name: Brute
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Base Saving Throws; Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Vigilante Specialization; Vengeance Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: Some vigilantes can transform into brutish versions of themselves, becoming larger, more terrifying in appearance, and far more formidable in combat—though at a price.

archetypes.name: Cabalist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Skill Ranks; Weapon and Armor Proficiency; 4th, 8th, 10th, 14th, 16th-level Vigilante Talent; Vigilante Specialization; Startling Appearance; Frightening Appearance; Stunning Appearance
archetypes.aonSummary: Practice with blood sacrifices, necromancy, and shadow magic gives a cabalist a reputation as a sinister and dangerous vigilante.

archetypes.name: Chu Ye Enforcer
archetypes.replaces: Dual Identity; 1st-level Social Talent; 4th, 6th, 12th, 14th, 18th-level Vigilante Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Donning terrifying masks, these vigilantes forsake their humanity to become more like the evil oni they mimic.

archetypes.name: Darklantern
archetypes.replaces: Creature Type; Dual Identity; 1st-level Social Talent; 4th-level Vigilante Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Select members of the Lantern Bearers undergo a horrific ritual allowing them to temporarily experience the dark transformation into a drow, but at the cost of their sanity.

archetypes.name: Dragonscale Loyalist
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Social Talent; Unshakable; Startling Appearance; Frightening Appearance; Stunning Appearance
archetypes.aonSummary: Dragonscale loyalists serve the throne of Brevoy. When not acting as courtiers, these agents don fearsome draconic masks, becoming anonymous protectors of the king-regent’s rule.

archetypes.name: Experimenter
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Vigilante Specialization; 1st-level Social Talent; Unshakable; Startling Appearance; Frightening Appearance; Stunning Appearance
archetypes.aonSummary: Some vigilantes adopt lives of secrecy to hide their strange experiments from public view.

archetypes.name: Faceless Enforcer
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Dual Identity; 2nd, 6th-level Vigilante Talent; 5th, 11th, 17th-level Social Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Unyielding warriors, faceless enforcers lock their identities behind implacable helms.

archetypes.name: Ferocious Hunter
archetypes.replaces: Dual Identity; 2nd, 8th-level Vigilante Talent; Unshakable
archetypes.aonSummary: Some half-orcs have such distant orc ancestry that they have the ability to move through the world without experiencing the same discrimination many of their kin, yet many of these half-orcs still take great pride in their heritage and have a powerful desire to show the world that half-orcs are deserving of respect

archetypes.name: Gunmaster
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Vigilante Specialization; Unshakable
archetypes.aonSummary: Gunmasters brandish firearms like extensions of their will, taking down their foes with deadly accuracy and skill.

archetypes.name: Half-Elf Double Scion
archetypes.replaces: Dual Identity
archetypes.aonSummary: The deception of hiding their true heritage can take a toll on some half-elves, and some form alternate identities to let the suppressed side of their heritage be known.

archetypes.name: Hangman
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Vigilante Specialization; 2nd, 4th-level Vigilante Talent; Unshakable; Startling Appearance; Frightening Appearance; Stunning Appearance
archetypes.aonSummary: Wherever the guilty walk free, the hangman brings judgment.

archetypes.name: Hidden Current
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Social Talent; 2nd-level Vigilante Talent; Frightening Appearance
archetypes.aonSummary: The hidden current operates above and below the sea.

archetypes.name: Imperial Agent
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 5th-level Social Talent; Unshakable
archetypes.aonSummary: Imperial agents are often the descendants of nobility and generals from Lung Wa, devoted to reuniting the empire by conquering Lung Wa’s successor states

archetypes.name: Magical Child
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Skill Ranks; Weapon and Armor Proficiency; 4th, 8th, 14th, 16th-level Vigilante Talents; Vigilante Specialization
archetypes.aonSummary: Some vigilantes, no matter their age, carry a spark of capricious whimsy under which flows a powerful current of magic and wonder.

archetypes.name: Masked Maiden
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Dual Identity; Seamless Guise; 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, 19th-level Social Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Masked maidens find themselves leading a double life: ordinary (albeit troubled) citizen by day, faceless warrior by night. In the most tragic cases, the identities entirely disassociate, with the maiden experiencing unexplained exhaustion and injuries upon awakening.

archetypes.name: Mounted Fury
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Vigilante Specialization; 6th, 12th-level Vigilante Talent; Vengeance Strike
archetypes.aonSummary: Some vigilantes form special bonds with the creatures they use as steeds, considering these loyal and trusted mounts just as much heroes or antiheroes as they might be.

archetypes.name: Mutated Defender
archetypes.replaces: Vigilante Specialization; Vigilante Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Occasionally a mutation takes hold of the body of a vigilante, but he learns to hide his maladies, usually through alchemical concoctions or magical concealment

archetypes.name: Psychometrist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 1st-level Social Talent; 2nd, 6th, 12th, 18th-level Vigilante Talent; Unshakable
archetypes.aonSummary: Psychometrists aren’t spellcasters; instead, they collect strange items or create their own uncanny gadgets that seem to only work for them.

archetypes.name: Serial Killer
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Vigilante Specialization; Unshakable; 4th, 6th, 12th, 14th-level Vigilante Talent; 7th, 9th, 19th-level Social Talent; Startling Appearance; Frighting Appearance; Stunning Appearance
archetypes.aonSummary: Some vigilantes adopt an innocent guise to cloak their acts of brutal murder.

archetypes.name: Splintersoul
archetypes.replaces: Dual Identity; Unshakable; 3rd, 7th-level Social Talents; Startling Appearance; Frightening Appearance; Stunning Appearance
archetypes.aonSummary: A splintersoul pushes the boundaries of what it means to have two separate identities.

archetypes.name: Teisatsu
archetypes.replaces: Weapon and Armor Proficiency; Vigilante Specialization; 2nd-level Vigilante Talents; Vigilante Talents
archetypes.aonSummary: Teisatsu are specialized vigilantes who focus on infiltrating social scenes and high-society gatherings on behalf of the feuding lords of Minkai.

archetypes.name: Warlock
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Skill Ranks; Armor Proficiency; 4th, 8th, 10th, 14th, 16th-level Vigilante Talent; Vigilante Specialization; Unshakable
archetypes.aonSummary: Practicing magic in secret, the warlock obscures her arcane scholarship from public view.

archetypes.name: Wildsoul
archetypes.replaces: Vigilante Specialization; 2nd, 6th, 12th, 18th-level Vigilante Talent
archetypes.aonSummary: Within some vigilantes are incredible innate abilities that, although normally the domain of natural beasts, inexplicably aid them in fighting their enemies.

archetypes.name: Zealot
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Skill Ranks; Weapon Proficieny; 4th, 8th, 10th, 14th, 16th-level Vigilante Talent; Alignment; Vigilante Specialization;
archetypes.aonSummary: Dedicated to a single deity, the zealot hunts the enemies of his faith in secret, often because his religion is outlawed or persecuted in the region.

archetypes.name: Calamity Caller
archetypes.replaces: Blessings; Focus Weapon; Sacred Weapon; Bonus Feats; Aspect of War
archetypes.aonSummary: (Elf Only) While all elves feel a deep connection to nature, some elven priests take this bond further, using their link to call down the wrath of nature upon their enemies

archetypes.name: Champion of the Faith
archetypes.replaces: Sacred Weapon; 3rd-level Bonus Feat; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Champions of the faith are crusaders who use the power of their divine patron to annihilate the faith’s enemies.

archetypes.name: Cult Leader
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Skill Ranks; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Focus Weapon; 3rd, 9th, 12th, and 15th-level Bonus Feats; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Referred to as fanatics, lunatics, or obsessives, cultists see themselves as genuine devotees of their deity.

archetypes.name: Disenchanter
archetypes.replaces: Bonus Feats; Channel Energy; 6th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: While many warpriests focus on threats to the body, the disenchanter focuses on dangers to the mind and the soul.

archetypes.name: Divine Champion
archetypes.replaces: 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th, 18th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Divine champions are unswervingly devoted to their causes, and specialize in bringing battle to the enemies of their faiths.

archetypes.name: Divine Commander
archetypes.replaces: Blessings; 3rd, 6th, 12th, and 15th-level Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Some warpriests are called to lead great armies and face legions of foes. These divine commanders live for war and fight for glory.

archetypes.name: Feral Champion
archetypes.replaces: Blessings; Sacred Weapon; Sacred Armor
archetypes.aonSummary: When a warpriest devotes himself to a god of the natural world, he is sometimes blessed with supernatural powers that allow him to evoke animalistic power and fury.

archetypes.name: Fist of the Godclaw
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Deities; Blessings; 3rd, 6th, 12th-level Bonus Feat; Aspect of War
archetypes.aonSummary: Devoted to the divine control of law above all else, these zealots seek to establish absolute order.

archetypes.name: Forgepriest
archetypes.replaces: Blessings; Spells; Bonus Feats; 3rd and 6th-level Bonus Feats; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Armorers of exquisite skill, forgepriests take inspiration from their deity to produce the most perfect weapons and armor they can, the better to equip the armies of the faithful.

archetypes.name: Jistkan Magistrate
archetypes.replaces: Class Skilss; Blessings; Spontaneous Casting; Bonus Languages; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Some warpriests study the ancient magic that the Jistkan magistrates used to bind elementals and make pacts with genies.

archetypes.name: Liberty's Blade
archetypes.replaces: Blessings; Sacred Weapon; Channel Energy; Sacred Armor
archetypes.aonSummary: There are some who find in the call to freedom something primal and spiritual, even more so than other Andorens.

archetypes.name: Mantis Zealot
archetypes.replaces: Deity; Alignment; Weapon and Armor Proficiencies; Sacred Weapon; Sacred Armor; Aspect of War
archetypes.aonSummary: Among the Red Mantis worshipers of Achaekek, some hold such strong faith in their assassin god that they gain divine power.

archetypes.name: Molthuni Arsenal Chaplain
archetypes.replaces: Blessing; Sacred Armor; Sacred Weapon; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: Molthuni arsenal chaplains are warpriests trained in the Arsenal District in Korholm. They bolster their nation’s military by focusing on the militant aspects of their gods.

archetypes.name: Proclaimer
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Deity; Spellcasting; Fervor; Sacred Armor; Channel Energy
archetypes.aonSummary: A proclaimer rushes into Abyss-twisted wastes with nothing but his weapon in his hand and his faith in his heart, shouting his deity’s name to the skies

archetypes.name: Proselytizer
archetypes.replaces: Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Sacred Armor; 3rd-level Bonus Feat; Sacred Weapon; Blessings; Blessings (Major)
archetypes.aonSummary: The proselytizer is the perfect militant missionary. He seeks to win the hearts and lay claim to the souls of those he meets, and—failing that—spreads the word of his deity at the edge of the sword.

archetypes.name: Sacred Fist
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Weapon/Armor Proficiencies; Sacred Weapon; Focus Weapon; 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th, and 18th-level Bonus Feats; Sacred Armor
archetypes.aonSummary: Unlike many warpriests, sacred fists leave behind armor and shield and instead rely on their fists and whatever protection their deity bestows on them.

archetypes.name: Shieldbearer
archetypes.replaces: Focus Weapon; Sacred Weapon; Sacred Armor;
archetypes.aonSummary: Shieldbearers are divine warriors who stand on the front lines of battle, shoulder to shoulder with the soldiers of their people.

archetypes.name: Sixth Wing Bulwark
archetypes.replaces: Armor Proficiencies; Focus Weapon; Sacred Weapon; Sacred Armor; 6-th, 12th-, 18th-level Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: The Sixth Wing bulwark are followers of Ragathiel that train to hold the line and defend against the incursion of evil forces, fortifying herself and her allies to stand strong in the face of any opposition, no matter how dire.

archetypes.name: Alley Witch
archetypes.replaces: Familiar; 1st and 6th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Some witches find their spark of magic in the long, dark shadows and forgotten places within the city.

archetypes.name: Ashiftah
archetypes.replaces: Familiar; 2nd, 6th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Known in Taldane as a “battle witch,” an ashiftah drifts like a phantom among the enemy armies, calling down disaster upon their heads and weakening their resolve.

archetypes.name: Beast-Bonded
archetypes.replaces: 4th-level Hex; 8th-level Hex; 10th-level Major Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: While all witches are intimately tied to their familiars, a beast-bonded witch’s craft focuses specifically on her familiar bond and developing the relationship with her patron through her familiar.

archetypes.name: Bonded Witch
archetypes.replaces: Familiar
archetypes.aonSummary: (Half-Elf Only) While all witches commune with the unknown, the blend of human ingenuity and adept learning mixed with elven blood gives some half-elves a unique conduit to channel the powers of the arcane.

archetypes.name: Bouda
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Familiar; 1st-level Hex; 10-level Major Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: These strange and often solitary witches have a strong connection to curses, the evil eye, and hyenas.

archetypes.name: Cartomancer
archetypes.replaces: Familiar; 2nd-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: A witch who serves the spirits of the harrow in exchange for mystical power is known as a cartomancer.

archetypes.name: Coral Witch
archetypes.replaces: Patron; Familiar; 8th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Coral witches use their magic to fashion familiars from living coral and emulate the unyielding tenacity of these durable marine organisms.

archetypes.name: Demon-Sworn
archetypes.replaces: Patron Spells; 6th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: In the depths of the Darklands, as well as similarly inhospitable locales on Golarion, many seek the succor of demons as a means of survival.

archetypes.name: Dimensional Occultist
archetypes.replaces: 2nd-level Hex, 8th-level Hex, 12th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: The dimensional occultist sacrifices some of her mastery over hexes in return for much increased planar lore.

archetypes.name: Dreamweaver
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Patron Spells; 2nd, 6th, 10th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: (Changeling Only) A changeling dreamweaver draws upon her hag heritage to ply the dream realms in order to touch mortal minds and souls, for good or ill.

archetypes.name: Flood Walker
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Class Skills; 4th, 10th, 16th, 18th-level Patron Spells; 1st, 6th, 10th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Witches who dwell in floodplains or along the banks of predictably dangerous rivers can tap into the underlying potential of surging waters in order to enhance their eerie powers.

archetypes.name: Gingerbread Witch
archetypes.replaces: Familiar; 1st, 4th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: A sweet tooth lures the gingerbread witch’s victims to doom.

archetypes.name: Gravewalker
archetypes.replaces: Patron Spells; Familiar; 1st-level Hex; 4th-level Hex; 8th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Having much in common with necromancers, the gravewalker is obsessed with the occult manipulations of the dead, particularly mindless undead such as zombies.

archetypes.name: Hag of Gyronna
archetypes.replaces: Patron; Spells; 2nd, 8th, 12th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Only female witches dare dedicate themselves to the Angry Hag, and those who do so are feared for their ability to bend minds and sow discord.

archetypes.name: Hagbound
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 2nd, 4th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th, and 20th--level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Whether a changeling in the process of succumbing to her mother’s call, a witch cursed by a hag to become her instrument of torment, a vain and petty witch overeager for power, or some other unfortunate soul, a hagbound witch finds its soul has been infected by a hag’s spite and powerful, corrupt arcane magic.

archetypes.name: Havocker
archetypes.replaces: Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Although most witches are guided to subtle curses and debilitating hexes by their mysterious patrons, some are instead taught the secrets of harnessing raw, destructive elemental power.

archetypes.name: Hedge Witch
archetypes.replaces: 4th-level Hex; 8th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Among witches, there are those who devote themselves to the care of others and restrict their practices to the healing arts.

archetypes.name: Herb Witch
archetypes.replaces: Patron; 1st, 2nd, 10th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Herb witches brew foul-tasting medicines, sweet poisons, and other concoctions from the untamed plants of the wild.

archetypes.name: Hex Channeler
archetypes.replaces: 2nd-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: A hex channeler is a witch who devotes herself to either life—healing the wounded and destroying the undead—or death, slaying the living and aiding undead.

archetypes.name: Invoker
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 8th, 10th, and 16th level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: The invoker uses her familiar to summon facets of her mysterious patron directly into her body, enhancing her skills and granting her powerful abilities.

archetypes.name: Jinx Witch
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 2nd, 6th, 10th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Jinx witches specialize in calling down subtle misfortunes and deceiving enemies and allies alike. While they lack any ability to truly eliminate bad luck, they are uniquely gifted at making others believe otherwise.

archetypes.name: Ley Line Guardian
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Familiar; 1st and 8th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Some witches tap into the power of their patrons not through a special connection with a familiar, but rather directly through the vast network of ley lines that crosses the planes.

archetypes.name: Medium
archetypes.replaces: Patron; 2nd, 6th, 20th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Mediums tap into the spiritual power of those who have yet to find their final rest. Their ability to interact with these souls allows mediums to learn about the physical world through the experiences of those who came before them.

archetypes.name: Mirror Witch
archetypes.replaces: Familiar
archetypes.aonSummary: Mirror witches eschew animal familiars and isntead talk to their patrons via mirror magic

archetypes.name: Mountain Witch
archetypes.replaces: Spells; Hex; 2nd-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Mountains can be sanctuaries for witches hunted by society. Here they form bonds with the spirits of the lofty reaches.

archetypes.name: Nexian Spellspy
archetypes.replaces: Deliver Touch Spells; 4th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Nexian spellspies are witches who use their familiars and divining talents to spy on their rivals and protect themselves from similar intrusions.

archetypes.name: Pact Witch
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Patron; Familar; 6th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Though all witches forge bonds with mysterious powers known as patrons, a pact witch takes this bond to an extreme by forging an inexorable pact with the Outer Planes.

archetypes.name: Putrefactor
archetypes.replaces: Familiar; Patron; 1st, 2nd, 4th, 6th, 10th, and 16th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Some witches find their patrons while in the throes of despair and grief, when all they desire is to see the veneer of civilization peel back to reveal the filth and rot that underlies all things.

archetypes.name: Rhetorician
archetypes.replaces: 1st-level Hex; Spells
archetypes.aonSummary: Rhetoricians feel driven to engage in debate, learn as much as they can about their potential foes, and seek ways to use information and quick talking to handle problems before resorting to raw violence.

archetypes.name: Scarred Witch Doctor
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Hexes; Familiar; 1st-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: (Orc Only) The scarred witch doctor draws power from her ability to endure pain and suffering.

archetypes.name: Sea Witch
archetypes.replaces: Patron Spells; 1st-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: A sea witch’s affinities are tied to the vast oceans and the rolling waves.

archetypes.name: Season Witch
archetypes.replaces: Patron; 1st-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Season witches gain their power from the cyclical and mystical exchange of energy passed from one season of nature to another.

archetypes.name: Seducer
archetypes.replaces: Patron; Key Ability Score; 1st, 6th, 8th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: These charismatic witches, often devotees of the Green Mother, rely on their otherworldly charms to achieve their aims.

archetypes.name: Synergist
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 8th, and 14th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Synergists gain the ability to combine their forms with their familiars’ in order to create something more powerful than either alone.

archetypes.name: Tatterdemalion
archetypes.replaces: Weapon Proficiencies; Cantrips; 1st, 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: Some witches can bend the warp and weft of fabric and thread.

archetypes.name: Vellemancer
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; 2nd, 6th, and 8th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: While the popular stereotype envisions witches as wicked spellcasters sowing misery, many people turn to the arcane to heal others and better the world. The vellemancer is a guide, using her witchcraft to empower and teach others.

archetypes.name: Veneficus Witch
archetypes.replaces: 2nd and 10th-level Hexes
archetypes.aonSummary: Veneficus witches specialize in poisons—brewing both magical and traditional concoctions, and applying them to weapons, traps or even her potent hexes.

archetypes.name: Venom Siphoner
archetypes.replaces: 1st, 2nd, 6th-level Hex; Alertness
archetypes.aonSummary: Witches are no strangers to poisons, using them alongside their various brews, curses, spells, and other tools of the trade.

archetypes.name: White-Haired Witch
archetypes.replaces: Hex; Major Hex; Grand Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: A white-haired witch concentrates her mysterious powers on improving her prowess in melee, using feats of agility and her prehensile hair to deal extreme damage.

archetypes.name: Winter Witch
archetypes.replaces: Familiar; Patron; 4th-level Hex
archetypes.aonSummary: The descendents of Baba Yaga rule the frozen realm of Irrisen, and possess a unique power stemming from their otherworldly origin and their ties to cold magic.

archetypes.name: Witch-Watcher
archetypes.replaces: Spells per Day
archetypes.aonSummary: For reasons known only to them, witch-watchers offer protection to nobles across Golarion.

archetypes.name: Wyrm Witch
archetypes.replaces: Patron; Familiar
archetypes.aonSummary: Some witch covens have learned to use treasure to access other draconic powers.

archetypes.name: Absalom: Arcanamirium Crafter
archetypes.replaces: Hand of the Apprentice
archetypes.aonSummary: One trained by the Arcanamirium, a college specializing in the universalist school of magic and the art of crafting magical items.

archetypes.name: Arcane Bomber
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Cantrips; Arcane School
archetypes.aonSummary: To many wizards, the experimentation of the alchemist seems quaint, if not dangerous or frightening. A few wizards take up the secrets of the bomb, however, fusing alchemy with their already considerable magical power.

archetypes.name: Arcane Physician
archetypes.replaces: Arcane School; Scribe Scroll
archetypes.aonSummary: Arcane physicians use their scholarly knowledge and arcane mastery to achieve incredible feats of medicine.

archetypes.name: Arcane Warden
archetypes.replaces: Arcane School; Class Skills; Scribe Scroll; Bonus Feats; Hand of the Apprentice; Metamagic Mastery
archetypes.aonSummary: Arcane wardens are wizards who specialize in the discovery or generation of places of safety and refuge.

archetypes.name: Bonded Wizard
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; 5th, 10th, and 15th-level Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Many wizards form an arcane bond with an item, but for some this bond becomes a powerful mystic union.

archetypes.name: Cheliax: Egorian Academy Infernal Binder
archetypes.replaces: Acid Dart, Dimensional Steps
archetypes.aonSummary: A wizard trained by the prestigious Egorian Academy, best known for its Infernal Binding program in the school of conjuration.

archetypes.name: Chronomancer
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; 10th, 15th, 20th-level Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Rare arcane scholars known as chronomancers demonstrate the ability to shift themselves in short bursts between the past, future, and alternate presents.

archetypes.name: Clocksmith
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Arcane School; Scribe Scroll; Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Clocksmiths are oddities among wizard communities, pursuing the study and creation of clockwork constructs to near obsession

archetypes.name: Cruoromancer
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: (Dhampir Only) A cruoromancer infuses his necromantic magic with the power of his unique mixture of living blood and undead ichor.

archetypes.name: Elder Mythos Scholar
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; 1st, 8th-level Arcane School Ability; Spellbook; Scribe Scroll; 5th, 10th-level Bonus feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Elder Mythos scholars risk their sanity to seek knowledge of alien and awful entities from beyond the stars.

archetypes.name: Exploiter Wizard
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Arcane School
archetypes.aonSummary: Contrary to traditional wizardly study, an exploiter wizard forgoes the tried and true methods of arcane focus and arcane schools for the exploits favored by an arcanist.

archetypes.name: Familiar Adept
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; 5th and 10th-level Bonus Feats; Arcane Bond; Spellbooks
archetypes.aonSummary: Many wizards employ familiars to assist them, but only a few have unlocked the true power of their school of magic through the familiar itself.

archetypes.name: First World Caller
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Arcane School; Scribe Scroll; 10th, 15th-level Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Some wizards, typically First World gnomes, have mystical ties with the First World, the primordial home of the fey

archetypes.name: Hallowed Necromancer
archetypes.replaces: Arcane School; Spells; Power Over Undead; Grave Touch; Scribe Scroll; 5th, 10th, 15th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Many wizards study necromancy to create undead, but some study the same arts to purge the stain of undeath.

archetypes.name: Instructor
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th-level Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Whether serving as staff at a formal school of magic or simply acting as a wandering teacher, an instructor has an apprentice who trades service to the instructor for lessons in magic.

archetypes.name: Pact Wizard (FF)
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Arcane School
archetypes.aonSummary: Some wizards make bargains with beings from other realms in order to gain arcane power. These pact wizards have unparalleled access to extraplanar allies, but these bonds never come without strings attached.

archetypes.name: Pact Wizard (HHH)
archetypes.replaces: Spellcasting; Scribe Scroll; 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th level Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Wizards who seek mastery of arcane power without tedious study and monotonous research.

archetypes.name: Poleiheira Adherent
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Arcane School
archetypes.aonSummary: Poleiheira adherents are wizards who wish to emulate the explorations and discoveries of Arustun and partake in great odysseys as they seek to imitate his achievements.

archetypes.name: Primalist
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond, 5th-level Bonus Feat, 10th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: A primalist is a wizard who has spent a considerable amount of time studying the chaos that is primal magic.

archetypes.name: Qadira: Mage of the Veil
archetypes.replaces: Blinding Ray, Invisibility Field
archetypes.aonSummary: Rather than controlling the elements or transforming the environment, mages of the veil focus on much more subtle magic.

archetypes.name: Runesage
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Arcane School
archetypes.aonSummary: Runesages draw upon the mystic energies of ancient Thassilon.

archetypes.name: Scroll Scholar
archetypes.replaces: Diviner's Fortune (diviner) or Hand of the Apprentice (universalist), 5th-level Bonus Feat, 4th-level spell slot
archetypes.aonSummary: Those who trade some of their potential to better understand ancient texts and scrolls can become learned scroll scholars.

archetypes.name: Scrollmaster
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; 10th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: To some wizards, a scroll is not just a written form of a spell, it is a physical weapon meant to be used in combat like a sword or a shield.

archetypes.name: Shadowcaster
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; 5th-level Bonus Feat; 10th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Trained in the dark mysteries of Nidal's Umbral Court, the shadowcaster harnesses the power of shadows to bolster their spellcasting.

archetypes.name: Siege Mage
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; Arcane Bond; Cantrips; Arcane School
archetypes.aonSummary: The siege mage combines his arcane mastery with a supernatural link to siege engines.

archetypes.name: Spell Sage
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Arcane School
archetypes.aonSummary: A spell sage has mastered spells of all types, and is able to increase the effectiveness of his own spells and eventually even cast spells from other classes’ spell lists.

archetypes.name: Spellbinder
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond
archetypes.aonSummary: (Elf Only) A spellbinder is an elven wizard who forges an arcane bond between himself and one or more wizard spells.

archetypes.name: Spellslinger
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Scribe Scroll; Cantrips; Arcane School
archetypes.aonSummary: While few contest the seductive allure of commanding arcane and occult powers, there are those wizards who become obsessed with the natural mysteries of black powder.

archetypes.name: Spirit Binder
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Arcane School; Scribe Scroll; Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: While most wizards learn their arts through gradual study, spirit binders have made a sudden arcane breakthrough due to the traumatic experience of losing a loved one.

archetypes.name: Spirit Whisperer
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Spellbooks; Arcane School; Bonus Feats; 20th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Spirit whisperers are a breed apart among wizards, and are often mistaken for witches.

archetypes.name: Sword Binder
archetypes.replaces: Arcane Bond; Arcane School; Bonus School Spell Slots; 10th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Sword binders follow a tradition of martial wizards who often worked with the Church of Aroden and the crowns of Taldor and then Cheliax.

archetypes.name: Thassilonian Specialist
archetypes.replaces: Lose access to two schools of magic
archetypes.aonSummary: Specialist in a Thassilonian school of magic, this specialist sacrifices his connection with two schools in order to greatly strengthen his chosen specialty.

archetypes.name: Undead Master
archetypes.replaces: Alignment; Arcane School; Arcane Bond; Scribe Scroll; 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th-level Bonus Feats
archetypes.aonSummary: Undead masters have great power over undeath.

archetypes.name: Wind Listener
archetypes.replaces: Class Skills; Arcane School; Arcane Bond; 5th, 10th, 15th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: (Sylph Only) The wind listener takes a sylph’s natural curiosity to the extreme, enhancing his natural skill at subterfuge and eavesdropping with potent arcane magic.

archetypes.name: Worldseeker
archetypes.replaces: Scribe Scroll; 6th/8th-level School Ability; Arcane Bond; 5th, 15th-level Bonus Feat
archetypes.aonSummary: Worldseekers are wizards who travel to all corners of the Great Beyond.
